News.title: Pregnant mum asked for cigarette & opened window before falling 90ft to death – but unborn baby miraculously survived
News.content:
FAMILY TRAGEDY Pregnant mum asked for cigarette & opened window before falling 90ft to death – but unborn baby miraculously survived

A PREGNANT mum who died after falling from a tower block had asked her dad for a cigarette moments before, an inquest heard today.

Emma Atkinson, 38, plunged 90ft from the ninth floor of Shakespeare Towers in Leeds while she was visiting her dad.



Her baby, who has been named Posie, was delivered in hospital five weeks premature but miraculously survived.

Tragically Emma couldn’t be saved and was declared dead at the scene following the horror at Shakespeare Towers in 2024.





An inquest heard she had asked her dad David Atkinson for a cigarette when she visited him that morning.

The mum-of-five sat in a chair by the window and opened the pane so far that it was horizontal, he said.

The dad said he asked her to close the window because it was cold then heard her say “I’m off”.

How to get help EVERY 90 minutes in the UK a life is lost to suicide. It doesn’t discriminate, touching the lives of people in every corner of society – from the homeless and unemployed to builders and doctors, reality stars and footballers It’s the biggest killer of people under the age of 35, more deadly than cancer and car crashes. And men are three times more likely to take their own life than women. Yet it’s rarely spoken of, a taboo that threatens to continue its deadly rampage unless we all stop and take notice, now. If you, or anyone you know, needs help dealing with mental health problems, the following organisations provide support: CALM, www.thecalmzone.net, 0800 585 858 Heads Together,www.headstogether.org.uk HUMEN www.wearehumen.org Mind, www.mind.org.uk, 0300 123 3393 Papyrus, www.papyrus-uk.org, 0800 068 41 41 Samaritans,www.samaritans.org, 116 123

He turned to see her “feet going out of the window”. David told Wakefield Coroner’s Court: “I thought I was having a nightmare.”



Devastated, he rushed to the ground floor and an off-duty doctor living in the tower block provided vital first aid to Emma and her unborn baby.

She was rushed to hospital but suffered “catastrophic and unsurvivable injuries”.

But doctors at Leeds General Infirmary were able to save her baby.

The inquest heard Emma was diagnosed with emotional unstable personality disorder and had tried to take her own life twice previously.

Emma had tragically shared a picture showing off her baby bump in a final Facebook post before she died.



It showed her posing in a mirror and showing off her baby bump while a child hugs her legs.

She confirmed in the comments that she was due in 10 weeks at the time.

Emma wrote: “It’s a girl, couldn’t be happier.”



Devastated friends also released balloons from outside the tower block the next day.

Emma’s daughter Demi left a message to her “perfect” mum.

It read: “Rest in paradise mama. You were one of a kind. I miss you more than anything already, too perfect for this world.”

News.title: Brit dad-of-two, 35, dies suddenly on fishing trip with son, 8, in France as heartbroken family pay tribute
News.content:
FAMILY'S AGONY Brit dad-of-two, 35, dies suddenly on fishing trip with son, 8, in France as heartbroken family pay tribute

A BRIT dad has tragically died on a fishing trip with his eight-year-old son in France.

Keiren Bell, 35, suffered a ruptured abdominal aneurysm while on a last-minute getaway with his son, also called Keiren.



Despite the efforts of medical staff, he could not be saved and died on August 2.

Now, heartbroken relatives have launched a fundraiser to help cover the cost of repatriating him to the UK after revealing he had no travel insurance.



In an emotional appeal, family member Beth Lynch said: “Our family is devastated to be writing this.

“Our beloved Keiren, aged just 35, travelled to France on a last-minute fishing trip with his 8-year-old son, Keiren, spending precious time together doing something they both loved.

“Tragically, while they were there, Keiren suffered a ruptured abdominal aneurysm.

“Despite the best efforts of the medical team, he sadly passed away.”

She described Keiren, from Leeds, West Yorks, as a devoted family man whose sudden death has left loved ones shattered.

Beth said: “Keiren was a devoted dad to his two beautiful children, 13-year-old Kaitlyn and eight-year-old Keiren, a beloved son to Janine, a caring brother to Konnor, a devoted partner to Lisa, and a loyal friend to so many.



“He was the kind of person who would do anything for the people he loved, and his sudden passing has left an unimaginable hole in the lives of everyone who knew him.

“He leaves behind his beloved son, Keiren, his beautiful daughter, Kaitlyn, his loving mum, Janine, his brother, Konnor, his heartbroken partner, Lisa, and countless family members and friends who are struggling to come to terms with this devastating loss.”

The family is currently in France, arranging to bring Keiren back to Britain.



Beth said: “His family are currently in France, trying to navigate the unimaginable heartbreak of losing Keiren while also facing the overwhelming practical and emotional challenges that come with such a tragic loss so far from home.

“Their only wish is to bring him back to the UK, where he belongs, so he can be surrounded by those who love him and laid to rest with the dignity he deserves.”

She explained that the unexpected financial burden has forced the family to ask for help.

“As Keiren had no travel insurance, his family are now faced with the unexpected costs of bringing him home to the UK,” Beth said.

“Every donation will go directly towards the cost of repatriating Keiren to the UK, allowing his family to focus on one another and saying goodbye to him, rather than the overwhelming financial pressures they now face.”



Beth said that if donations exceed the cost of bringing Keiren home, the remaining money will go towards supporting his children.

“On behalf of Keiren’s children, his mum, his brother, his partner, and our entire family, thank you for your kindness, generosity and support during this incredibly difficult time,” she said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Every donation and every share brings us one step closer to bringing Keiren home, where he belongs.”

So far, £26,350 had been raised of a £30,000 GoFundMe target.

News.title: New rule change that blocks Brits from buying digital train tickets officially rolls out – don’t get caught out
News.content:
PASSENGERS have been warned they may be blocked from buying digital railway tickets under a new rule.

The country’s biggest rail operator has introduced the major change in an effort to stop fare evasion.

Greater Thameslink Railway (GTR) has launched a three-month ticketing trial where digital train tickets will no longer be sold from major railway hubs.



The operator, which controls Thameslink, Southern, Great Northern and Gatwick Express services, introduced the programme last week in an attempt to prevent passengers from using methods of fraud known as “short faring” and “quick scanning”.



With the “short- faring” method, travellers may purchase tickets for the last section of their journey, saving them the full ticket cost.

While “quick scanning” refers to passengers quickly purchasing a digital ticket if an inspector arrives, or if the barriers at their destination are closed.

Under the change, customers will now be required to collect their ticket from a ticket office or machine at the station, rather than receiving a standard QR code.



GTR also chose not to disclose which stations the new rule would affect, in order to prevent fare evasion later down the line.

Stephen MacCallaugh, head of revenue protection at GTR, told The Times: “It is only fair that everyone travelling on our railway pays the right fare, and as the UK’s largest train operator in public ownership, reducing fare evasion and the taxpayer’s subsidy on the railway is crucial to our success.

“This trial is one of several initiatives we’re exploring to reduce fare evasion while making sure genuine customers can still buy tickets easily and conveniently.”

This comes as another operator, South Western Railways, introduced similar measures in order to crack down on the scams, with some customers forced to repay thousands of pounds after being caught.



In June, the operator blocked the purchase of digital tickets between Vauxhall and Waterloo, after data revealed up to 95 per cent of them were being used unlawfully.

Costing the industry up to £400million a year, the government also announced a host of measures over the last few months to tackle evasion.

News.title: Grooming gang members who sexually abused girls may be freed under early release scheme in ‘another betrayal to victims’
News.content:
BACK ON STREETS Grooming gang members who sexually abused girls may be freed under early release scheme in ‘another betrayal to victims’

GROOMING gang members who sexually abused teen girls could be freed under Labour’s early release scheme in another “betrayal to victims.”

A number of men who were members of Asian gangs that abused children in Bradford may be turned loose in the coming years.



Because they committed their offences before anti-grooming laws were introduced in 2003 the men were charged and jailed for indecent assault.

It means they do not fall within the exemptions of early release announced by the Prime Minister, The Times reports.



Five men who were jailed last October for a collective 35 years after they abused a girl from the age of 13 are among those eligible for release.

Mohammed Imran Akram, Safraz Ahmed Latif, Wajid Hussain, Mohammed Naheem and Nadeem Ali were all found guilty on various counts of indecent assault.



They were each sentenced to between six and eight years in 2025, meaning some of them could be freed in 2028 because they are not classed as serious sexual offenders.

After the trial the victim said the men had taken away “my basic rights and stole my future.”



New Prime Minister Andy Burnham is facing growing backlash after only excluding rapists and the most serious sex offenders from early release.

The scheme was paused when it was revealed the killers of hero PC Andrew Harper would be among those freed.

But following a review, soft-justice plans to free Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole halfway through their 13-year jail terms were not changed.

This means the two thugs could be let out on the streets in a matter of months.

Furious widow Lissie Harper, 35, said: “This is disgusting. I’m beyond appalled and bristling with anger to hear Andrew’s killers are soon to be free.



“The level of disrespect the Government are showing to Andrew and other victims, and their loved ones such as me, is beyond contempt.”

A Police Federation chief has now revealed they are poised to take legal action unless Mr Burnham reverses the decision.

Thames Valley chair Aileen O’Connor called the ruling “an insult to Andrew’s family, friends and colleagues” and said “Andy Burnham may be on his holidays but we won’t rest on this.”



After pausing the scheme last month, Andy Burnham promised no prisoners would be freed until an urgent review was carried out.

Ministers examined the early release policy and went ahead with it, but prevented serious sexual abusers and rapists from being turned loose.

The decision has sparked fury as it was revealed serious criminals – including grooming gang members – would still be let out after only serving half of their sentence with a loophole leaving them eligible.

Kemi Badenoch wrote to the PM to highlight the issue that allows members of grooming gangs to be set free.

She branded it “yet another betrayal of victims.”



The Tory leader said: “On Tuesday, you told the country that those convicted of grooming offences would be excluded.

“Your own government has now put in writing that some of these men will be released early anyway.”

The Ministry of Justice said: “We have been clear that we wanted to go further and block more offenders from getting out sooner into their sentence, but could not do so without risking prisons reaching capacity and collapsing.

“If that happened, police could not make arrests, courts could not remand offenders and there would be unchecked criminality.”

It comes after it was revealed that some 9,000 domestic abusers are set to be let out of prison under Labour’s early release scheme.



According to the Conservatives 3,000 domestic abuse perpetrators a year could be turned loose to roam the streets.

However, Shadow Justice Secretary Nick Timothy branded the move “disgraceful.”

Andy Burnham’s own backbenches turned on him over the move, with Stoke-on-Trent MP Allison Gardner saying the prospect of abusers being let loose is “frightening” for victims.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In response to the Conservative claim of 9,000 domestic abusers being up for release, an MoJ spokesperson said: “This is a speculative figure.

“It wrongly assumes prison population and sentencing patterns will remain unchanged throughout Parliament, while also counting people who have not yet committed offences.”

News.title: Top heart surgeon who was ‘twisted sexual predator hiding in plain sight’ with ‘god complex’ is struck off
News.content:
MONSTER MEDIC Top heart surgeon who was ‘twisted sexual predator hiding in plain sight’ with ‘god complex’ is struck off

A “HIGHLY-SKILLED” heart surgeon who revealed himself to be a “twisted” sexual predator has been struck off the register.

Dr Amal Bose molested five junior hospital employees at Lancashire Cardiothoracic Centre in Blackpool between 2017 and 2022.



Bose preyed on five female colleagues over the five-year period, hiding his despicable behaviour “in plain sight”.

The predatory surgeon regularly commented on women’s appearances, referring to one as “fresh meat” and others as “shaggable” on a WhatsApp group.



He also touched women’s breasts, groin and waists while passing it off as accidental.

One of his victims began self-harming to deal with the trauma – which he played down as “banter” – while another reported suffering from anxiety following the abuse.

The “predatory” surgeon was described as the root cause of the department’s “toxic and sexualised culture”.

The assaults had “severe impacts” on the women, with some having to take time off work and another even leaving the role entirely.



Bose was convicted of 12 counts of sexual assault at Preston Crown Court on June 19 last year.

He was sentenced at the same court to six years in prison and placed on the sex offenders’ register on September 16.

Now Bose has been struck off the medical register following a hearing at the Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service (MPTS) on July 31.

Following the sentencing, Judge Ian Unsworth KC described his vile acts as “sexually charged, targeted and predatory”.

He said: “On the evidence before me I am satisfied so that I am sure that you used your exalted position to facilitate your sexual offending.



“To the outside you were a highly skilled and sometimes popular cardiac surgeon.

“The reality is that you were a sexual predator hiding in plain sight.”

The case was taken to a Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service hearing, where Bose was let go due to his convictions being “fundamentally incompatible” with registration.

He had been previously called a man of good character, with the tribunal noting that he was a “good cardiac surgeon”.

The tribunal concluded: “The tribunal determined that the conviction fell towards the higher end of the spectrum of seriousness.



“The tribunal also took into account that the doctor was working in a difficult and pressurised environment at times where colleagues have said that workplace banter was required stress relief.”

It added that the environment should not have impacted how he “physically treated and spoke about colleagues”.

It said: “The tribunal noted that Dr Bose had found it difficult to explain why he acted as he did save for describing his behaviour as ‘banter’.

It concluded that Bose posed an ongoing risk to the public.

After the criminal proceedings concluded, Sacha Coyne, Senior Crown Prosecutor for CPS North West’s Rape and Serious Sexual Offence Unit, said: “Amal Bose was in a trusted position at the hospital.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“He appeared not to recognise the serious and lasting impact his actions would have, describing his behaviour at trial as ‘workplace banter’.

“This case should send a clear message to perpetrators of sexual abuse, the Crown Prosecution Service will not hesitate to prosecute abusers, regardless of the position that the abuser holds in society.”

News.title: Putin ‘is prepared to take down a passenger jet in Europe’ after ‘Russian’ bomb drone sparks chaos at German airport
News.content:
AN EXPLOSIVE-laden drone found at a German airport shows Vladimir Putin is prepared to take down a European passenger jet, an expert has warned.

Panic broke out at Leipzig Airport on Wednesday after a rigged drone was discovered near a fleet of Ukrainian cargo planes.



Moments later, chaos escalated when a second unidentified object collided with an incoming aircraft.

Security expert Will Geddes said the terrifying breaches had “shaken fear across not only militaries and across the world, but also commercial airports”.



And he warned the chilling ordeal proved that Putin is more than capable of using a drone to blow up a passenger plane in Europe.

Geddes told The Sun: “It’s a disaster waiting to happen.”



He added that the device could have been adapted to carry radioactive material or even a biological weapon.

Geddes said: “The visible demonstration of the ability to get close to a cargo plane in an airport in Leipzig shows that if that had detonated… that would have had a drastic impact.”



He also warned the West was lacking in the necessary countermeasures to defend against drones – a weakpoint which could leave Britain vulnerable.

“These are almost impossible to stop in many regards, they’re also incredibly difficult to shoot out the sky by infantry,” he warned.

“And then you put that into an environment like the United Kingdom, Manchester, London, Birmingham, Glasgow, anywhere with a major transport hub, then an FPV drone could cause huge impact.”



He also highlighted how the immense range that UAVs have poses another major threat to Nato.

Geddes said: “The versatility of launching an FPV drone is that you could launch it from your car, you could launch it from your home, you could launch it from virtually anywhere.

“That ‘safe space’ of airspace outside an airport will extend quite far, depending on the aircraft and its ability to reach high elevation beyond the reach of a drone as quickly as it possibly can.”



Following the ordeal, shocking images of the drone were released as Nato investigators joined local authorities to launch a probe.

Speculating on who was responsible, Kyiv’s ambassador to Germany Oleksii Makeiev said: “Who else could it be but Russia?“

German airports have been on high alert after a string of unauthorised drone overflights in recent months.

Several unidentified flying objects have been seen worryingly near to military facilities, energy terminals, seaports and logistics companies.

Putin sending drone swarms to Britain a 'mathematical certainty' IT’S a “mathematical certainty” that Vladimir Putin will spark chaos in Britain with drone swarms, an ex-Navy commander has warned. Russia has brazenly infringed Nato airspace and sought to wreak havoc in Europe over recent months. Former Royal Navy Commander Tom Sharpe told The Sun it’s only a matter of time before the Kremlin tries to send drone swarms to Britain. Read more here…

Police say these overflights might be connected to Russian agents.



Geddes also said Russia and the West are now “almost in an arms race of countermeasures” as they scramble to find ways to defend against UAVs.

The expert said: “We’ve seen the evolution of the technology and capability these drones advance so quickly, especially in Ukraine.”

Geddes added that the bomb drone has also sparked fear among potential suppliers who Russia might target.



He said: “It’s not necessarily the end target, but it’s part of that supply chain, which if it’s interrupted, targeted, attacked, creates a concern.

“Other people within that supply chain, who feel that even though they’re not directly contributing to the war effort by Russia in Ukraine, that they are part of that machinery and they could just as easily be targeted.”

The drone on Wednesday was found near a fleet of planes owned by Antonov – a major Ukrainian aerospace firm.

Antonov planes have used Leipzig/Halle as an operating base since Russia‘s full-scale invasion in 2022.

After the drone was found, the southern runway of the airport, a major hub for DHL and Ukrainian jets, remained closed while bomb experts examined the device.



X-ray imaging showed the drone was attached to a defective detonator.

The explosive may have been one that can be made easily from fertiliser and petrol, according to Bild.

Several planes, including a passenger flight, were diverted overnight.

Amid the chaos while air traffic was being redirected, one cargo plane had to abort its landing.

It then reportedly hit an unknown object before landing in Hanover, where minor damage to the nose section was discovered.



European security agencies have been probing a series of incendiary devices concealed in parcels that caught fire in 2024.

These incidents raised concerns that malicious actors may be planning to sabotage air cargo operators.

Putin was even suspected of planting a parcel bomb on a flight headed to a depot in the UK.

Some of the devices were found at a DHL warehouse in Leipzig and in freight shipments in transit across Europe.

The Leipzig package started burning as it was being loaded onto a plane after it had come from Lithuania.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The head of the German domestic intelligence agency said if it had exploded on the plane it could have brought it down.

News.title: Moment criminals deliberately smash into innocent drivers in multi-million pound world of ‘crash for cash’ scams
News.content:
THIS is the moment a group of criminals deliberately smash into innocent drivers as part of a multi-million pound “crash for cash” scam.

Shocking dashcam footage showed a crook pulling out quickly and slamming into another motorist side-on in a dangerous manouevre while on a busy road.



The spike in incidents comes as organised criminals have been deliberately crashing into innocent motorists on British roads, authorities have warned.

The fraud involves gang members intentionally staging or inducing vehicle collisions to trigger fraudulent insurance payouts for financial gain.



Other footage captured showed cars deliberately braking in front of a motorists in a bid to try and cause an accident with no time to react.

Many occasions resulted in near misses, narrowly avoiding what could have easily been dangerous collisions at speed.

And another video in the montage showed a brazen criminal turning head first into incoming traffic, causing the driver to swerve wildly.

The Insurance Fraud Enforcement Department (IFED) and dashcam manufacturer Nextbase are urging drivers to remain vigilant against the growing threat.



Detectives warn the scams have evolved beyond basic staged bumps into aggressive roadside operations.

Modern tactics – such as the ones captured on video – combine dangerous driving, on-the-spot identity theft, and collusion with corrupt repair networks.

Another video even showed two crooks elaborately staging a crash scene with one driver crashing into a bike while the other pretended to be injured before calling 999.

Over the past five years, IFED has investigated more than £25.3 million in suspected “crash for cash” cases with roughly 75 per cent of these involved deliberately staged or induced crashes.



Criminals are also now increasingly targeted methods to pressure shaken victims into immediate cash settlements or inflated insurance claims.

Moped riders are increasingly targeting lone motorists, striking from blind spots or while drivers are momentarily distracted.

The rider will throw their vehicle to the ground, feign injury, and film the scene to intimidate the victim into paying up on the spot.

Identity theft has also become a core component of the fraud.



Criminals are routinely demanding to photograph driving licences at the roadside, using the personal data to commit further crimes.

Corrupt garages then systematically inflate repair bills to maximise the fraudulent insurance payout.

Drivers are being advised to install dashcams to capture clear, timestamped evidence of any incident in order to combat the scam.

Cops warned motorists to never hand over bank details, pay cash at the roadside, or allow their driving licence to be photographed.

All collisions should be reported directly to insurers as quickly as possible.



Detective Chief Inspector Nik Jethwa, Head of IFED, said: “Crash for cash fraud is a growing problem and criminals are becoming more aggressive in how they carry out these schemes.

“We want the public to be more aware than ever of the tactics being used, which put innocent road users at risk.

“Please take extra care at difficult junctions and roundabouts and follow our safety advice if you suspect something is wrong.

“There is also a real risk of identity theft, so consider the potential consequences if you are involved in a collision.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“IFED will continue to pursue those who exploit vulnerable people.



“We are working with Nextbase to amplify this message and to highlight one of the simplest ways to protect yourself: consider getting a dashcam”
