To view this content you can use the button below to allow Captivate cookies for this session only. Enable Cookies Allow Cookies Once

"My main goal was always to get to the Olympics in London. Trabzon just wasn't to be, as you know. It felt like we won the fight and we just didn't get the decision," Ward told Sky Sports.

He regrouped and made the 2016 Olympics his target. He reached the Rio Games, only to crash out at the first stage as the referee gave him two baffling points deductions, tipping the three-round amateur bout in his opponent's favour.

"It was one of these things that was out of my control," Ward reflected. "I picked up two public warnings, where I was still winning on the scorecards but because of the warnings I was beaten on a 3-2 split decision. Definitely at that time I was very disheartened.

"I was kind of saying to myself: 'Am I ever going to get that little bit of luck?' But again after a few weeks you just regroup and go back to the gym."

Image: Ward was a superstar of Irish amateur boxing

He won three European golds in all and a cluster of World Championship medals.

"It's not an accident to be consistently winning," he said. "You have to have something a little bit special about you. I believe so."

But an Olympic medal could have taken put him on a completely different trajectory. That was something he was denied.

"I kind of always focus on the future," he reflected. "Sometimes you can overthink about what's gone. It's not going to change anything.

"I've always loved boxing and loved being around it and it's something that gave me huge opportunities in my life, to travel the world and meet so many great people. For me I just don't think there's anything else.

"It's something that I love doing."

Eventually, in 2019, he turned professional. He had his first pro fight at Madison Square Garden in New York, it was all set up for him. Then painful disaster struck.

In the second round his knee dislocated and collapsed beneath him. His debut could scarcely have been gone worse.

"You kind of question it sometimes," Ward said. "It could have happened somewhere else but I believe everything happens for a reason. It was out of my control. It was one of these freak accidents that happen. Obviously it was devastating when it happened, I was very upset.

"Mentally you don't want to leave the game, you always want to be involved. Sometimes injuries can stop that from happening, I was hoping that that my knee wasn't going to stop me continuing chasing my goals and my career. It was good that everything worked out well with the operation and they said there were no more issues."

The business of boxing can be unforgiving. Opportunities dried up, but Ward stayed patient, fought on and now on Saturday, live on Sky Sports, he takes on hard-punching, undefeated light-heavyweight contender Artjom Kasparian in Dublin.

Image: Ward fights Artjom Kasparian on Saturday live on Sky Sports

"There's no point getting in there to take easy fights," he said. "It's an opportunity to step up and fight decent fighters and move on and challenge myself to see how far I can really take it. I really believe in myself, I can go all the way.

"That's the key, just getting the opportunity, getting the right fights at the right time. It felt like that never happened over the last couple of years."

He believes all that misfortune, the bad luck that has shrouded his talent, will now help him.

"Things will change, you will get a bit of luck along the way," Ward said. "That makes you a stronger person. I feel like that will give you the extra edge then when something happens in a fight or a moment where you just need something different. That will always flash back - look, I've been through it all and now I can fight through this.

"The most important thing as a fighter is to still believe in yourself, still stay focused, still keep in the gym, keep learning. Doors will open for you, opportunities will come.

"I've had a lot of ups and downs in my career but looking back I'm grateful for opportunities and grateful for what I've achieved. I just stuck at it and here I am still going strong, still believe in myself, believe I'm probably the best I've ever been physically, mentally. So I'm excited."

Sports.title: Rockets march on after easy win while Buttler makes history in The Hundred
Sports.content:
Trent Rockets extended their lead at the top of The Hundred table with a near-perfect performance that secured their fifth win in six games, leaving Birmingham Phoenix rooted to the bottom.

Sam Billings' unbeaten 31 sealed a scrappy chase after Phoenix stuttered to 111-6 despite Joe Clarke's 50, while Jos Buttler made history for the Manchester Super Giants as he became the leading Twenty20 run-scorer of all time.

After the Rockets elected to field, Will Smeed broke an unwanted record by being the first batter in The Hundred history to be unbeaten without scoring at the end of the powerplay. 25 runs came from that powerplay for the loss of Mitch Owen to Mohammad Amir, who had to leave the field with a strained hamstring immediately after taking the wicket.

Smeed eventually fell for six off 16 balls, with the visitors appearing tentative against a disciplined attack led by outstanding performances from spinners Calvin Harrison and Mitch Santner, along with Lewis Gregory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A crowd member made a great catch during Trent Rockets match against Birmingham Phoenix

Only Joe Clarke, Phoenix's leading run-scorer this season, managed to break free, reaching a half-century from 37 balls before finishing with 62 off 47. He became the fourth victim of Craig Overton's safe hands, with the catches setting a competition record. Of the remaining batters, only Laurie Evans reached double figures as Phoenix limped to an underwhelming 111-6 from their 100 balls.

After Amir's departure, skipper Billings had juggled his bowlers expertly as he searches for a fourth successive title in The Hundred. And when the Rockets batted, there was little pressure on the openers, Ben Duckett and Finn Allen progressing smoothly to 29-0 in the powerplay.

Mystery spinner Usman Tariq removed Duckett for 22 and delivered his customary bow celebration, conceding just six runs from his first 10 balls. However, there were simply not enough runs on the board, with 113 becoming the lowest total ever successfully defended in The Hundred men's competition.

Nye Donald came and went after a typically pugnacious six-ball 17, before Allen and Billings calmly rotated the strike at around a run a ball. Two successive sixes from Billings off Saqib Mahmood, including an outrageous slog sweep, accelerated the finish, and the result was all but confirmed when Allen holed out to Tariq at short mid-on for 28 with only six runs required.

The Rockets completed the victory with another Billings six, winning with 17 balls to spare to be sitting pretty with two games to come, their route direct to the final having got that bit easier.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Overton makes FOUR great catches for Trent Rockets

Gregory said: "We were superb with the ball. We kept chipping away with important wickets. It was a little bit two-paced, with a bit of variable bounce at times. The bowling unit spoke about smashing the top of the stump as hard as we could.

"The guys up front with the bat have been outstanding. We're in a really good position, playing some fantastic cricket, and hopefully we can continue that."

Buttler become the leading Twenty20 run-scorer of all time

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jos Buttler hits a mega half century to win it for Manchester Super Giants vs Welsh Fire

After three straight defeats, Manchester Super Giants got the win they needed over Welsh Fire at an overcast Emirates Old Trafford to remain in contention for qualification.

Half-centuries from Tim Seifert and Jos Buttler propelling them to a crunching win with 31 balls to spare.

Seifert said: "We just tried to get off to a good start and maintain the run rate and it was good that we both got going. And it was quite nice to watch Buttler from the other end! We've got two big games ahead and this is a good little boost for us."

The Super Giants move up to 12 points, now just four behind the Fire with two games left each.

They had to do it without their captain Aiden Markram, who has returned to South Africa for personal reasons, Jos Buttler taking over captaincy duties and Paul Walter replacing him at the top of the order, meaning there were just three overseas players in the line-up.

Second-placed Fire won the toss and chose to bat, reaching an uncomfortable 4-0 from the first ten balls after Josh Tongue didn't concede a single run off his first five balls.

Spin was introduced at that stage, with Liam Dawson seeing Matt Short dropped almost immediately. The openers took full advantage, progressing steadily at first before opening up to reach 76 at the halfway stage. Their century partnership - the first in Fire men's history - came up after 70 balls.

Short was particularly severe on Noor Ahmad, who conceded 34 runs from 15 balls, while Sonny Baker was even more expensive. Walter went for 37 but the home side were 104-1 off 50, an extraordinary three no balls in six balls from Ferguson giving them a real boost.

Buttler started cautiously before switching into full attack mode, launching Marco Jansen into the stands to become the leading run-scorer in Twenty20 history, surpassing Kieron Pollard's tally of 14,803 runs. He celebrated the milestone by clearing the ropes in each of the next two balls, before adding further successive sixes to bring up a 20-ball half-century and guide his side home with ease.

Sports.title: Infantino remains FIFA president following crisis meeting
Sports.content:
Under-fire FIFA president Gianni Infantino has shaken off calls to resign - for now - with the backing of the governing body's leaders, though apologised for "mistakes" in his botched attempts to sell off a stake in the World Cup.

In a statement released after seven hours of crisis talks in Morocco, FIFA said its management board had reaffirmed their "full support" for Infantino - including secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, only days after he had labelled the World Cup plans "a sad and reproachable series of events". The pair were later seen laughing together watching a Women's AFCON game in Rabat.

Infantino had faced mounting calls to resign following the leak of previously undiscussed proposals, after it was revealed national associations had not been consulted and had been given a deadline barely a month away in mid-September and the promise of a £30.1m incentive to back them.

In a letter seen by Sky News sent to national associations and signed by Infantino and Grafstrom, the pair wrote that they "sincerely apologised for the errors" in the plans which were eventually withdrawn on Saturday following days of criticism from across world football.

Twitter Twitter , which may be using cookies and other technologies. To show you this content, we need your permission to use cookies. You can use the buttons below to amend your preferences to enable Twitter cookies or to allow those cookies just once. You can change your settings at any time via the Privacy Options Unfortunately we have been unable to verify if you have consented to Twitter cookies. To view this content you can use the button below to allow Twitter cookies for this session only. Enable Cookies Allow Cookies Once

A second statement released publicly through FIFA.com hit back at those critics, threatening that FIFA would "no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation".

FIFA said it had "not been the intention… for member associations to feel excluded from the process" and admitted they should have been "handled differently" while further acknowledging "errors were also made after the proposal was leaked to media."

The governing body also promised a review would be conducted into the fiasco and a report into its findings presented at the next FIFA Council, comprising 37 national representatives from around world football.

Infantino and FIFA's reputation had taken increasing hits from inside and outside of its own walls over the plans with Arsene Wenger, its chief of global football development, distancing himself publicly while Infantino's personal senior advisor Carlos Cordeiro quit his role on Friday, labelling them a "bad deal" and "irresponsible".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports’ Kaveh Solhekol explains whether Gianni Infantino will walk away from FIFA after crisis meeting

The head of the Jordan FA went further by accusing Infantino of "blackmail", while UEFA announced it had "lost confidence in the current FIFA leadership" and the FA called for a "full and robust review of FIFA's leadership".

Those calls had grown further on Wednesday as legendary winger Luis Figo labelled Infantino's actions "the lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour I have ever witnessed" while Canada prime minister Mark Carney - whose country had welcomed Infantino in as World Cup co-hosts only weeks earlier - said the incident should be "fatal" for his position as FIFA president.

FIFA did not address those calls directly and instead said the marathon meeting would "strengthen FIFA's governance, help restore confidence in the organisation and enable us to prepare for the major events and challenges ahead in a united and transparent manner".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney speaks out on his lack of confidence in FIFA president Gianni Infantino following his private investment plans.

Timeline: How FIFA's World Cup private investment plan imploded

July 28: FIFA announces its "FIFA forward Enterprise" investment plan, proposing to spin off the commercial rights to competitions, including the World Cup, into a new company.

July 28: UEFA launches a fierce public attack, accusing FIFA of rushing through a transformative proposal with little consultation.

July 30: UEFA's 55 member associations vote to boycott World Cup if plans go ahead.

July 31: Infantino's adviser Carlos Cordeiro resigns amidst the controversy.

July 31: UK PM Andy Burnham says Infantino is the "wrong man" to lead FIFA.

August 1: FIFA abandons the investment plan after only a few days of intense opposition. Infantino withdraws the proposal before it reaches a formal vote.

August 1: UEFA releases a statement in which it says it has lost confidence in Infantino's leadership of FIFA.

August 1: Spanish league boss Javier Tebas says Infantino "must not continue at the helm of FIFA".

August 3: Wales becomes the first Football Association to officially withdraw support for Infantino's re-election as FIFA president.

August 3: UEFA reportedly threatens legal action and instructs lawyers to preserve FIFA documents and communications relating to the proposal.

August 3: English Football Association set to write to Infantino withdrawing its previous support.

August 5: Luis Figo becomes first legendary former player to call for Infantino's resignation.

August 5: Crisis meeting held in Morocco and FIFA reaffirms "full support" for Infantino.

What next for Infantino? 'Associations have levers to force him out'

Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol:

Infantino is a man with a very thick skin, obviously he's aware of what is being said about him - but his feeling all along has been that he was elected president by the 211 associations around the world which make up FIFA and if he's going to be removed, it's going to be by them.

The Prime Minister of Canada, Mark Carney, said he's lost confidence in Infantino. That's significant because Canada were one of the three co-hosts at the World Cup this summer, and Carney was at the World Cup final two and a half weeks ago sat near Infantino.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol provides the latest update regarding the ongoing situation with Infantino, as the Football Association is set to withdraw their support for the FIFA president

I don't think him refusing to resign is something all the associations around the world are going to accept after losing faith in him. They have a few other levers they can use to try to force him out.

There could be an emergency FIFA Council with a vote of no confidence, and he would be out if he lost. There could be an emergency FIFA Congress, with the same outcome.

If he wants to cling on and wait until the next presidential election in March, he may feel he has the numbers to get re-elected despite the opposition against him.

The date to look out for in that case is November 18, the deadline for candidates to declare themselves.

He has got his calculator out and still feels he has support in different parts of the world - South America, Africa and parts of Asia. He feels he lives to fight another day.

What were FIFA's World Cup plans?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martyn Ziegler joins the Paper Talk team to discuss Infantino's future at FIFA

Under the initial proposal to launch FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), football's world governing body aimed to raise up to $4.2bn (£3.1bn) from external investors through the sale of minority, non-controlling stakes in FFE, which it said would be valued at around $20bn (£15bn).

The governing body said its plans - which would have required approval from member associations - could deliver more than $10bn in "football development funding" over the next four years.

Who could replace Infantino?

Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol:

There's been talk about the president of Paris Saint-Germain, Nasser Al-Khelaifi, one of the most powerful men in world football, who is on the UEFA executive committee. But my understanding is that he is not interested in replacing Infantino.

Other candidates are people like Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, who came second in the vote to become FIFA president 10 years ago. He's the president of the AFC, who also oppose the sell-off plans.

Then there's the president of CONCACAF, Victor Montagliani. We've just had the World Cup in three CONCACAF countries and historically, CONCACAF have been close to Infantino, but they said on Thursday that they rejected the proposal as well.

Finally, someone I think would be very popular is Aleksander Ceferin, the president of UEFA. He has a totally different vision about the way football should be run. If he was the president of FIFA, there would be no hydration breaks, no FIFA Peace Prizes, no Qatari-owned private jets for the president, no $1m (£742,000) World Cup tickets.

But I don't think Ceferin has ever expressed any desire or interest publicly to replace Infantino.

Perhaps we are getting ahead of ourselves. Infantino is under a lot of pressure and it would be fair to say he is fighting for his job, but we are not at the stage where people are going to come out and say they are going to stand against him.

Sports.title: Castleford head coach Carr to miss the game against Hull KR
Sports.content:
Castleford Tigers head coach Ryan Carr will not be in attendance at the Hull KR game due to personal reasons.

Chris Chester, Scott Murrell and Rob Nickolay will lead the team in his absence and they will be supported by club legend and Man of Steel Adrian Vowles.

Australian Carr took charge in pre-season on a three-year deal having previously been coach of Featherstone Rovers and assistant manager at Leeds Rhinos in 2019.

A statement released by the club read: "Castleford Tigers RLFC can confirm that head coach Ryan Carr will not be in attendance at the Hull KR game this coming Friday. We can confirm that this is due to personal reasons, contrary to the reports on social media.

"In the interim, Chris Chester, Rob Nickolay and Scott Murrell will lead our on and off field operations. This leadership group will be heavily supported by Adrian Vowles and we thank Adrian for offering his support at short notice.

"We will not be making any other further comment at this stage, and we urge our fans to once again get behind our team this coming Friday."

Castleford currently sit ninth in the Super League table with seven wins from 21 games.

With six games remaining in the season, they face the Robins followed by Hull FC, St Helens, Catalans Dragons, Bradford Bulls, and Huddersfield Giants.

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

Sports.title: Fifa insists Gianni Infantino will remain president after Rabat crisis meeting
Sports.content:
Fifa on Wednesday night confirmed that Gianni Infantino will remain as president after a meeting of its senior executives in Rabat.

In a statement which also revealed that Infantino has sent written apologies to the Fifa council and the 211 member associations for failing to consult them over the World Cup sell-off, the world governing body said that he retains the full support of his leadership team.

Infantino had spent the day in talks with Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, and chief legal officer, Emilio García Silvero, during which he expressed his determination to stay on in the face of mounting criticism from Uefa and Concacaf – the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation – both of which have called for a review of Fifa’s governance.

In another indication that he plans to carry on as before, Infantino will fly to Colombia on Thursday to attend the inauguration of the country’s new president, Abelardo de la Espriella, in the city of Cali.

“Following a meeting in Rabat, Morocco, the Fifa secretary general and members of the Fifa management board in attendance reaffirmed their full support for Fifa president Gianni Infantino, as the only official elected by the 211 Fifa member associations,” Fifa said in a statement. “In turn, the Fifa president reiterated his full support for the Fifa secretary general and the Fifa administration for their necessary and outstanding work in the delivery of his vision.

“It was discussed and agreed that the processes, communications and interactions between the Fifa president, the Fifa secretary general and the Fifa management board that support the delivery of this vision can and should always be continuously improved in terms of their effectiveness and efficiency.

“In this regard, Fifa’s top management is fully confident that the outcomes of today’s meeting will strengthen Fifa’s governance, help restore confidence in the organisation and enable us to prepare for the major events and challenges ahead in a united and transparent manner while continuing our mission to develop the game around the world.”

While acknowledging that Infantino has apologised for his role in the abandoned Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal, which would have seen 21% of Fifa’s commercial rights sold to private investors, the statement also insisted that Fifa will not tolerate further criticisms of its governance.

Uefa is unlikely to be cowed however, with the European governing body continuing to search for a candidate to stand against Infantino in the presidential election next March, which will also take place in Rabat.

“Mistakes made were acknowledged,” the statement continued. “It was agreed that it was not the intention for the Fifa council and Fifa member associations to feel excluded from the process and that the process should have been handled differently. It was further acknowledged that errors were also made after the proposal was leaked to media.

“In a separate letter to the Fifa council and Fifa member associations, an apology was made for these errors together with a commitment to ensure they do not happen again. A review will now be conducted, and a report will be presented to the Fifa council at its next scheduled meeting.

“As previously communicated, the FFE proposal, which would have been subject to the approval of the Fifa member associations and the Fifa council, is now off the table. With the project withdrawn, it was agreed that Fifa will no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation.

“There are always lessons to be learned, and Fifa will continue to improve its processes in light of this experience. In this instance, however, it is important to stress that, although mistakes were made, everything that was done was done in full compliance with the Fifa regulatory framework.

“Fifa will work closely with the relevant stakeholders to examine how it can further support the development of the game through the Fifa Forward programme for the benefit of Fifa’s 211 member associations, the confederations and the regional associations.”

Infantino and Grafström appeared together at the Malawi v Zambia Women’s Africa Cup of Nations group game on Wednesday as a show of solidarity, having also written a jointly signed letter to Fifa council members and vice-presidents echoing the Fifa statement.

Sports.title: ‘Fifa Super League’: Infantino discussed having governing body’s name on European breakaway
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino held talks about rebranding the ill-fated European breakaway competition the “Fifa Super League”, with negotiations going as far as the term sheet for an agreement that would have changed the face of European football.

The term sheet, whose full contents can be revealed for the first time, is dated October 2020 and proposes renaming any new competition under Fifa’s branding. It outlines the extent to which Infantino’s administration were implicated in a scheme that caused widespread revulsion among fans and excluded clubs in April 2021. It also reveals that Fifa was prepared to sideline its member associations in pushing plans to cut back the number of international windows and outlines how global football’s governing body would have been given special governance and political rights with a “golden share”.

In a week when football is reeling from the fallout after Infantino scrapped his plan to sell chunks of the World Cup to private investors, the document shows Fifa’s leadership was deeply involved in another attempt to put the sport’s major competitions under corporate control. It sets out a partnership of at least 12 years between Fifa and the Super League and proposes a joint venture that would have run its commercial operations.

The document also proposes that an iteration of Fifa’s expanded Club World Cup, referred to as the “global club competition”, would be held annually over an enshrined three-week period and tied directly to the Super League. That tournament would have been a straight knockout competition rather than the group-based version that relaunched in 2025. While the term sheet states that the new tournaments would have to be passed by Fifa’s annual congress and the Fifa council, federations around the world are understood to have been bypassed in the plan’s formation.

Infantino was among a number of Fifa staff involved in the project and is understood to have been fully aware of its progression. The term sheet says the founding clubs “want to agree the terms of a partnership” between the Super League and Fifa, leading to the creation of the two competitions. It follows an initial proposal to Fifa by the breakaway clubs, also seen by the Guardian, that sketches the framework for a potential agreement. While non-binding, a term sheet is generally the precursor to a definitive contract and suggests discussions between Fifa and the Super League’s creators were nearing a conclusion at the time.

It is unclear whether Infantino and Fifa progressed their role in the project beyond the term-sheet stage. After a version of the scheme was infamously launched without Fifa’s direct involvement in April 2021, ultimately scrapped following large-scale protests, Infantino addressed Uefa’s congress in Montreux saying his organisation could “only strongly disapprove the creation of the Super League”. Multiple sources have stated that an earlier conversation with the Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, convened by a third party, hastened Fifa’s president distancing himself from the new venture. Infantino is understood to have told associates afterwards that he had no wish to work against football’s institutions.

Yet the evidence of Fifa’s outline agreement with the Super League, coupled with Infantino’s disastrous Football Forward Enterprise scheme, casts doubt on that assertion and suggests multiple attempts to reshape the game without consulting its most important stakeholders. The league would have contained 15 permanent members and five clubs qualifying from existing competitions. It also commits to creating a women’s equivalent, using the same clubs, by an unspecified date. The term sheet refers to Fifa under the name “WO1”, which is also the name used in the British army for a high-ranking officer.

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino later changed tack in relation to a European breakaway. Photograph: Louisa Gouliamaki/Reuters

In a section outlining the agreement’s key components, it says the Super League “is open to discuss naming the competition WO1 SL”. It also confirms Fifa would be “granted a preferred equity stake in the Super League”, which would give it decision-making capability on format changes, calendar alterations, distribution of solidarity money and the appointment of a chief executive for the competition.

Senior figures within European football are understood to have been shocked by the plan to drastically shrink the number of international windows, squeezing them into two fortnight-long spaces each year. Member associations, many of whom are being courted for support by Infantino as he battles to save his tenure this week, may have lost the commercial opportunities available from added visibility for their national teams and found themselves at the behest of a privately run club competition.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

A separate point in the earlier proposal also notes “reduction of leagues” as a point for discussion. The term sheet states that “a new international match calendar” devised by Fifa, the Super League and “other relevant stakeholders” would be reviewed and implemented with Fifa’s agreement.

Clubs participating in the Super League would have been required to join the World Football Club Association (WFCA), which was a short-lived representative body launched by the Real Madrid president, Florentino Pérez, in 2019. Real were key drivers of the Super League scheme and only closed the door on the project when announcing an agreement with Uefa in February this year.

Fifa’s close proximity to the Super League proposal adds to the growing number of privately backed ventures brought to the table by Infantino during his 10-year reign. In 2018 he pressed the case for a $25bn offer from SoftBank, the Japanese institution, to create an expanded Club World Cup and global Nations League. Close allies within Fifa are understood to have cautioned him against the plan, which failed to gain support after opposition from Europe.

Fifa was approached for comment.

Sports.title: How to fix Fifa: what can be done to salvage football’s beleaguered governing body?
Sports.content:
1) Split the governing body up

How can an organisation that runs the biggest sporting event in the world also be the one that sets the rules for the entire game? We saw the reality of such a conflict at the recent World Cup as Fifa ran roughshod over its rulebook – be it over the length of suspensions or the duration of half-time – in an attempt to generate more attention for its competition. One person with extensive knowledge of the inside workings of Fifa puts it like this: “They have shown that they will bend the rules to make them more money. This is a big conflict of interest. Not only should the commercial and the regulatory parts of Fifa be separated, but so should the development part and possibly one or two others as well.”

According to Miguel Maduro, a former chair of Fifa’s governance committee and now one of the leading critics of the organisation, the creation of different corporate entities – even if they ultimately came under its umbrella – would allow for different priorities to take hold. “There would have to be a Chinese wall between these entities and they would have to have different incentives,” he says. “Those who are seeking to maximise commercial income should not be dependent on the regulatory rules and those working on the regulatory side should not be influenced by commercial considerations.”

One insider notes that Gianni Infantino’s aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme would have created such a separation “but for completely the wrong reasons”.

2) Introduce external regulation

The least sexy word in sport might be necessary if a new Fifa – answerable to nobody bar the courts – is to be expected to follow its new rules. “Change needs to be imposed from the outside. It won’t happen from the inside,” says Maduro. He shares the belief with other critics that it would be necessary to create a new equivalent to Wada, the global anti-doping body. It would hold sporting organisations to account on rules related to governance.

“There’s so much money swirling around in football it could easily be funded,” says one Fifa-watcher. The question is under whose auspices the new body would be created. “One way is to do something at the level of the EU,” Maduro says. “Other countries could join, perhaps the UK for example, and that could then evolve into a world sports agency that would exist to review ethical issues and compliance of the sports associations.”

In this context it is perhaps worth noting that Uefa, which is leading the protests against Infantino’s FFE plan, has in recent years been moving closer to Brussels. Meanwhile another body, the European Leagues, has called on the EU’s executive, the European Commission, to intervene over another Infantino plan: to expand the World Cup from 48 to 64 teams. The commission, it said, “should take the necessary action to protect fair competition and ensure compliance with the principles already set out by the court of justice of the EU”.

3) Defang the president

As has been proven by the FFE affair, where the whole scheme was apparently devised without the knowledge of anyone outside Infantino’s office, Fifa’s president has too much power. “The president was not supposed to control the administration, but then he began to control the administration,” Maduro says. “Then the Fifa council was supposed to control the president and be involved in the real big decisions outside the congress, and they weren’t. At the political level itself you need checks and balances.”

One suggestion on limiting executive power would be to remove the president’s power to determine funding. The governance expert Mark Pieth has an alternative proposal, one he says was once mooted by the president of Uefa, Aleksander Ceferin. It would see the heads of Fifa’s six continental confederations taking turns at being president.

“It’s not an outrageous idea,” Pieth says. “I am Swiss and it happens in my country. Seven ministers take turns being the president, but their tenure lasts one year and it’s clear who the next president is because they go around in order. The effect is nobody gets really powerful. Then you ask yourself, well, why would a Fifa president need power anyway? He’s there to organise matters.”

View image in fullscreen Uefa’s Aleksander Ceferin (left) once floated a plan for heads of Fifa’s six continental confederations to take turns at being president. Photograph: Fernando Calistro/AP

4) Greater transparency

For campaigners looking to hold Fifa to account over the world body’s existing commitments, such as human rights, a lack of transparency over decision-making and the existing appeals process are longstanding frustrations.

Equally, what Fifa does with the money it generates and distributes to its member associations can be opaque. Nick McGeehan, the director and co-founder of the not-for-profit Fair Square, has frequently come up against the limits of transparency within Fifa. “Where are the audited accounts?” he asks.

“Fifa have a development budget that is equal to many big development agencies, but not only is there no needs analysis in terms of how that money is distributed but there is literally no evidence of any audits. Go on their website and you can find all sorts of data about what money is spent, but if you actually wanted to verify what that money is being spent on, it’s impossible.”

McGeehan notes that greater transparency would also involve engaging more with the media. “It seems like Infantino only calls a press conference once every four years,” he says. “It shows an authoritarian state-style distrust of the media and a concomitant lack of transparency.”

5) Rethink development

“Fifa is a not-for-profit organisation – the money it makes is reinvested in football.” This phrase has become something of a mantra under Infantino and following the $15bn (£11.2m) generated by this year’s World Cup, each member nation can expect to receive $8m between 2027 and 2030. But not only is there a lack of scrutiny over how the money is spent, the nature of the distribution itself is questionable.

“It’s an issue that one country, one vote is combined with giving everyone the same amount of money,” says the Fifa-watcher. “The money is distributed in proportion to votes, which is completely wrong because Montserrat and Gibraltar have very different needs to Nigeria or India. It’s amazing that he didn’t look to even try and tweak that.”

With money neither distributed according to need nor determined by strategic goals to grow participation in the game, Fifa is undermining its own aims, the critic says. “If Fifa were to be judged on results, then football is more Eurocentric now than it was 20 years ago. You can expand the World Cup, that’s easy. They claim it’s development but if you get into the nitty-gritty it can be a negative. Associations spend all their money on the men’s national team, on a European coach, and there’s nothing spent on the grassroots or technical development.”

View image in fullscreen The recent World Cup generated $15bn but there is a lack of scrutiny over how the money gets spent. Photograph: Hannah McKay/Reuters

6) Switch the electorate

The steady funnel of funds shared with associations big and small has kept Infantino popular with his electorate, the heads of his 211 member associations. A change in who gets a say in Fifa’s decisions might be another way to achieve more effective governance.

“When I am at a Fifa meeting and I look around the table, I see very few people who have direct experience of either playing the game, or being a coach or an executive at a club,” says one senior football figure. “I see very few people who actually understand the day-to-day of football.”

The overwhelmingly male makeup of the Fifa electorate is another fact at glaring odds with the real world, while supporters are, as ever, not invited to the party. Ashish Prashar, a political consultant who regularly engages with Fifa on the game’s social responsibilities, says: “What we need is confederations to get together and form a new entity to solidify the game with the values that serve the people. The biggest item for that entity must be fan ownership of the game. The World Cup and its surrounding events should involve the public in its decision making whether that’s fan groups, fan ambassadors or elections for fans.”

For Maduro, a change in the electorate could then unlock further progress. “Currently you have voting syndicates at Fifa, which creates a huge degree of voting control,” he says. “You need to force new mechanisms of representation, and be creative in finding solutions to bring in people that have so far been absent. If you create a diverse electorate that, by itself, will create a mechanism of checks and balances that can help to lead to better decision-making in the interests of football and all its stakeholders.”

Fifa was approached for comment.

Sports.title: Alessia Russo: ‘When you join the club, you take on a part of Arsenal and the love’
Sports.content:
Arms hooked over the bar at the front of the bus, sunglasses on, a drink in one hand and the other pointed towards the fans as she vibed along to the music and joined in with the singing and chanting, Alessia Russo was having a blast.

“I had the time of my life that day,” says the Arsenal forward of the 9km parade through the red smoke-filled streets of north London after Arsenal men’s Premier League triumph and Arsenal women’s Champions Cup success.

It has been a running joke among fans to refer to the 27-year-old as a “childhood Gooner”, a joke which was turbo-charged when the shirt a very small Russo was wearing in a family photo with the FA Cup was Photoshopped from a Manchester United one into an Arsenal one.

While she may not have been a childhood Gooner, she’s fast becoming an adult one.

“I came to Arsenal and I wasn’t an Arsenal fan, but since I’ve joined the club and seen the people around the place, it’s impossible to not become a part of Arsenal and to feel like I support Arsenal,” she says. “I want them to do well, I’m backing them every way, and then the parade was just one of the most amazing things I’ve ever experienced. The fans, the atmosphere, the celebrating the men winning the Prem, something that they’d worked so hard for so many years, I was just soaking it in, having fun and enjoying myself.

“It was just a really really special day. It was nice to experience it with the likes of Lotte [Wubben-Moy] and Leah [Williamson] who are proper Gooners, but I think when you come to Arsenal, and I’m speaking for myself here, you kind of take on a part of it and really start to understand and absorb their love for Arsenal. I definitely feel that and it’s really nice to feel like you’re a part of something like that.

“You pick out moments where you win trophies as the main ones that stand out within your career but that will definitely always stand out for me.”

There were faces everywhere, on every balcony, rooftop, bollard and traffic light, of all ages, races and religions. Young boys, but also, in contrast to the Arsenal parades of the 90s and noughties, so many young girls. Cultivating and supporting that fresh generation of girls interested in watching and playing the game is something Russo is incredibly passionate about.

View image in fullscreen Top: The Arsenal team drive past fans with the Women’s Champions Cup trophy in May. Photograph: Steven Paston/PA

Above: Fans celebrate Arsenal men’s and women’s success during the club’s victory parade. Photograph: Aldo Ciarrocchi/Alamy

That’s the reason she launched her own foundation earlier this year and why she helped launch the fifth year of Starling Bank’s Kick On initiative, which partners local businesses with girls teams desperately in need of sponsorship and subsidises the front of shirt sponsorship.

According to Starling – which commissioned surveys of 1,000 adult female football players, 1,010 11-17 female players, 501 small- and medium-sized business leaders and 1,092 grassroots football coaches – nearly every grassroots female football club (97%) said their team needed more funds, with opportunities for girls suffering as a result.

The survey also found that 76% of female players said they will have to drop out of their team or the sport altogether if more funding isn’t secured in the next five years and 40% of female players said their team doesn’t get the same amount of funding as male teams.

“They are quite damning statistics, which is such a shame considering the growth that we see in the women’s game,” says Russo. “Over the last five or six years, the growth has just been incredible, but there’s still work to do at the bottom to build it up.”

The risk is that women’s football loses its momentum and misses out on great players coming into the pathway.

“I always say you never want to miss out on the next Leah Williamson or Lotte Wubben-Moy, you don’t want to miss out on talented young players just because they haven’t got a local team or the team that they were at folds,” she says. “It seems like such an easy fix as teams don’t need much, but obviously it isn’t because it’s still a problem.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“I look back on all the people that I met through my grassroots journey and every single one of them played a part in my career, and I’m still friends with many of them. If local businesses can invest in one team, you never know, you might help produce a superstar who goes on to have an incredible career who will always remember you being a part of it. There’s more to it than just investment, it’s that you can really have a say in a core part of these young girls’ journeys and lives.”

View image in fullscreen Russo scored key goals in Champions League last season, including against Chelsea. Photograph: Harvey Murphy/News Images/Alamy

With no major international women’s tournament this year, Russo has enjoyed a rare summer off, where she has had the chance to focus on these broader issues she’s passionate about, as well as getting in some much-needed rest.

“It was really important that I did have some proper downtime,” she says. “Over the last few years, the minutes and tournaments have really increased, so I needed to look after my body and get myself in a good place mentally. I shut down for about two-and-a-half weeks and just enjoyed time with friends and family, which was lovely, but by the end of it, I was ready to start exercising again, I didn’t know what to do with myself.

“I quite enjoy training on my own over the summer, you get to know your best routines and habits. I often go on holiday with my family too and train out there on the family holiday, which is nice because everyone wants to get involved. I just took time for myself too, being a normal 27-year-old girl, going on holidays. I went to the England v Panama game in New York and got to be a fan and be around that buzz of the World Cup and I had Toonie’s [England teammate Ella Toone] hen do and wedding, which was amazing”.

View image in fullscreen After a few months off, Russo is back at Arsenal for pre-season training. Photograph: Alex Burstow/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

Russo had a standout year in 2025-26, many believe her game moved up a level for club and country. How does she reflect on it after some time off?

“I’m obviously pleased with my season for Arsenal and England from a personal point of view but, ultimately, I’ll always judge it on the trophies that we win,” she says.

“We’ve learned a lot as a team over the last couple of years at Arsenal, but are really hungry for the new season. We’ve made it quite clear that we want to do everything that we can to be the team most capable of winning the WSL and Renée [Slegers] has set the standard really high this pre-season. We’ve got seven new players that have come in, we’ve got a squad that’s raring to go, the competition in it is really high.

“So yeah, I feel happy but now I really want to continue to push on with Arsenal and England and win some trophies.”

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Arsenal back for £60m Konsa? Asencio to Liverpool?
Sports.content:
Aston Villa struggling to hold on to their World Cup stars has become something of a theme of this transfer window and off we go again with Arsenal stepping up their interest in Ezri Konsa. The Daily Mail reports that the Premier League champions, having had a bid for the England defender rebuffed last month, are coming back with a bigger offer for Konsa, who Villa value at £60m minimum. Meanwhile, Villa are trying to nail down a £14m deal for Atlético Madrid’s Italian left-back Matteo Ruggeri.

Liverpool are looking for defensive reinforcements and could swoop for the Real Madrid centre-back Raúl Asencio. The 23-year-0ld has been told he can leave the Bernabéu and various Mr 15%s have approached Liverpool about a move, reports Teamtalk. Also on Andoni Iraola’s radar is the teenage Paris Saint-Germain winger Ibrahim Mbaye. The 18-year-old, who scored a stunning goal for Senegal against France at the World Cup, is believed to be keen on a move to Anfield.

Across the city, Everton like the cut of Alistair Johnston’s jib and the Celtic and Canada full-back fancies a switch to the Premier League, according to the Scotsman, which reports that David Moyes and Martin O’Neill have already had a chinwag about a possible deal.

It’s all happening in Turkey. Mohamed Salah, whose arrival at Trabzonspor on Wednesday brought fans into the streets, could be joined by his old mate Darwin Núñez as the Turkish club prepare to party like it’s 2023. The Uruguayan striker has struggled since joining Al-Hilal in the Saudi Pro League last year and would be available on a free.

Elsewhere, Fenerbahce have been linked with a move, most likely on loan, for Real Madrid’s Endrick. Fiorentina and Roma have also shown interest in the Brazil forward, who was on loan at Lyon last season, but Fenerbahce reportedly fancy their chances of adding young Endrick to a maverick squad that contains veterans Nathan Aké, N’Golo Kanté and Marco Asensio.

After another summer of high-profile exits, Newcastle could do with some incomings and Football Insider reckons a bid for the Tottenham midfielder Lucas Bergvall is on the cards, though Nottingham Forest are also making eyes at the Swede. Down in west London, Fulham are eyeing up a deal for Southampton’s Northern Ireland midfielder Shea Charles, who Saints value at £30m.

Middlesbrough are poised to snap up the goalkeeper Radek Vitek from Manchester United from after the clubs agreed a £14m deal. The 22-year-old Czech spent last season on loan at Bristol City, making 41 appearances, and did not feature for United’s first team but that hasn’t stopped the Reds getting a 35% sell-on clause inserted into the deal, according to Sky Sports. Boro are also about to complete a £7m deal for the Spurs centre-half Ashley Phillips.

And Hamburg are keen on bringing the Leeds defender Sebastiaan Bornauw back to the Bundesliga after a year in Yorkshire. The 27-year-old has previously played for Wolfsburg and Köln.

Sports.title: Real Madrid agree club-record £115m deal for Yan Diomande and want to keep Vinícius
Sports.content:
Real Madrid have agreed a club-record fee of €135m (£115.7m) with RB Leipzig for Yan Diomande and are confident of warding off Arsenal’s interest in Vinícius Júnior after offering an improved contract to the Brazil forward.

After several weeks of negotiations that saw Paris Saint-Germain pull out of the race, the deal for Diomande – the 19-year-old who joined the German side from Leganés last summer and starred for Côte d’Ivoire at the World Cup – was finally struck on Wednesday afternoon. It is understood that Madrid will pay an initial €125m plus another €10m in add-ons, a total that would eclipse the fee the Spanish side paid Borussia Dortmund to sign Jude Bellingham in 2023, believed to have been worth up to €134m including add-ons.

Leganés are due a 5% sell-on fee from any transfer. The teenager made only 10 appearances for their first team before being sold to Leipzig for €20m (£17.4m). Diomande, who was pictured arriving at Leipzig’s pre-season training camp in Austria on Wednesday, is expected to sign a contract until 2031 and becomes the most expensive African player in history, surpassing the £72m Arsenal spent on Nicolas Pépé in 2019.

His impending arrival is not thought to have any bearing on whether Vinícius stays in the Spanish capital. The Brazilian and his representatives, Roc Nation, held talks with Madrid officials on Wednesday over a contract extension, with Arsenal waiting in the wings if he decides to depart.

Mikel Arteta’s side are understood to be ready to pay more than £100m for the 26-year-old who has less than a year of his contract remaining. But despite some reports that Vinícius had rejected Madrid’s latest contract offer, it is understood that he is now weighing up an improved deal closer to the €30m a season requested after what sources in Spain have described as positive talks. Vinícius said on Tuesday that Madrid’s new manager, José Mourinho, wants him to be “happy, cheerful ‌and playing my football” after returning to pre-season training following the World Cup.

Arsenal, who have agreed a £75m deal to sign his Brazil teammate Bruno Guimarães from Newcastle, are believed to be exploring other options in attack should Vinícius opt to renew with Madrid.

Barcelona’s sporting director, Deco, held talks with Atlético Madrid over Julián Alvarez on Wednesday in a bid to secure a deal for the Argentina forward but Arsenal are hoping that the 26-year-old could yet be persuaded to join them.

Arsenal, who missed out on Morgan Rogers last month when the England forward joined Chelsea for a British record fee of £117m instead, have also been linked with PSG’s Bradley Barcola, who is wanted by Liverpool and valued at around £145m by the European champions.

Sports.title: ‘Dream come true’: Eva Olid delighted after being named Manchester United’s new head coach
Sports.content:
Eva Olid has described being appointed as the Manchester United Women head coach as a dream come true after signing a two-year contract until 2028 with the option of a further year.

The Spanish coach will replace Marc Skinner, whose surprise departure came on Monday.

Olid led Hearts to their first Scottish Women’s Premier League title last season and departing the Edinburgh club by mutual agreement in a five-year spell during which she oversaw a remarkable period of progress.

The 40-year-old’s arrival comes as United are understood to be prioritising developing homegrown players rather than spending large transfer fees rather than spending large fees.

In a statement, the club said: “Olid’s appointment marks the start of an exciting new era for Manchester United Women as the club embarks on a clear vision for long-term, sustainable growth and success.

“Important foundations have already been put in place to further support the development of homegrown talent and young players, as well as senior internationals, and establish a clear football identity. Significant investment has been made into the academy infrastructure and facilities, underlining the ambition to build the leading youth development system in the country.”

Olid told the club’s website yesterday: “The opportunity to become head coach of Manchester United Women is a dream come true. The club has outstanding infrastructure and everything we need to achieve our ambitions. We have an excellent training facility, an academy that is already producing players capable of performing in a competitive first team, and an exceptional group of support staff.

View image in fullscreen Eva Olid signs up for Manchester United. Photograph: Manchester United/Getty Images

“There is already so much talent within our squad and I am excited to work with the players to support them to fulfil their immense potential. I am joining Manchester United at a really exciting time. There is a clear alignment in our shared vision for long-term success. I cannot wait to begin preparing a team that will make our incredible supporters proud.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

United finished fourth in the Women’s Super League last season and reached the quarter-finals of the Women’s Champions League, as well as the League Cup final.

Matt Johnson, United’s director of women’s football, said: “Eva is an outstanding coach with an incredible determination to succeed. Her remarkable achievements at Heart of Midlothian showcased her ability to maximise the potential of individual players, whilst also implementing an exciting style of football.

“Eva is the perfect coach to lead us into an exciting new era. She shares our commitment to developing exciting homegrown and young players, a tradition deeply embedded in our club’s history and culture, as well as improving established senior internationals, both of which form an integral part of our vision for long-term, sustainable success.”

Sports.title: ‘There is a clear vision’: Matthias Jaissle installed as Newcastle head coach
Sports.content:
Matthias Jaissle has described Newcastle “as an incredibly compelling place to be” after finally formalising his managerial move from Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ahli.

The 38-year-old German has been with his new players at their training camp in La Manga, southern Spain, since last Saturday but, despite also falling under the ownership of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, Al-Ahli took time to provide Newcastle with some vital paperwork regarding the release of a head coach they were extremely reluctant to lose.

Jaissle won two Asian Champions Leagues at the Jeddah-based club and, having enjoyed earlier success during a much-vaunted stint in charge of RB Salzburg, is regarded as one of the brightest young coaches in football. He will be installed as the head coach at St James’ Park.

Nonetheless, the task of succeeding Eddie Howe with the start of the new season only a fortnight away is considerable – and particularly as Newcastle have lost three key players this summer in Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and, now, the Arsenal-bound Bruno Guimarães.

Jaissle remains undaunted. “When Newcastle United come your way you take notice,” he said. “The ambition of the club, the vision for the future and the opportunity ahead made this an incredibly compelling place to be.

“I am incredibly excited about the future. I fully and unreservedly believe in this project, the ambition and the direction the club is taking. There is a clear vision, strong leadership and an exceptional platform to build on.”

Under Howe, Newcastle’s motto was “intensity is our identity” and Jaissle suggested he would be following a similar path. “My teams are built on togetherness, hard work and a passion to improve every single day,” he said.

“I believe there is enormous potential within this squad and throughout this football club. I give my complete commitment and total energy to bringing further success to Newcastle.”

With Howe’s coaching staff having departed with him, Jaissle is assembling a new backroom team but it seems David Hopkinson, Newcastle’s chief executive, and Ross Wilson, the sporting director, have full faith in his ability to revive the fortunes of a club that finished a disappointing 12th in the Premier League last season. “Matthias is one of the most exciting and highly regarded young coaches in football and I’m thrilled to welcome him to Newcastle,” Hopkinson said.

Wilson said: “Matthias’s leadership style and football philosophy are strongly aligned with our sporting vision. His teams play high-energy football and we could feel his passion during all our discussions throughout the recruitment process.”

Sports.title: Where to watch Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund: Mikel Arteta hints at team news with timeline for player returns
Sports.content:
Where to watch Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund: Mikel Arteta hints at team news with timeline for player returns

Arsenal return to the Emirates for the first time since being crowned Premier League champions.

The Gunners continue their pre-season with the Emirates Cup, welcoming German giants Borussia Dortmund to London.



7 Arteta is preparing his squad for their return to London for pre-season action where he will welcome back his captain Credit: Getty

Mikel Arteta's men are just two games into their preparations for the new campaign, taking on Spanish opposition so far.

They thrashed Girona 4-1 in their opening friendly before taking on Real Betis on Wednesday, which they lost 3-1 in Dublin.

“I'm disappointed with the result," Mikel Arteta told arsenal.com. "We are here to win football matches.



“We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I’m very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It's true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that's the learning from today.”



As for Dortmund, they've played four games already this summer, winning two and losing two of their outings.

The Bundesliga side have just returned from Japan, where they came out on top against Tokyo but lost to Cerezo Osaka.



Where to watch the match

This Emirates Cup clash will take place on Sunday, August 9.

Kick-off at the Emirates Stadium is scheduled for 2pm.

This is Arsenal's first match back at home since their 1-0 win over Burnley in May before lifting the Premier League title on the final day of last season as champions at Selhurst Park having beaten Crystal Palace.

7 Arsenal lost their first match of pre-season friendlies when Real Betis beat them 3-1 Credit: Getty

7 Former Arsenal defender Hector Bellerin was among the familiar faces in Dublin Credit: Getty

7 Arsenal fans and players got a reminder of what they were preparing to defend in the coming season at the Aviva Stadium Credit: Getty



Fans will be able to watch the action live on the Gunners' website and app, via their Pre-Season Pass.

Supporters can 

talkSPORT and talkSPORT.com will also keep you up to date with all the latest news, scores and reaction during pre-season.

What is the Emirates Cup?

The first Emirates Cup game was played 19 years ago in 2007.

It is a friendly clash that has been played yearly in various formats to celebrate the partnership with club sponsor Emirates.



When the event was first founded, four teams competed in a group stage, with each team playing two matches each.

7 The Emirates is hosting the Emirates Cup, the glamorous annual pre-season tournament involving Arsenal Credit: Getty

7 Arsenal captain Odegaard is back training after his World Cup exploits and could play against Dortmund Credit: Getty

7 Bellingham is following in brother Jude's footsteps in Germany and could play against Arsenal Credit: Getty



However, more recently, it has changed to a simple one-off tie.

Arsenal have won the Emirates Cup nine times since its creation, aiming to make it to double digits this pre-season.

Last year, the Gunners beat Athletic Bilbao 3-0 thanks to goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz.

What is the current team news?

Gabriel and Gabriel Martinelli should both be back to feature for Arsenal after rejoining the squad post-World Cup after playing for Brazil.

Meanwhile, Ecuador's Piero Hincapie, who joined the club in a permanent transfer, Germany international Havertz and Sweden striker Gyokeres will continue to get minutes following their earlier return from the tournament.



A host of other big names are due back soon, too, Arteta confirmed as he attempted to offer a timeline for key names returning.

“It has been ten days away from home," he said in reference to the pre-season tour. "So we’re looking forward to coming back, seeing some players as well."

Mikel Merino, Martin Zubimendi and David Raya all won the World Cup with Spain and were given extra-time to recover, while Eberechi Eze, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka all played for England.

"Martin [Odegaard] will be back and then the English and Spanish internationals will be back soon as well. So, we're going to start to have more and more players at the moment, we still miss a lot of them.”



Jurrien Timber remains a fitness worry in pre-season.

For Dortmund, 20-year-old England U21 international Jobe Bellingham is sure to feature, along with World Cup star Felix Nmecha in midfield.

Ex-Chelsea midfielder Carney Chukwuemeka was substituted with a knock last time out, so he is a doubt.

Sports.title: National League South club suspended and unable to fulfill opening three fixtures
Sports.content:
National League South club Ebbsfleet United have been suspended from the league with their opening three fixtures postponed.

Concerns have been raised about the club’s financial position and they had recently been subject to a winding up petition by HM Revenue and Customs [HMRC].

2 Ebbsfleet play in the National League South - but their opening three games are postponed Credit: Getty

The Fleet, who are managed by former Millwall, Leyton Orient and Gillingham player Josh Wright, have until 5pm on Tuesday, August 18 to provide satisfactory evidence that they can meet their financial obligations for the upcoming season.

The National League’s Compliance and Licensing Committee will review the case on August 19.

As a result, their opening three fixtures against Slough Town, Folkestone Invicta and Chelmsford City have been postponed.

National League statement

In a statement, the league said: “The National League’s Compliance and Licensing Committee convened on 5 August 2026, following recent correspondence and information relevant to the club, to further consider ongoing issues regarding Ebbsfleet United FC and its financial position.

“The club, which competes in the National League South, has previously been found in breach of National League regulations and is under embargo.

“One significant issue is settlement of PAYE liabilities dating back to April 2026, which led to HM Revenue & Customs reportedly issuing a winding-up petition against the club.

“The Committee considered ongoing non-compliance, in particular under Appendix H of the National League Financial Reporting Initiative.

“Appendix D Clause 4.3 of the National League Financial Reporting Initiative relates to a club's ongoing obligations in relation to its financial position. The Committee determined that these obligations are not met to its satisfaction, specifically regarding the club’s ability to meet its financial obligations throughout the 2026/27 Season.

“Following careful consideration, the Committee has taken the decision under applicable regulations to suspend Ebbsfleet United FC, with a review to be undertaken by the Committee on 19 August. As a result of suspension, at this time, the club will not be able to fulfil the opening three fixtures of the coming Season.

“A detailed letter has been issued to the club today, setting out the Committee’s decision. Ebbsfleet United FC has until 5.00pm on Tuesday 18 August to provide satisfactory evidence that its obligations have been and will be met in accordance with applicable regulations.

“The club remains subject to embargo until such time as the Committee is satisfied that relevant matters have been resolved.

2 Ebbsfleet have also been under an embargo since July Credit: Getty

“Opponent clubs for the first three published fixtures have been informed of the decision. Others have also been informed, including the Independent Football Regulator.”

Ebbsfleet statement

Ebbsfleet also released a statement explaining its position in relation to the winding up petition and the suspension from the league.

The statement read: “The club were informed by The National League at 9.31am this morning that, after a committee meeting last night on August 5, they have come to the decision to suspend the club for the first 3 matches of the season.

“The first 3 league matches will be postponed and re-scheduled for a later date.

“Obviously, for our playing group, management , staff and most importantly supporters, this has come as a shock and is extremely upsetting.

“The league wrote to club owners last week in response to the HMRC winding up petition and requested assurances around the debt and other liabilities and asked for a response by midday yesterday ( August 5)

“We had been advised these debts would be satisfied in time and our statement of August 4 outlined that.

“The owner’s letter of response to the league yesterday proposed the HMRC debt would be cleared by the end of August once a full transfer of ownership had taken place and the league in their letter this morning have highlighted that inconsistency in undertakings by the ownership.

“The league’s letter today also identifies their concerns around the club’s budgeting for the coming season and debt position , although that information was presented on July 10 with the club’s budget pack to the league within compliant timelines.

“Vetting and financial checks for the new proposed ownership and takeover have taken place over the last 12 months and were approved by the league on May 1 in writing.

“However, with the recent overturning of the Northfleet Harbourside development, the league have also raised concerns around the club’s financial viability, debt that has been placed into the club and how it is treated.

“The league have provided the owners until 10am on August 19 to rectify its position and demonstrate this to the league.

“Obviously our players, staff and supporters have taken a number of blows in the last week, none of which is within their control or a result of their work or actions, and we ask for understanding and care during this time while the ownership situation is solved.

“Everyone has worked so hard and completed an excellent pre-season and we look forward to this being rectified and demonstrating the results of that hard work throughout the season.”

Sports.title: Tottenham in line for seven-figure windfall from possible West Ham transfer
Sports.content:
Tottenham in line for seven-figure windfall from possible West Ham transfer

West Ham United are pushing hard to sign Troy Parrott, talkSPORT understands.

The former Tottenham Hotspur man is in demand after two prolific seasons at AZ Alkmaar in the Eredivisie.

2 West Ham are interested in signing Parrott this summer Credit: Getty

Parrott has netted 51 goals in 95 appearances for AZ since his move from Spurs in 2024.

talkSPORT reported last week that Fulham, Ajax, PSV Eindhoven, Real Betis and Como have shown interest in the Republic of Ireland star.

West Ham have now entered the race for the £25million-rated striker.

His ex-club Spurs are also understood to be in line for a 20 per cent share of any transfer fee, so could earn around £5m from a move.

Busy building

West Ham were given a massive boost in their bid to win promotion from the Championship when Jarrod Bowen signed a new deal.

The Hammers have committed their future to the club with a revised contract until 2030.

However, he can leave for as little as £15m next summer if West Ham miss out on promotion at the first time of asking.

Sales of Mateus Fernandes and Crysencio Summerville in deals worth a combined £153m have generated some much-needed income.

Academy graduate Freddie Potts has also left for Club Brugge in a £10m move, although his exit has been touted as a 'mistake'.

West Ham have been quiet in terms of incomings, but Joel Veltman is understood to be close to signing on a free transfer.

2 Spurs are set to benefit from a move Credit: Getty

The Dutch defender, who left Brighton in the summer, underwent a medical on Wednesday night.

Parrott could be second through the door in what would be a coup for the east Londoners.

West Ham begin their 2026/27 campaign on Saturday afternoon in the Carabao Cup against Portsmouth, live on talkSPORT.

Their Championship opener follows on August 16 as they take on fellow relegated side Burnley.

Many fans will already be looking towards their first match against arch-rivals Millwall, who they haven't played since 2012.

It was announced earlier this week that their clash at The Den on September 19 will be broadcast for free on ITV.
