Sports.title: Real Madrid move for Rodri in jeopardy as rivals launch transfer hijack
Sports.content:
Barcelona have entered the race to sign Rodri from Manchester City this summer, talkSPORT understands.

Real Madrid recently opened talks with City over a move for the World Cup winning Spain captain.

2 Fresh from winning the World Cup, Rodri finds himself at the centre of a high-profile transfer battle Credit: Getty

However, their famous arch rivals in LaLiga are ready to hijack the deal.

talkSPORT understands Barca are moving ahead of Madrid in the race to sign Rodri.

The 30-year-old is out of contract at the Etihad next summer, but City are still thought to be demanding a significant transfer fee, more than the £42million being reported.

City are not yet resigned to losing Rodri this summer and could elect to keep the four-time Premier League winner - even if he refuses to sign a new deal.

The midfielder, who won the Ballon d'Or in 2024 and the Golden Ball at the 2026 World Cup, is thought to prefer a move to Spain.

Rodri is expected to be sidelined for the beginning of the season, wherever that may be, after recently undergoing back surgery.

Keep at all costs?

City recently signed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m and are expected to land superstar Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi.

However, talkSPORT host Adam Catterall recently argued that losing Rodri could cost City their shot at regaining the Premier League title.

"There's a lot of chat about Rodri, at the moment, off the back of his fantastic World Cup (with Spain)," he said.

"I know that off the back of his injury last year, he wasn't at his scintillating best, but the World Cup kind of pointed in the direction that the Ballon d'Or winner is back to his very, very best.

2 Anderson is City's latest big-money signing Credit: Isaac Parkin / Manchester City FC

"I genuinely believe that if he does go to Real Madrid in this window, that will scupper any chances that Manchester City have of winning the Premier League.

"I think he's that influential. He has to be at City, if City are going to make a Premier League challenge this year."

Ex-Premier League defender Ashley Williams added: "My concern is that they've brought in Elliot Anderson and think, 'We can probably live without Rodri', but they can't, I think they need both of them.

"I love Elliot Anderson, I think he's brilliant, he'll be the future.

"But wouldn't it be great for him to have all that he's got already and learn off Rodri with the way he plays? And have both of them at least overlapping for a couple of seasons.

"At no point would you ever, ever get rid of Rodri, for no amount of money. They could offer me whatever and I wouldn't sell Rodri."

Sports.title: FIFA officials make immediate decision on Gianni Infantino’s future in emergency board meeting
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino will remain as FIFA president for now, despite acknowledging mistakes with his ill-fated World Cup plans.

Infantino has increasingly lost support and faced calls for resignation after the controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.



1 Infantino is set to stay on as FIFA president Credit: Getty

It would have seen a merge of the commercial and operational arms at FIFA into a body funded by private equity.

All 211 Member Associations were even offered $40million (£30m) by Infantino as an incentive to back the project.

The 56-year-old has been accused of 'blackmail' by the Jordanian FA president Prince Ali bin Al Hussein over endorsing his re-election.



And FIFA were forced to deny claims that Morocco were offered the World Cup final in exchange for an endorsement of Infantino.

Now, in a leaked letter after crisis talks in Morocco, Infantino apologised for the errors made with FFE but showed no sign of backing down.



The letter reads: "We acknowledge mistakes were made in the process of the proposed establishment of FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

"It was certainly not the intention for the FIFA Council and FIFA Member Associations to feel excluded from the process and it should have been handled differently.



"We acknowledge that errors were also made after the proposal was leaked to media. We sincerely apologise for these errors and commit to them not happening again.

"With this in mind, we will conduct a necessary review, and a report will be presented to the FIFA Council at its next scheduled meeting."

It added: "Furthermore, as already known, the proposal, which would have been subject to the approval of the FIFA Member Associations and the FIFA Council, is now off the table.

"With the project withdrawn, FIFA will no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation."



Infantino's position as FIFA president has also been backed by a media release published on the governing body's website.

A statement read: "Following a meeting in Rabat, Morocco, the FIFA Secretary General and members of the FIFA Management Board in attendance reaffirmed their full support for FIFA President Gianni Infantino, as the only official elected by the 211 FIFA Member Associations.

"In turn, the FIFA President reiterated his full support for the FIFA Secretary General and the FIFA Administration for their necessary and outstanding work in the delivery of his vision."

talkSPORT have reported that the UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin has discussed whether to ask all UEFA members that have backed Infantino to revoke their support.



Member nations have also threatened to boycott tournaments in a bid to oust Infantino.

Sports.title: Where to watch Liverpool vs Monaco: Andoni Iraola marks milestone and reveals Victor Munoz decision
Sports.content:
Where to watch Liverpool vs Monaco: Andoni Iraola marks milestone and reveals Victor Munoz decision

Liverpool have returned from their pre-season tour of the United States, but their friendly action continues at Anfield.

New Reds boss Andoni Iraola will be in the home dugout at the stadium for the first time, as his side welcome Monaco.



4 It's not a competitive game, but it still marks a first for Iraola as he takes charge of his first home game as Liverpool manager Credit: Getty

Fans could also see new signing Victor Munoz in action for the first time, too.

The manager told fans the no.23 made the decision to cut short his holiday to link up with his new teammates early having been given an extended break after winning the World Cup with Spain.

"You need time to adapt when you are moving to a new club and a new country so for me it was a case of the earlier I could get started, the better," he told the club's official website.



Asked if he will play against Monaco, he added: "Well, I think I’m ready. Obviously if the coach says so after training and asks me to feature in the starting XI, I’ll be there. I’m keen and I can’t wait to get started. [Against] Monaco, why not?"

So far this summer, Iraola's side have won two and lost one of their outings, being beaten 4-2 by Leeds last time out.



That disappointing result followed a 1-0 win over Wrexham and a 4-2 victory against Sunderland in the States.

As for Monaco, they've won just one of their three friendlies so far, beating French lower-league side Saint Priest 5-2.



After that win, they lost to Sporting Lisbon and then were held to a 2-2 draw against Belgian outfit Cercle Brugge.

Where to watch the friendly

This pre-season friendly will take place on Sunday, August 9.

Kick-off at Anfield is scheduled for 2:30pm.

4 Munoz didn't play for Spain so was more than willing to get to training sooner than later with Liverpool Credit: Getty

Fans will be able to watch all of the action live on All Red Video.

All Red Video is Liverpool's own streaming channel, which is broadcasting all of the club's pre-season friendlies this summer.

You can 



talkSPORT and talkSPORT.com will be across all the latest too.

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app.

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 



What is the team news?

In addition to Munoz being ready, Florian Wirtz, Ryan Gravenberch and Alexander Isak all made their first appearance of pre-season against Leeds.

They are sure to get some further minutes in this clash, while Jeremie Frimpong has raised some fitness concerns.

4 Frimpong asked to be taken off during Liverpool's last friendly Credit: Getty

Frimpong asked to be substituted last time out, but Iraola said post-match that he had not picked up an injury.



As for Monaco, former Arsenal striker Mika Biereth is set to feature, along with ex-West Ham defender Thilo Kehrer.

Manchester City loanee Mathys Detourbet will play too.

Liverpool vs Monaco: Special tribute

Liverpool have announced that a series of tributes will take place at Anfield in the coming weeks for legend Kevin Keegan.

Keegan, who scored 100 goals in 323 appearances for the Reds, sadly passed away in July.

A statement from the club reads: "Supporters attending the Monaco game will also see special tributes displayed on Anfield's LED screens, with a period of applause observed before kick-off and players wearing black armbands.



4 Liverpool will pay tribute to legend Keegan at the match Credit: Getty

"This will be the club's first home fixture since Keegan's passing and will provide an opportunity for fans to remember one of LFC's greatest players.

"LFC are also in direct contact with Newcastle United ahead of the Premier League opener at St. James' Park regarding special tributes to Keegan, who represented both clubs so successfully and managed the Magpies.

"In addition, a further tribute will be held ahead of the Reds' first Premier League home game of the season on Saturday, August 29 against Nottingham Forest.



"This will provide another opportunity for supporters to pay their respects with a special fan mosaic and a period of applause observed before kick-off, with players also wearing black armbands."

Hammers confirm Veltman

West Ham have confirmed the signing of former Brighton defender Joel Veltman.

The Dutch defender has signed a one-year contract with an option for a second year.

Barcelona have finally expressed their interest in Manchester City and Spain midfielder Rodri

The 22-year-old arrived on the south coast yesterday to finalise his £11.2m transfer.

A central defender became Boro's priority after Dael Fry’s decision to leave for Birmingham at the end of his contract.

Sports.title: Powerlifting racism row: Spotter declares 'I am racist' after sabotaging star's record attempt - admitting in astonishing social media post: 'I did it intentionally'
Sports.content:
A powerlifting assistant is under police investigation in Lithuania after claiming he deliberately sabotaged a Black athlete's squat attempt because he is 'racist'.

Belgian athlete Sonita Muluh's attempt to squat 334.5kg at the World Classic Open Powerlifting Championships in Lithuania in June was disqualified after spotting assistant Ernestas Kusinas placed his knee under the barbell during the lift.

After the event, Kusinas sparked outrage by claiming in an Instagram post that he had deliberately sabotaged Muluh's lift because he is 'racist', a remark he later insisted was intended to mock those accusing him of racism.

The Lithuanian Powerlifting Federation referred the case to police, who have launched an investigation into both the Instagram post and the events at the championships, a spokesperson told Reuters.

The Instagram remark read: 'Sorry for you morons, I'm racist and I did it on purpose because I hate you pieces of s***'.

If found guilty, Kusinas could face a maximum sentence of two years in prison.

Powerlifting assistant Ernestas Kusinas (above) is under police investigation in Lithuania after claiming he deliberately sabotaged a Black athlete's squat attempt because he is 'racist'

The spotter placed his knee on the barbell during Sonita Muluh's attempt to squat 334.5kg

Kusinas later told Reuters the Instagram post was written in anger and was intended to mock social media users who had accused him of racism, rather than reflect his true views.

The spotter claimed he had unintentionally interfered with Muluh's attempt as a result of being tired from his duties at the event.

Kusinas, who has since been banned for life from all powerlifting events by the Lithuanian federation and switched his social media accounts to private, claimed he had 'thrown him the bone he wanted' in response to an unidentified Instagram user who had accused him of racism.

Muluh, 29, became world champion in 2024 and has won medals at multiple Powerlifting Championships throughout her impressive career.

The Cameroon-born powerlifter's partner Kristof De ​Coninck urged that she could have won the event in Lithuania without Kusinas' interference, insisting poor assistance risked 'very serious injuries'.

'Initially, we thought it was a mistake,' De Coninck said.

'But then, it became clear (because of the social media comment) that the person had done it ⁠deliberately, motivated ​by racial bias.'

Speaking to BBC Sport about the controversy, Muluh said: 'It's shocking to wake up five weeks later and it's all over the internet that he did it on purpose because of the colour of my skin.

'I feel unsafe and uneasy that this person is standing beside me with massive weight, with what can go wrong, with the amount of weight on your back.

'I was lucky when I realised [it hit his knee] and I could stabilise it. Not everyone could. It was the heaviest ever squat for a female.

'(Kusinas) did not reach out afterwards to apologise, but he is not obliged to. I thought it was a human mistake, that cost me a lot on the day.

In an Instagram post after the event, he claimed he did it intentionally because he is 'racist'

Muluh, pictured in 2025, admitted she feels 'unsafe and uneasy' after his Instagram comment

'But there was no hatred [from me]. I didn't lash out; didn't curse at him. There was a video of it posted afterwards and I said: "I hope he does not get hate." I believed it was an honest mistake.

'And then I find out five weeks later that he said this.'

Meanwhile, the Lithuanian Powerlifting Federation has said in a statement: 'We would like to address the situation that unfolded on social media.

'We reviewed available information relating to Ernestas Kusinas and were deeply shocked by the views and activities addressed publicly which contradict the principles we stand for.

'The federation takes full responsibility for addressing this matter.'

Sports.title: Barcelona go head-to-head with bitter rivals Real Madrid in battle to sign Man City midfielder Rodri
Sports.content:
Barcelona go head-to-head with bitter rivals Real Madrid in battle to sign Man City midfielder Rodri

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Barcelona have finally made their interest in Manchester City midfielder Rodri official to rival Real Madrid for his signature.

Rodri wants to return to Spain for family reasons but Manchester City have been waiting for other clubs to declare their interest to get the optimum price for the 30-year-old.

They made a new contract offer to the Spain captain in April - who has one year left on his current terms - but are aware of his desire to explore a move back.

Rodri was keen on a move to Madrid but equally is understood to be open to joining Barca’s project where eight of the national team are in the current squad.

Barcelona beat Real Madrid to LaLiga last season, clinching the win in May with a 2-0 victory in El Clasico.

Rodri wants to return to Spain for family reasons but Manchester City have been waiting for other clubs to declare their interest to get the optimum price for the 30-year-old

Real Madrid president Florentino Perez was initially reluctant to back the transfer but others within the club have suggested it would be a good deal for the club and their image.

Rodri, who won the Ballon d'Or in 2024, goes into the new season having just won the World Cup with Spain.

Sports.title: Arsenal target Vinicius Jnr adds uncertainty to Real Madrid future as he wipes all pictures from his Instagram account
Sports.content:
Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jnr has deleted all posts from his Instagram account amid speculation surrounding his future.

The Brazil international has been offered a mouth-watering £19million a year contract renewal at Los Blancos, but is yet to make a decision on his future.

But their hopes of retaining the 26-year-old for the upcoming season seemingly took a slight hit on Wednesday night by deleting his entire Instagram history.

Vinicius' page, which has 64.1million followers – somehow growing by 200,000 since his post exodus – currently displays no images or bio and he's also removed his profile picture.

The attacker's current terms with Madrid expire at the end of next season and Arsenal have made their interest in the star known. If he fails to find agreement with the Spanish giants, they will be ready to pounce.

However, despite the Premier League champions lingering, and Vinicius' surprise social media deletion, Real are believed to be increasingly confident of keeping the Brazilian superstar at the Bernabeu.

Vinicius Jnr has decided to delete all pictures from his Instagram account with 64.1m followers

Talks between the player’s agents, general director Jose Angel Sanchez and chief scout Juni Calafat took place in Madrid on Wednesday. Jose Mourinho also underlined that the winger is firmly in his plans.

Vinicius' dramatic move to delete all social media posts could be cause for concern for Madrid, though.

While it is not uncommon among footballers – it could be interpreted in a number of different ways but typically can be interpreted as dissatisfaction with the current club.

This comes three days after he returned from his post-World Cup holiday, and started training under the new Mourinho regime.

Speaking to Real Madrid TV earlier this week, Vinicius said: 'It has ⁠gone very well, getting to know the new coach and the new ​players, and training very hard. Mourinho wants me to be as I have always been: happy, cheerful ‌and playing my football.'

But there is still hope on Arsenal's side that they can swoop in and sign the superstar, if the opportunity arises.

The Gunners made initial enquiries into the player last week, with manager Mikel Arteta insisting that the Premier League winners will be 'very ambitious' during the summer's transfer window.

One of the major sticking points in negotiations between Real and Vinicius' camp has been the re-signing fee. But the latest increase in their offer has left Real confident that Vinicius Jr will commit his future to the Spanish giants.

Real do not want to lose the Brazilian on a free, with his contract set to expire in less than a year.

The player is thought to view any contract he signs with Los Blancos, where he has played since 2018, as the defining deal of his career – and recognition of his efforts for the club that in recent seasons have seen him become a Ballon d'Or contender in their colours.

Sports.title: Trips into the bushveld, braais, Springbok endorsements everywhere and why Rassie Erasmus is the country's God: Daily Mail's journey to South Africa's rugby mecca
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Over the next month, the All Blacks will make their way around South Africa for what is being marketed as 'Rugby's Greatest Rivalry'.

They will play tour matches against the Stormers, Sharks, Bulls and the Lions, readying themselves for a blockbuster Test series with the Springboks.

It will pitch New Zealand's latest superstar Ruben Love against Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu and provide a gauge of how Dave Rennie's Kiwi project is shaping up for the World Cup.

On a trip to South Africa last month, I witnessed how the country has become rugby's mecca.

Setting off from Heathrow, we were soon airborne and making our way on Virgin Atlantic's overnight flight to Johannesburg. And what better movie for the journey than Clint Eastwood's Invictus. The perfect sporting docudrama to go with a glass of red wine from Richard Branson's vineyard in Cape Town.

Morgan Freeman plays the presidential role of Nelson Mandela and Matt Damon is cast as former Springbok captain, Francois Pienaar. It tells the story of how Mandela used the Springboks to unite their broken country at the 1995 World Cup. As he famously stated: 'Sport has the power to change the world. It has the power to inspire. It has the power to unite people in a way that little else does.'

Daily Mail Sport's Nik Simon visited South Africa - the mecca of rugby - and spent time with former Springbok Victor Matfield in Pretoria

Simon took a trip into the bushveld as he soaked up the culture. Here he is pictured beside a Nelson Mandela statue in Sandton

Every shop seemed to feature some sort of South Africa rugby brand endorsement as seen by Bok Bites - the snack of champions - Springboks

After landing at Tambo Airport, I set off on a 350-mile journey towards Limpopo to visit the family farm of new England centre, Benhard Janse van Rensburg. We drove over Crocodile River. They live in bushveld territory. I saw buffalo, giraffes, ostrich and, of course, springboks.

Van Rensburg's younger brother, HJ, fired up the braai in the evening and, in the background, the TV seemed to show wall-to-wall rugby coverage. There is an omnipresence with the sport, almost a religion to some.

On my next stop, in Pretoria, I happened to visit a church where the pastor asked the congregation if they were looking forward to seeing England back-row Henry Pollock getting 'smoked' by his opposite number, Jasper Wiese.

Every school, no matter the size, seemed to have its own set of rugby posts.

And every shop seemed to feature some sort of brand endorsement featuring Siya Kolisi, Handre Pollard and Cheslin Kolbe.

Since winning back-to-back World Cups in 2019 and 2023, the Springboks director of rugby, Rassie Erasmus, has become a national treasure among his public.

'Rassie is a God in South Africa now,' former Springbok Victor Matfield told me over a coffee.

Virgin Atlantic Clubhouse at Heathrow before flying from London Heathrow to Johannesburg

Simon pictured on board the Virgin Atlantic plane before setting off on a 350-mile journey towards Limpopo to visit the family farm of new England centre, Benhard Janse van Rensburg

The All Blacks will make their way around South Africa for what is being marketed as 'Rugby's Greatest Rivalry'. Pictured: A famous power station in Soweto

Madela's house in Soweto. Mandela famously stated: 'Sport has the power to change the world. It has the power to inspire. It has the power to unite people in a way that little else does'

'In the last four or five years, the team have really unified the country and brought people together. Rassie made Siya captain and now our team is the most representative team you'll ever get. A guy like Siya has got all the South Africans behind the Springboks.'

As a World Cup winner himself, Matfield has witnessed the power of rugby in South Africa first hand.

He was a part of the team that beat England in Paris in the 2007 final – but he believes that is nothing compared to the fever that sweeps through the country now.

'We got home and visited Mandela,' he said.

'The airport was full in Johannesburg and we went on a tour through the country. We went through townships, through Sandton, through Pretoria. We went into Soweto and as we drove in, we saw these Afrikaners, who wouldn't normally go into Soweto, in backyards braaiing with the locals. It just summed up what Mandela said in 1995 that sport unifies this country. What we achieved then was unforgettable. But this, now, is the most dominant era of Springbok rugby.'

Virgin Atlantic flies direct between London Heathrow and Johannesburg seven times a week with return fares from £624 per person, including complimentary food, drink, inflight entertainment and taxes. For further information visit https://www.virginatlantic.com/ or call 0344 8747 747.

Sports.title: Inside the fall of the Hundred: Attendances down, prices up and locals snubbed as counties fear massive divide once IPL windfall wears off. 'We've seen this all before - it was called LIV Golf. Is the Hundred even going to be here in three years?'
Sports.content:
When Harry Brook was wowing those at Headingley on Tuesday night with a no-look six during a record-equalling 50, it felt in that particular moment that everything might at last be coming together for the Hundred.

A competition with multiple launches but a recurring marketing campaign promising to take a new audience to new places – what better than a shot that wasn’t even a thing when 100-ball cricket was dreamt up? – was doing so through one of its homegrown pin-ups.

Undoubtedly, Brook’s 15-ball half century at Headingley just past the midpoint of the Hundred’s sixth season ticked all the boxes, fulfilling the pledges to make this competition second only to the Indian Premier League in short-form stature and to feature England’s premier players at its forefront.

The strength of the attack the 27-year-old was up against spoke of the quality on show this year: six of the London Spirit bowlers were internationals and the seventh was James Coles, the Hundred’s most expensive auction purchase ever at £390,000.

Yet that snapshot also exposed two sporting spheres colliding. In South Asia and North America – the territories from which this year’s new money in a £975million Hundred upgrade has come – franchises pop up, move cities and disband with minimal fuss while supporters are more willing to change allegiance depending on where their favourite players move.

Here in the UK, though, we are a parochial bunch and one trick that the newly owned teams either missed, or brazenly disregarded, was signing local county players to their respective Hundred teams to boost identity.

When Harry Brook was hitting a no-look six during a record-equalling 50, it felt in that particular moment that everything might at last be coming together for the Hundred

Australia stars Marcus Stoinis (left) and Adam Zampa (batting) are two of the international stars cementing the Hundred as the second-strongest short-form competition behind the IPL

Nowhere in the country is as insular as Yorkshire and it felt wrong during the early stages of this year’s auction that SunRisers Leeds were not going all out to recruit one of Joe Root, Jonny Bairstow or Adil Rashid. It left Brook and his former Burley-in-Wharfedale club mate Matthew Revis as the only familiar faces to relate to on Tuesday.

Southampton-based Southern Brave have just one Hampshire player in their ranks in teenager Manny Lumsden, a squad player rather than a first-choice pick and could not retain their local hero and captain James Vince in this season’s auction.

Somerset’s England Twenty20 international Tom Banton has played for three Hundred franchises, but has spent the past three seasons at Trent Rockets and admits continuity in squads is needed to deepen connections with fans.

‘If they're coming every year and there's new faces, I guess it's hard for people to get behind the team and support, isn't it?’ says Banton. ‘Whereas if you've been playing for a few years, they can kind of relate to you, get to know you and want to come and watch you.’

In contrast to the majority of their new-money rivals, the table-topping Rockets have also maintained the same colours and badge following the tournament’s unofficial relaunch. Five seasons of familiarity has been removed elsewhere.

Until recently, Headingley was full of purple-shirted Northern Superchargers fans. Overnight, following the complete buyout of Yorkshire’s stake in the competition by Sunrisers Hyderabad, they were being asked to form an orange army, and support Leeds rather than band together as the North. Best of luck.

Colours and identities are important to a British supporter base. Recall the anger when Cardiff City switched from blue to red shirts and ditched the bluebird for a dragon or when Hull City’s former owner Assem Allam applied to change the club’s name to Hull Tigers.

The Sunrisers are one of three teams to have changed names, along with Oval Invincibles becoming MI London and the Manchester Originals being renamed Manchester Super Giants. All have badges and kits to reflect their IPL links, although MI have retained the colours of the reigning three-in-a-row champions Invincibles for training.

‹ Slide me › Oval Invincibles won the last three men's titles wearing a turquoise strip, before being taken over by Mumbai Indians and becoming MI London, playing in royal blue

‹ Slide me › Meanwhile, the Old Trafford-based franchise have gone from being Manchester Originals in black kits to Manchester Super Giants in red and navy stripes

Southern Brave have gone from green and black to blue and red. Birmingham Phoenix have moved from orange shirts to black. To their credit, both Manchester and Leeds teams have begun schemes to make the switch easier, giving out replica shirts to every ticket holder at their early matches.

MI London launched a shirt amnesty in which turquoise 2025 Oval Invincibles shirts could be exchanged for the new royal blue ones. Additionally, they produced a club T-shirt for £20 under their ‘Twenty’s Plenty’ campaign.

Vikram Banerjee, the Hundred’s managing director, says that 40 per cent of those through the turnstiles are Under 16s and that ‘as we look to deepen and accelerate fandom, merchandise sales are a great barometer. Southern Brave and London Spirit are already having to restock, and nearly 40,000 fans are wearing the new jerseys of Manchester Super Giants or SunRisers Leeds.’ Presumably referencing the freebies.

Filling their grounds with a shirt-donning, flag-waving, family-oriented crowd has been championed as a success by the host counties too, but there are sceptics from within the county game about the real impact underneath the veneer, with one executive telling Daily Mail Sport: ‘The rebranding is utterly ridiculous. They’ve alienated the local people, and now they've whacked the prices up that nobody can afford it. And the sales are through the floor.

‘I don't know about anybody else, but I'm just looking at the Hundred right now and thinking we've seen this before – it was called LIV Golf. So, is the Hundred even going to be here in three years’ time?’

Whether it is the impact of the cost-of-living crisis, increased ticket prices or the rebranding that has proved a turnoff remains to be seen, but the Hundred is proving a hard sell in 2026. The first block of matches saw attendances down around 20 per cent on last year, the second block dropping by 27 per cent.

Crowds have generally picked up across the competitions since, but with ticketing operations now run by the organisations themselves rather than centrally, entrance fees hitting a high of £55 is an issue, even if you do get access to both parts of the men’s and women’s double-header for your money.

That is some hike for a competition that spent its first iteration between 2021-25 dishing out complimentary seats to its target audience of mums and kids. The problem with freebies, though, comes when you ask people to start paying instead.

The first block of matches saw attendances down around 20 per cent on last year, the second block dropping by 27 per cent

Brook’s blockbuster knock was watched by just over 9,000 spectators this week, a few hundred down on the 9,438 that turned out for the Leeds v Manchester contest. By comparison, the established Roses Twenty20 Blast fixture, promoted with a fraction of the budget, drew 11,300 at Headingley in June.

Kaviya Maran, part of the Sun Group that owns the SunRisers said the first signs at Headingley were ‘a good beginning’, adding: ‘Obviously it's a new brand for them.’

It was a similar story across the Pennines at Old Trafford, scene of a 16,500 sellout for the reverse Blast match. The cheapest tickets were £30 with £8 concessions for that, and while those for Super Giants matches cost less, starting at £24 and £5 in advance, their average men’s Hundred crowd has been under 12,000.

There have been some misjudgments. A huge proportion of Yorkshire fans will refuse to support a team with Leeds in its name, especially after the woeful attempt to incorporate Leeds United’s Marching On Together as the club song via a (swiftly deleted) social media post.

There have been highs, such as Welsh Fire setting attendance records for any women’s match in Wales and in the men’s competition on July 25 for the visit of the MI London teams. And the women’s game is benefitting with a higher percentage of people turning up earlier to stadia. Eighty per cent of fans that watched Southern Brave’s men on July 27 had been there early doors to see the women’s game too.

While the cash-rich Hundred stumbles, the county game it has kicked into the side verges has witnessed a series of triumphs. Helped by the presence of Ben Stokes, Durham sold out Jesmond when hosting Glamorgan in the MetroBank One-Day Cup and had to warn ticketless supporters not to turn up on matchday. There were 2,300 present to witness a thrilling match that saw Durham recover from 97 for six to knock off their 327-run target with three balls to spare.

Stokes was also in the Durham team that played to almost 5,000 in defeat by Yorkshire at York last week, 48 hours after the same venue accommodated 4,500 for the visit of Worcestershire.

Gloucestershire have had to expand their capacity for their visits to Cheltenham this year because of demand and although these numbers are more modest than the Hundred, full outgrounds are aesthetically pleasing to see and provide a county’s emerging players with an entry level for professional cricket.

By contrast, the Roses T20 Blast match drew a sell-out crowd of 16,500 - despite prices being higher than the Hundred

Peter Matthews, chairman of Gloucestershire, is an advocate of taking 50-over cricket to venues ‘that don't normally see cricket,’ adding: ‘It has echoes for those of a certain generation of some of the Sunday League grounds. Gloucestershire used to play a Sunday League game at a number of different grounds – Lydney, Moreton-in-Marsh, Gloucester – which we can't do now because it doesn’t work economically.’

Matthews says the lack of an obvious Hundred competitor in the region has helped footfall during the period between the World Cup and the start of the Premier League in a fortnight. And non-host clubs like his have been able to plan for more sustainable futures thanks to the £25million individual windfalls from the ECB’s big sell-off.

In addition to paying off their debts – ‘we got ourselves into a bit of a muddle,’ says Matthews – Gloucestershire ploughed £3million into a project codenamed Dressing Rooms, which drastically improved player and match official facilities plus general infrastructure at their Nevil Road headquarters.

Leicestershire are another to have been dragged out of the red by the Hundred’s millions, and they have begun feasibility studies on adding further non-cricket earnings to their annual income.

They have already been creative in this space on a smaller scale, holding drive-in cinema days last weekend and planning to install a 4G multi-sports pitch alongside the country’s largest playing area to be hired out during the winter. Their decision to allow children in free this month has resonated with their following, coming during the school holidays.

Chief executive Emma White says: ‘We're in the middle of a cost of living crisis, so I think there’s a ridiculous squeeze on the leisure pound. Are we getting a true reflection of the Hundred effect? I'm not entirely sure we are, if I'm totally honest. We're seeing a true reflection of the fact that people can't afford to do much at the moment.

‘The massive positive is that it's given quite a lot of counties more than you would imagine, the breathing space needed to kind of reset a little bit and almost future-proof cricket in their area by investing in revenue-generating projects.’

With the £25million lump sums viewed as a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to become less reliant on ECB annual handouts, counties – particularly the non-hosts – are taking their time to assess how best to invest. Durham recently received planning permission for an on-site hotel that they first discussed pre-Covid and will now employ a project director to produce a report on profitability, given the rise of costs in the hospitality industry.

Counties – particularly the non-hosts – are taking their time to assess how best to invest. Durham received planning permission for an on-site hotel that they first discussed pre-Covid

But there is a fear that however smartly the money is used, the disparity between those that have taken the finite sum and those still with skin in the Hundred game is only going to widen

The IPL might be a behemoth now but it took the expansion of the league from eight to ten teams in 2011 to truly realise its potential

But there is a fear that however smartly the money is used, the disparity between those that have taken the finite sum and those still with skin in the Hundred game is only going to widen.

‘Host counties are going to become wealthier and more able to attract the best players,’ said one county chair. ‘Fundamentally you're talking about those grounds having tradition, history and scale. It's very difficult to argue against tradition, history, and scale. They’re always going to generate more revenue than elsewhere.’

To back up the theory, the Lord’s-based Spirit have been valued at £300million – two and a half times more than the field. Suspicion remains around the shires that while this year’s competition will not return profits for the new investors, they are biding their time until expansion. Teams based in Bristol and Chester-le-Street would be the most obvious additions.

It was not until the IPL increased from eight to ten teams that the original set hit a goldmine, as the fee paid for the rights to own a new franchise would be distributed among the rest of the existing teams. And that with half the teams now controlled by powerful IPL owners, it is only a matter of time before Indian players are allowed to feature in a league outside of their own, significantly increasing its value in television and commercial rights on the subcontinent.

At which point, Hundred teams would potentially need fewer Englishmen and counties would be re-stocked with some of their primary talents, opening the chance to play the County Championship throughout August once more and easing a schedule already past saturation point. Unlike Brook’s shot in Leeds, all eyes are on what direction the Hundred will go now.

Sports.title: The clues Enzo Maresca gave away in Man City's K-League cruise: The new ways he wants this team to play, who's ready to start... and who isn't
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca will hope that Seoul’s searing and suffocating heat – the extent of which has seen local government advise residents to stay indoors – will fast-track the fitness of Manchester City’s squad before their season starts a week on Sunday.

A 3-1 victory over the K-League All Stars was noticeable for patterns that Maresca is trying to implement and the structures his new players need to work in.

But question marks do loom over key areas of the pitch as Daily Mail Sport looks at how the first proper week of the post-Pep Guardiola era is shaping up.

Manchester City cruised to a 3-1 win over the Korean League All Stars, scoring all three goals in the opening quarter of the match

Enzo Maresca will hope that Seoul’s searing and suffocating heat will fast-track the fitness of Manchester City’s squad before their season starts a week on Sunday

Kovacic stakes his claim

Mateo Kovacic was bullish about his future this week, claiming he never had the feeling from City’s hierarchy that a departure was in the offing this summer despite interest from elsewhere.

That throws up an intriguing conundrum around Maresca’s midfield options. With £116million club-record signing Elliot Anderson set to link up with the squad ahead of the Community Shield next weekend, and a move for Lille’s 18-year-old Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi progressing, the numbers are beginning to look crowded.

Kovacic would have appeared an obvious candidate to move on but he has been utilised as the deep-lying No6 in both of the friendlies so far – notably ahead of Nico Gonzalez.

Gonzalez has had the summer off after not being involved in Spain’s World Cup triumph, while Kovacic was Stateside with Croatia. Sources suggested at the end of last season that City would listen to offers for Gonzalez, who joined from Porto for £50million in January 2025.

Kovacic was replaced by Gonzalez at half-time of this win, with Tijjani Reijnders kept on for just over an hour amid interest from Nottingham Forest surrounding a £55million transfer. Reijnders has much to prove in the Premier League and his main characteristics – a strong ball-carrier who crashes into the box late – should make him an asset in the division.

While mindful of the level of opposition, he did himself no harm on Wednesday. An assist for Rayan Ait-Nouri’s opener came from Reijnders taking up a dangerous position in the right-hand channel – clearly an intentional tactic by Maresca.

His goal, swivelling first time to find the far corner following good work by Rico Lewis and Antoine Semenyo, was not the sort of action often seen in his debut campaign. But the manager was not exactly unequivocal about the Dutchman’s future.

Mateo Kovacic would have appeared an obvious candidate to move on but he has been utilised as the deep-lying No6 in both of the friendlies so far – notably ahead of Nico Gonzalez

Rayan Ait-Nouri gave City the lead inside nine minutes at the Seoul World Cup Stadium

Tijjani Reijnders, who has been linked with a £55million move to Nottingham Forest, put City back in front on 20 minutes with a low strike

‘He is here with us,’ Maresca said. ‘The players that are with us until the day that they aren't with us, it's my duty to do the best for them. I'm happy with his performance and he's working good since he came back from his holiday. At the moment I'm very happy with him.’

City will have big decisions to make on Reijnders and others in the coming weeks – even if Rodri is granted his Real Madrid wish.

Divin intervention

There are a number of clubs in the Championship weighing up loan offers for striker Divin Mubama, who scored his second poacher’s finish of pre-season when mopping up a saved Semenyo effort.

The 21-year-old West Ham academy product scored five times on loan at Stoke City last term and his role leading from the front gave some clues on how Maresca might want to deploy Erling Haaland.

City pressed with more intensity than expected, given the humidity meant the 35°C heat had a 'real feel' of 45°C. That came in the form of a 4-2-4 system, with Phil Foden up alongside Mubama.

Foden, though, was the one tasked with leading the closing down. Mubama dropped in deeper to something resembling a No10 position, sitting on the K-League midfield. That gave Foden more room and freedom to head off the press, with the rest following, and plays into his skillset.

Mubama, who is insisting that Maresca’s arrival represents a ‘fresh start’, is more adept at hunting down possession high up the pitch than Haaland, who can then serve a purpose by blocking off the passing lanes.

Divin Mubama turns in his second goal of pre-season to give City a 3-1 lead

Mubama's positioning as a No10 gave Phil gave Foden more room and freedom to head off the press, with the rest following

Wing wonders

New father Jeremy Doku is still to come back from the World Cup and will arrive as the premier winger at the club – but the fight for who earns starts on the other flank seems one-sided at the moment.

Semenyo has described Maresca’s philosophy as music to his ears, revealing how he was always struck by the clear instructions of Chelsea’s wide men to stay high.

The Ghana international has caught the eye in recent days, with that direct style favoured by his new boss. He’s done it off both flanks too, and wants to add a touch more mystery to his game.

Separate bits of ingenuity and power, showing off both sides of his talent, were meaningful contributions to a couple of City’s three goals. Both of those came shortly after Gianluigi Donnarumma was beaten at his near post by Kim Dae-won’s equaliser from the edge of the box. The Italian will hope to get those mistakes out of the way now.

Sports.title: England name throwback squad for Test series against Pakistan as returning captain Joe Root puts his trust in old favourites after Ben Stokes' retirement
Sports.content:
Joe Root’s first squad in his second coming as England Test captain has a real back to the future feel about it.

In recalling Surrey’s Dan Lawrence to bat at six against Pakistan at Leeds in a fortnight, it feels like a throwback to the tour of the Caribbean in the spring of 2022, Root’s previous series in charge.

Ollie Pope, Ollie Robinson and Matthew Fisher all featured in the squad during that 1-0 defeat to West Indies and their inclusions again indicate Root’s trust in them. A captain always gets the players he wants, particularly at the start of a reign.

It has been a case of needs must, however. A side already robbed of its balancing all-rounder with Ben Stokes’ retirement will now also be missing another crucial component in its No 3 Jacob Bethell, ruled out of Tests until the Christmas clashes with South Africa due to a knee injury.

Jordan Cox slots into that role against Babar Azam’s team, having made his debut against New Zealand at The Oval in June as Stokes’ replacement at No 7.

Despite the shift up the order, Cox’s retention shows continuity in selection, but it is something of a surprise that Ollie Pope returns as the squad’s spare batsman so soon after his axing.

Joe Root’s first squad in his second coming as Test captain has a throwback feel about it

Ollie Pope has returned to England's Test squad to face Pakistan in Jacob Bethell's absence

While his county colleague Lawrence has knocked the door down with five County Championship hundreds, earning the chance to resurrect a Test career the last leg of which came two years ago as an opener versus Sri Lanka, Pope’s recall comes on the back of just one in what has nevertheless been a solid 2026 - averaging 54 in Division One.

Former Test vice captain Pope lost his place to Bethell during last winter’s Ashes, but was name checked as a player with the ability to come again by England’s director of cricket Rob Key at the press conference to explain the pairing of Root with new coach Stephen Fleming.

Pope will be the spare batter in a 16-man squad that covers Test matches in Leeds and at Lord’s.

Returning to the old guard feels like a shift in policy from a previous regime who so often gave youth its head.

With Bethell out, Sussex’s James Coles felt like a potential like-for-like replacement, offering a left-arm spin option within the top six, but such a move has been resisted.

In the bowling, Hampshire’s up and coming quick Sonny Baker has been dropped, making way for the returning Brydon Carse, who has not played any first-class cricket since finishing England’s leading wicket taker in the Ashes, and Essex’s Sam Cook.

Bethell is out with a knee injury he sustained during England's one-day series against India

‘We have selected a squad for the first two Tests that balances rising talent with the experience needed against a quality Pakistan team,’ said national selector Marcus North.

Without a Test win since 2024, England’s new think-tank clearly do not view this new start as a time for experimentation, preferring to hand out a raft of second chances.

England squad to face Pakistan: Joe Root, Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson, Shoaib Bashir, Harry Brook, Brydon Carse, Sam Cook, Jordan Cox, Ben Duckett, Matthew Fisher, Emilio Gay, Dan Lawrence, Ollie Pope, Ollie Robinson, Jamie Smith, Josh Tongue

Sports.title: Godolphin superstar’s brother produces ‘wow’ moment with 21 length debut victory
Sports.content:
Godolphin superstar’s brother produces ‘wow’ moment with 21 length debut victory

Fortitudine, whose famous sibling is the recently retired Rebel’s Romance, produced a stunning performance to defeat the 5-6 favourite at Kempton

View 2 Images Fortitudine won by 21 lengths on debut (Image: https://x.com/RacingTV)

A brother of Godolphin superstar Rebel’s Romance produced a ‘wow’ moment on Wednesday night with a 21 length debut victory. Fortitudine is the three-year-old gelded full brother of the recently retired champion by supersire Dubawi.

‌



Rebel’s Romance ran his last race at Newmarket last month when he captured the Group 2 Princess Of Wales’s Stakes, the 22nd success of his career. He won nine Group 1 races including the Breeders’ Cup Turf twice, Dubai Sheema Classic and Hong Kong’s Champions & Chater Cup, finishing with career earnings of £12.2 million.

‌



Fortitudine has a long way to go to match those achievements but he began his career in impressive fashion on the all-weather at Kempton.

‌



Ffos Las race meeting moved to earlier start time to avoid effects of solar eclipse READ MORE :

The gelding went off the 7-2 second favourite for the 1m3f novice stakes behind the odds-on Dialstone, who had finished second on his only previous start.

Jockey James Doyle had him out of the stalls smartly and took him straight to the front. He kept pouring on the power, pushing right away from his rivals in the straight.

‌



The Racing Post analysis said the winner “produced a genuine wow moment on his debut, jumping from a wide draw at speed and keeping the gallop up right to the line to pull right away from the whole field. Post-race comments by the rider plus his starting price suggest this sort of performance wasn't expected at all, so he rates a most exciting prospect for the Charlie Appleby stable”.

View 2 Images Out on his own: Fortitudine at Kempton (Image: https://x.com/RacingTV)

Doyle was aboard Rebel's Romance when he triumphed in the 2022 Breeders' Cup Turf.

‌



He said: “He was quite professional. I gave him one tap, then he balanced up and away he went. He’s learning on the job nicely.

“He feels like he lengthens away. He doesn’t do anything too quickly, so I was keen to keep the revs up, keep him in a nice high gear and keep him galloping. The trip is right and he might even get a bit further.”

He added: “I was a bit surprised myself when I had a little look around. It bodes well; hopefully he's in for a good career.”

Sports.title: Michael Schumacher's family share heartwarming announcement
Sports.content:
Michael Schumacher's family share heartwarming announcement

The family of Formula 1 icon Michael Schumacher have revealed the positive news

View 2 Images David Schumacher and Vivien Keszthely are expecting their first child (Image: 2018 Getty Images)

The Schumacher family have shared a heartwarming update with the news that they are set to welcome a new arrival. Racing driver David Schumacher, nephew of seven-time Formula 1 world champion Michael and son of six-time F1 race-winner Ralf, has revealed he and his wife, Vivien, are expecting their first baby.

‌



David has been together with Vivien, herself a former racing driver who competed in the W Series and at Formula 3 level in 2019 under her maiden name, Vivien Keszthelyi, for several years. It was in February this year that they announced they had tied the knot.

‌



Sharing three pictures from the ceremony, they said they had married "surrounded by the love of our family and closest friends".

‌



And now they have even more wonderful news to announce. Sharing a photograph of a mirror, capturing themselves sharing a kiss against a stunning mountain backdrop, alongside a blanket, baby booties and a teddy bear, David and Vivien revealed they are expecting.

"Love made us two, life is making us three," read the caption alongside the image on Instagram. Within moments, the comments section was flooded with messages of love and congratulations, their combined following of over 150,000 fans sending their best wishes to them and their expanding family.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Michael Schumacher health update from family friend who's spoken with wife Corinna READ MORE :

Amongst those congratulating them was Davina Geiss of the Geiss family of German reality TV fame, who are close friends with the expectant couple. The joyful announcement comes just two months after David's father, Ralf, wed his partner Etienne in Saint-Tropez.

That ceremony took place less than two years after Ralf became arguably the most high-profile F1 driver ever to come out as gay, when he confirmed he was in a same-sex relationship with Etienne, who is 14 years his junior.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Ralf was previously married to David's mother, Cora, though the couple parted ways in 2014. Their relationship remained strained for many years, yet she publicly offered her congratulations to Ralf and Etienne on their nuptials.

"Steven [her new partner] and I wish Ralf and Etienne all the best and much happiness," Cora said. Ralf claimed six F1 victories throughout his career but was largely overshadowed by his seven-time world champion brother, Michael.

The entire family has fiercely guarded their privacy for over a decade since Michael sustained life-altering injuries in a skiing accident in December 2013.

‌



View 2 Images Michael Schumacher has not been seen in public for over a decade (Image: Lars Baron, Bongarts/Getty Images)

Very little remains known about his current condition, other than that he continues to require round-the-clock care from both his family and a dedicated team of nurses.

He is thought to spend the majority of his time at the Schumacher family home on the banks of Lake Geneva, Switzerland, though the family also own a lavish villa in Mallorca and a ranch in Texas, USA.

Sports.title: Liverpool could lose TEN players for nothing as they fail to learn their transfer lesson
Sports.content:
Liverpool could lose TEN players for nothing as they fail to learn their transfer lesson

Liverpool could suffer a massive loss in squad depth if they repeat past mistakes

View 3 Images Liverpool have plenty of work to if they want to keep several stars at Anfield (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

Despite Liverpool’s knack for recouping solid funds on fringe talent, their broader strategy around expiring contracts has cost them dearly. The Reds have had numerous successes in regards to player sales in the past, having previously sold the likes of Rhian Brewster for £23.5million and Sepp van den Berg for £25m.

‌



While they successfully leveraged £10m out of Real Madrid for Trent Alexander-Arnold by taking advantage of Madrid's eagerness to register him before the Club World Cup, their high-profile exits tell a much harsher story.

‌



Under the stewardship of Arne Slot, Andy Robertson, Ibrahima Konate and Mohamed Salah - who mutually agreed to rip up the last year of his deal - all departed the club for nothing this summer.

‌



The trio's exits could have resulted in a windfall if the Reds had learned from the free transfer departures of Roberto Firmino, Georginio Wijnaldum, and Emre Can in the past. The pattern may well be repeating itself with 10 first-team players currently poised to walk away for nothing next summer, unless contract renewals are agreed.

Virgil van Dijk, Alisson Becker, Curtis Jones, Harvey Elliott, Joe Gomez, Wataru Endo, Kostas Tsimikas, Stefan Bajcetic, Calvin Ramsay and Harvey Davies could all be experiencing their final campaign at Anfield.

Mohamed Salah agrees two-year deal with new club after emotional Liverpool exit READ MORE :

Virgil van Dijk transfer lined up as club chiefs 'gutted' at missed Liverpool opportunity READ MORE :

Reds captain Van Dijk will turn 36 years old a week after his deal runs out next June, yet remains an enormously influential presence at the club. Van Dijk clocked up the most minutes in Europe last season and it's still uncertain whether he'll be handed an extension on his £350,000-a-week terms.

‌



He's a prime target for MLS outfit Chicago Fire, who recently completed the capture of Robert Lewandowski. It did seem for a period that Liverpool supporters might have bid farewell to Alisson, with the Brazilian shot-stopper attracting attention from Juventus.

View 3 Images Joe Gomez, Harvey Elliott and Kostas Tsimikas have entered the last year of their contracts (Image: Getty Images)

Nevertheless, the 33-year-old chose to honour the final year of his Liverpool deal and could pursue a return to Serie A next summer or spend his latter years with boyhood side Internacional.

‌



Curtis Jones' future has been a persistent topic of discussion this summer as Inter Milan have repeatedly chased a move for the 25-year-old. Following a rejected £21m approach for the midfielder, the Serie A champions have approached the Reds regarding a £30m transaction, as reported by the ECHO.

Fellow midfielder Harvey Elliott has returned to Anfield following a disastrous loan stint at Aston Villa last season. The 23-year-old has been afforded an opportunity to impress Andoni Iraola this summer, as the Reds' shortage of options in midfield and attack could provide him with the chance to cement his place in the squad once more.

View 3 Images Alisson Becker and Wataru Endo could be playing their last season with the Reds (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

‌



Poised to begin his 12th campaign as a Liverpool player, Joe Gomez is the club's longest-serving member of the squad. The 28-year-old's persistent injury problems have meant he hasn't been dependable and is due to miss the opening of the season after sustaining a muscle injury in the Reds' first pre-season fixture against Sunderland.

Next summer could be the moment when Gomez and the club go their separate ways, but a return to Anfield will be arranged for his testimonial. Kostas Tsimikas will resume his previous position of backup left-back this season, after a disappointing season-long loan at Roma.

The Greek international, 30, acknowledged he's "really happy" to be back on Merseyside and will probably be afforded plenty of chances to prolong his stay at Liverpool, with the club involved in four competitions.

Midfield duo Wataru Endo and Stefan Bajcetic are both battling for their Liverpool futures this season. The Japan captain has been a useful squad player since arriving in 2023, but featured in only eight league matches in the 25/26 campaign.

Sports.title: Arsenal's 17 Brazilian stars ranked as Bruno Guimaraes deal nears – from Wellington Silva to Edu
Sports.content:
Arsenal's 17 Brazilian stars ranked as Bruno Guimaraes deal nears – from Wellington Silva to Edu

Bruno Guimaraes is set to follow a long line of Brazilians in joining Arsenal, though many of his predecessors failed to hit the mark in N5

View 7 Images Bruno Guimaraes is set to join Arsenal from Newcastle (Image: Getty)

Bruno Guimaraes is all set to become an Arsenal player after Gunners bosses finally reached a breakthrough with Newcastle United following several weeks of negotiations. The Premier League champions will sign the 28-year-old after agreeing a £75million deal.

‌



With personal terms long finalised and the midfielder granted permission to undergo his medical ahead of signing a five-year contract, Mikel Arteta is on the verge of landing his top target to reinforce the Gunners' engine room.

‌



When the Selecao star officially puts pen to paper, he will become the latest addition in a long and rich line of Brazilian talent plying their trade in the red half of north London. Arsenal's samba connection stretches back to the Arsene Wenger era and has remained strong throughout Arteta's tenure.

‌



Guimaraes arrives with massive expectations, following in the footsteps of compatriots who came before him, ranging from legendary Gunners figures to forgettable panic signings and fizzled-out youth prospects. Here, Mirror Football ranks all 17 Brazilians who have signed for Arsenal.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal set to agree blockbuster Bruno Guimaraes transfer as Newcastle demands finally met READ MORE :

Ex-Arsenal star makes winning return to English football with League Two club READ MORE :

17 - Pedro Botelho

Signed from Figueirense in 2007, persistent work-permit issues meant he spent his entire Arsenal spell shipped out on loan to various Spanish clubs. He departed in 2012 without ever making a single official senior appearance.

‌



16 - Wellington Silva

View 7 Images Wellington Silva didn't play an official game for the club (Image: Getty)

Arrived as a highly rated teenager in 2010 but work-permit restrictions forced him through five separate loan spells before he could officially feature in England. He eventually returned to Fluminense in 2016, leaving north London without playing a competitive first-team match.

15 - Juan

The left-back joined from Sao Paulo in 2001 but made just two appearances before a cruel knee injury halted his progress. He quietly headed back to Brazil in 2004 without ever getting the chance to launch his Gunners career.

‌



14 - Neto

You would be forgiven for forgetting the goalkeeper ever played for Arsenal. Brought in on loan from Bournemouth in August 2024 to provide experienced cover for David Raya between the posts. The veteran keeper made a solitary appearance in the Champions League before returning to his parent club at the end of the season.

13 - Marquinhos

One of Edu's signings, the young winger showed immediate promise by scoring and assisting on a dream Europa League debut against FC Zurich in 2022 after signing from Sao Paulo. However, he struggled to establish a permanent role in Arteta's plans and spent much of his time on loan away from the club before signing permanently for Cruzeiro in 2025.

‌



12 - Willian

View 7 Images Willian struggled in his only season at Arsenal (Image: Visionhaus)

Willian controversially arrived on a lucrative free transfer from Chelsea in 2020 but failed to reproduce his Stamford Bridge form in north London. After a miserable single season featuring just one goal in 37 outings, the best thing the veteran winger did was agree to tear up his contract and leave on good terms.

11 - Andre Santos

Andre Santos was signed in 2011 to plug a hole at left-back, offering plenty of attacking intent and memorable goals against Chelsea and West Brom. However, defensive frailties and an infamous half-time shirt swap with Robin van Persie made his stay short-lived. These days, memories of Santos are largely limited to memes, with some of his useful contributions being overshadowed.

‌



10 - Gabriel Paulista

Joined from Villarreal in 2015, bringing intense passion and aggressive defending to the Arsenal backline across 64 appearances. He picked up two FA Cup winners' medals during his two-and-a-half-year stay before returning to La Liga with Valencia.

9 - David Luiz

A polarising figure following his 2019 arrival from Chelsea, his two seasons were a rollercoaster of costly red cards and moments of brilliance. Despite the chaotic moments, his leadership off the pitch was vital during Arsenal's 2020 FA Cup triumph.

View 7 Images Luiz's arrival raised some eyebrows (Image: Getty)

‌



8 - Denilson

Signed from Sao Paulo as a teenager in 2006, the midfielder went on to clock up over 150 appearances during a transitional period for Wenger's side. While often scrutinised for his side-ways passing style, he proved to be a somewhat dependable option over five years in an inexperienced squad.

7 - Julio Baptista

'The Beast' spent the 2006/07 season on loan from Real Madrid as part of the exchange deal for Jose Antonio Reyes. Though inconsistent in the Premier League, his legendary four-goal demolition of Liverpool at Anfield in the League Cup etched his name in Arsenal lore. He netted a not-terrible 10 goals in 35 appearances before returning to Los Blancos.

View 7 Images Baptista didn't exactly thrive in north London (Image: Getty)

‌



6 - Sylvinho

Wenger's first-ever Brazilian recruit arrived in 1999 and quickly became a fan favourite thanks to his energetic runs and stunning long-range strikes. He racked up 80 appearances before passport complications unfortunately cut his Highbury career short in 2001, allowing a young Ashley Cole to take over at left-back.

5 - Gabriel Jesus

He arrived from Manchester City in 2022 and instantly revitalised Arsenal's attack. Unfortunately, the striker's career in N5 took a turn for the worse in late 2022 after his injury at the World Cup with Brazil. Since then, he has constantly battled niggles and a serious ACL injury, losing his spark but still managing to lift the Premier League trophy last season.

4 - Gabriel Martinelli

Plucked from the Brazilian lower leagues as an unknown teenager in 2019, he developed into one of the Premier League's best left wingers under Arteta. His progress has somewhat halted in recent seasons but his relentless work ethic and clutch goals have made him a crucial pillar of Arsenal's title-chasing era.

‌



View 7 Images Jesus, Martinelli and Gabriel are Premier League champions (Image: Getty )

3 - Edu Gaspar

A reliable midfielder who earned legendary status as a member of the iconic 2003/04 'Invincibles', winning two Premier League titles and two FA Cups during Wenger's tenure. He later returned to shape the club's modern era as sporting director, driving Arsenal's resurgence before departing in late 2024.

2 - Gabriel Magalhaes

Signed from Lille in 2020, the imposing centre-back has developed into a defensive cornerstone and a massive threat from set-pieces. Forming an elite partnership with William Saliba, he has established himself as one of the best defenders in Europe, with the potential to become Arsenal's greatest ever Brazilian by the time he hangs up his boots.

‌



1 - Gilberto Silva

View 7 Images Gilberto is Arsenal's greatest Brazilian (Image: Getty)

'The Invisible Wall' was the serene anchor of the undefeated 2003/04 Invincibles and scored the club's first competitive goal at the Emirates Stadium.

A World Cup winner and a true Arsenal legend, he brought invaluable composure and defensive bite across 244 appearances for the club.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola eyes £188m raid as gloomy prediction made by Reds hero
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola eyes £188m raid as gloomy prediction made by Reds hero

Liverpool believed to be looking to pull off a mega move in the transfer market this summer

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola is eyeing a major transfer raid (Image: Getty Images)

After a quiet summer, Liverpool could be set to significantly step up their transfer activity. The clock is ticking with the Reds set to face Newcastle in their opening game of the new Premier League on Sunday, August 23.

‌



Quite simply, Andoni Iraola's side are up against it when it comes to bolstering their squad with the transfer window also closing on September 1.

‌



The club has lost Mohamed Salah, who has joined Trabzonspor, Andy Robertson to Tottenham Hotspur and Ibrahima Konate to Real Madrid. Spanish winger Victor Munoz and French defender Jeremy Jacquet are the only signings through the door this summer.

‌



The Reds will play Monaco on Sunday, August 9, at Anfield as they enter the home stretch of their pre-season campaign. It looks like their off-pitch business is heating up too, as today sees the club eye a huge £188million transfer raid while a Liverpool icon has delivered a sobering message to his old club.

Huge £188m raid considered

Liverpool are reportedly targeting a move for Bradley Barcola and his PSG team-mate Ibrahim Mbaye as they look to bolster their options on the wings. Senegal international Mbaye joined the PSG academy in 2018 from Versailles.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Inside the murky world of FIFA lobbying as Jamie Carragher reveals World Cup request READ MORE :

Mohamed Salah agrees two-year deal with new club after emotional Liverpool exit READ MORE :

In 2024, he was called up by Luis Enrique to train with the first team after impressing in the youth ranks. Mbaye has eight goals and 13 assists in 36 games for PSG and while he primarily plays on the right he can operate on the opposite flank.

View 3 Images Bradley Barcola (R) and Ibrahim Mbaye are both wanted by Liverpool (Image: Getty)

The French giants are said to value him at around £43m. The Reds have had a long-standing interest in French international Barcola, with talks expected to get underway soon over a deal to bring him to Anfield.

‌



The reigning European champions are said to be demanding around £145m for the 23-year-old winger, although reports suggest the Reds are looking to pay considerably less.

Should Liverpool pull off a sensational double swoop for the duo, they may have to shell out a staggering £188m to bring them both to Merseyside from Paris.

Man Utd news: Atalanta star scouted as Michael Carrick ready to strike deal for £36.5m ace

Transfer priorities may have changed for Michael Carrick at Manchester United this month

View 3 Images Michael Carrick has yet to complete his transfer business this summer (Image: Michael Campanella/Getty Images)

Michael Carrick could be switching his transfer plans at Manchester United with less than a month until the summer window closes. The United boss has successfully transformed his midfield with the signings of Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos from Aston Villa and Chelsea, respectively.

‌



Just over two weeks remain until their season-opener against newly-promoted Hull City and Carrick remains on the hunt for new arrivals at Old Trafford. A defensive signing has yet to be made, but it could be on the cards as the Premier League giants target a player they've previously scouted.

‌



There's been several departures from the club this summer and one more player could soon be on his way out. Mirror Football takes a look at the latest transfer stories regarding United.

‌



Atalanta star scouted

View 3 Images Giorgio Scalvini has been a key star for Atalanta for a number of years (Image: Spada/LaPresse/Shutterstock)

Zirkzee departure

View 3 Images Joshua Zirkzee has fallen down the pecking order at Manchester United (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



United have yet to bolster their attack this summer, aside from the return of Marcus Rashford, but that hasn't stopped Carrick from entertaining the idea of letting Joshua Zirkzee leave the club.

According to Sky Sport Italia, Juventus are interested in signing the Dutch striker on a season-long loan. The 25-year-old has failed to establish himself at the club since his £36.5million arrival in 2024, scoring just nine goals in 75 appearances across all competitions.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Gabriel Martinelli transfer route becomes clearer as club 'braced for fresh bid'
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Gabriel Martinelli transfer route becomes clearer as club 'braced for fresh bid'

Arsenal's transfer business is gaining momentum as the Gunners eye several more deals before the start of the new Premier League season

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta has his sights set on defending Arsenal's Premier League title (Image: Getty)

After a steady start to the summer, the final month of the transfer window looks set to be an exciting one for Arsenal. The Gunners have landed Bruno Guimaraes for a fee of £75million after a lengthy transfer saga, tying the Newcastle captain down to a five-year deal.

‌



Having secured their primary midfield target, manager Mikel Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta are expected to turn their full attention to bringing in a defender and a marquee forward signing after being linked with several big names.

‌



It comes after the Premier League champions added some crucial squad depth early on in the window. They've already signed Piero Hincapie in a £34.5m permanent deal, back-up goalkeeper Illan Meslier as a free agent and winger Christos Tzolis for £34m as Leandro Trossard's replacement.

‌



More transfer developments are expected in north London in the coming days ahead of their Community Shield clash with Manchester City on August 16. But now, Mirror Football takes a look at two of the latest stories involving Arsenal in the transfer window.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

How Arsenal could line up after signing Bruno Guimaraes and completing Vinicius Jr transfer READ MORE :

Gabriel Marinelli's exit route

Gabriel Martinelli reportedly has several suitors ahead of a potential departure this summer. The Brazilian's playing time could be severely limited if Arsenal successfully sign another left winger, having been strongly linked with his international team-mate Vinicius Junior in recent weeks.

‌



View 3 Images Martinelli could leave the Emirates this summer (Image: PA)

CBS Sports reports that among the clubs interested in the 25-year-old's signature are Serie A clubs Roma and Juventus, as well as Turkish giants Fenerbahce, who are monitoring his situation in north London.

Martinelli will reportedly not rush to make a decision, given that he is currently happy and still has a year left on his deal. But talkSPORT reports he is not currently open to a transfer to the Saudi Pro League.

‌



This supposedly rules out Saudi Arabia as one of the many potential destinations he could end up at ahead of the new season. That's despite Cristiano Ronaldo's Al-Nassr showing considerable interest with the promise of a lucrative contract.

Villa brace for new bid

Aston Villa are reportedly set to receive a new offer from Arsenal for defender Ezri Konsa. They were said to have received a bid from the Gunners which fell well below the £60m valuation they have placed on the 28-year-old.

View 3 Images The Gunners are reportedly lining up another bid for Konsa (Image: Getty)

‌



But The Mail reports that Konsa has remained on Arsenal's radar since as a key defensive target. William Saliba's long-term absence due to injury is an important factor in Arteta's desire to sign Premier League-proven depth at centre-back, with Konsa's ability to play at right-back also a bonus.

Villa are not under financial pressure to sell Konsa as they recently sold Morgan Rogers to Chelsea for a mammoth fee. The England centre-back still has two years left on his deal, too.

Whilst Villa want him to sign a new contract, they are not at risk of losing him for free any time soon. They can refuse to deviate from their £60m valuation.
