The top two Dutch tennis players, Tallon Griekspoor and Botic van de Zandschulp, have both claimed major scalps in the second round of the Canadian Open.

Griekspoor, who turned 30 last month, put a wretched season behind him to knock out the world number three, top seed and French Open champion Alexander Zverev in three sets.

Zverev appeared to have overcome an early wobble when he rescued a set point before taking the first set on a tie-break.

But Griekspoor hit straight back to take a 4-0 lead in the second set, going on to win 6-2, before breaking the German twice in the decider to win 6-4.

“This is one of my most special wins,” Griekspoor said on court after the match. “There were times this year when I almost threw in the towel.”

Van de Zandschulp matched his achievement as he overcame blustery conditions to see off the Russian number four seed, Daniil Medvedev, in straight sets.

Multiple breaks

In an opening set that featured six breaks of serve, the 30-year-old Dutchman prevailed 6-3. The players broke each other twice in the second before Van de Zandschulp won the tie-break 7-5 with a sublime pass on his second match point.

“It was difficult for me and Daniil to play this evening and I’m happy that I got over the line in the end,” Van de Zandschulp said.

The results leave the draw wide open after world number one Jannik Sinner and 24-time Grand Slam champion Novak Djokovic opted to sit out the tournament, while the number two player Carlos Alcaraz is recovering from a wrist injury.

Griekspoor will face the Italian Matteo Arnaldi, who knocked him out of this year’s French Open, in the round of 32, while Van de Zandschulp takes on Poland’s Hubert Hurkacz.

Both players are also likely to rise in the ATP rankings from their current positions of 69th for Griekspoor and 70th for Van de Zandschulp as a result of their wins.

World.title: Bol and De Bijenkorf warn customers of possible data leak
World.content:
Online retailer Bol and department store chain De Bijenkorf have emailed customers to warn that their personal details may have been exposed in a cyberattack on a logistics company both firms use.

Hackers may have gained access to systems at CEVA Logistics, which handles deliveries for both companies. Names, addresses, postcodes, and phone numbers are among the details that may have been taken, broadcaster NOS reported.

Bol said its own systems were not affected and that the incident involves orders from a single distribution centre. Neither company has said how many customers may be affected, and De Bijenkorf has commissioned an external investigation into the breach.

Bol said there is no indication that payment details, passwords, or login credentials were affected and has taken part of its range offline – products handled by the logistics company – cancelled some orders, and stopped exchanging data with the firm as a precaution.

De Bijenkorf blocked access to the systems involved and added further security measures. It says customers may face delays to orders, returns, and refunds, and that email addresses and product information may also have been taken. The chain said it was certain no bank account numbers or passwords had been exposed.

CEVA told Bol about the possible breach on August 1 and the Dutch data protection authority AP was informed on August 3, but customers were only emailed on Wednesday.

A Bol spokesperson told NOS the company wanted to establish first what had happened and who was affected, rather than contacting people repeatedly.

World.title: Business confidence rebounds despite geopolitical fears
World.content:
Confidence among companies in the Netherlands has recovered sharply after a slump earlier this year, national statistics office CBS said on Thursday, though most firms also say they are operating in a more uncertain economy than a year ago.

It was the biggest quarterly improvement since 2021, but businesses remain more pessimistic than optimistic overall, and confidence is still below its long-term average.

Almost four in five companies said economic uncertainty had increased over the past 12 months. Wars and trade tensions were the main cause, cited by 42%, ahead of changes in demand and difficulty finding staff, suppliers, or materials.

Confidence improved in almost every sector. Construction and farming saw the biggest turnaround, though both still remain among the most pessimistic, along with bars, cafes, and restaurants.

Only the tech and media sector and the culture, sport, and leisure sector were positive outright. Car dealers and garages were the only sector to become more downbeat.

Nearly three-quarters of firms facing more uncertainty have changed how they operate, most often by making staff and working methods more flexible. Around one in five delayed or cut back investment.

World.title: Dutch intelligence service ranked third best in Europe

The Netherlands has the third most highly rated intelligence service in Europe, according to a ranking published by the French magazine L’Express and based on a survey of intelligence professionals.

The AIVD, the Dutch civilian intelligence agency, ranked third after Britain’s MI6 and France’s DGSE. Ukraine’s SBU and HUR shared fourth place, followed by Germany’s BND.

The ranking is based on votes from 60 intelligence officials in 25 countries.

Huib Modderkolk, who covers intelligence for the Volkskrant, told broadcaster NOS the Dutch have especially strong technical capabilities.

The AIVD runs a joint cyber team with military intelligence agency MIVD whose work includes infiltrating Russian and Chinese systems, he said.

It also works closely with bigger partners, including the US, and increasingly with other European services, he said. One example is Estonia, a small country whose service deals heavily with Russia.

World.title: Polish prosecutors end 10-year treason investigation into Tusk over Smolensk air disaster
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! After a ten-year-long investigation, prosecutors have concluded that Poland’s government in 2010 – which was led by current Prime Minister Donald Tusk – was not guilty of “diplomatic treason” in its response to the plane crash in Russia that killed President Lech Kaczyński. The national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party – which ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023 and is led by Lech’s twin brother, Jarosław – has always rejected the findings of official Polish and Russian investigations into the crash, which found it to have been an accident. Instead, PiS claims that the disaster, which claimed the lives of 96 people, many of them senior Polish state officials, was caused deliberately by Russia and then covered up with the help of Tusk’s government. However, while PiS launched various investigations during its time in power, it has never substantiated its claims. And prosecutors now say that there is no evidence that diplomatic treason, a crime that carries a potential prison sentence of up to ten years, took place. Teraz potwierdzenie @PK_GOV_PL: nie było żadnej zdrady dyplomatycznej ani żadnej intencji jej popełnienia. Oczywiście żaden z kłamców… https://t.co/VKZHlF5xkX — Radosław Sikorski 🇵🇱🇪🇺 (@sikorskiradek) August 5, 2026 Wednesday’s announcement by the National Prosecutor’s Office was welcomed by Radosław Sikorski, the current foreign minister, who held the same role in 2010. He condemned the “Smolensk liars”, such as Jarosław Kaczyński, who he suggested had exploited the tragedy for their own benefit. “They brainwashed millions of people, divided families, stirred up hatred within the nation,” he wrote. “They’ll burn in hell for it. But the power, money and satisfaction they gained from spitting on their rivals – that’s theirs.” The idea that Smolensk was an assassination of Lech Kaczyński has been a core part of PiS rhetoric. In 2022, for example, Jarosław Kaczyński said that the decision was made “at the highest level of the Kremlin” and Tusk’s government then “covered up” the incident as part of a “macabre reconciliation with Russia”. Smolensk was an “attack decided at the highest level of the Kremlin”, says Jarosław Kaczyński ahead of the 12th anniversary of the crash. Donald Tusk's government then “covered up” the incident as part of a “macabre reconciliation with Russia”, he adds https://t.co/5ae0gHJj3B — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 4, 2022 The investigation into diplomatic treason – a crime consisting of acting to the detriment of Poland while authorised to represent the country in relations with foreign states or organisations – was launched in August 2016, less than a year after PiS had come to power. Among the individuals who had formally notified prosecutors of a potential crime was PiS deputy leader Antoni Macierewicz, who from 2015 to 2018 served as defence minister. He has been the foremost proponent of conspiracy theories around the Smolensk air disaster. In their notifications to prosecutors, Macierewicz and the others accused Tusk and other officials of, in their relations with Russia, deliberately choosing a legal basis for an investigation into the crash that was unfavourable to Poland by giving it no real influence over how it was run. However, prosecutors now say that, after ten years in which they questioned 488 witnesses, gathered extensive documentation and requested legal assistance from several countries, they have “concluded that no crime of diplomatic treason was committed”. In a statement explaining the decision, the National Prosecutor’s Office said that the legal basis chosen for cooperating with Russia on an investigation – Annex 13 of the Convention on International Civil Aviation – was, in fact, “the most advantageous solution” for Poland. It ensured the participation of Polish representatives in the Russian-led investigation, including access to the wreckage and crash site. Other legal options would have offered no greater benefits and involved significant risks, concluded the Polish prosecutors. They acknowledged that Russia “subsequently failed to fulfil some of its obligations arising from the adopted procedure”, but said this should have no bearing on assessing the decisions that were previously made on setting up the investigation. The defence ministry will notify prosecutors of 41 suspected crimes linked to a commission established by the former PiS government to investigate the 2010 plane crash in Russia that killed President Lech Kaczyński https://t.co/aEAlmk9lDM — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 24, 2024 The prosecutors also found that, not only did Polish officials choose the best legal solution, but there was also “no evidence indicating that individuals authorised to act on behalf of Poland, including the prime minister and members of the Council of Ministers, acted with the intent to harm Poland”. Given that the crime of diplomatic treason requires intent, this finding further reinforced the decision to drop the investigation. However, the prosecutors note that their decision can still be appealed. At the time of writing, neither Kaczyński, Macierewicz, nor other senior PiS figures had commented on the prosecutors’ announcement. However, it is likely they will point to the fact that the current national prosecutor was appointed by Tusk’s government after it had removed the previous PiS-era incumbent in a legally questionable move. The Supreme Court has issued a ruling that effectively found that the government unlawfully replaced a senior prosecutor earlier this year However, the justice minister says the ruling has no legal force as it was issued by illegitimately appointed judges https://t.co/9fCE6d18uy — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 27, 2024 In 2020, in a separate civil case, a court ordered Jarosław Kaczyński to apologise for accusing Sikorski of “diplomatic treason” in relation to the Smolensk crash. Two years later, after Kaczyński had refused to comply with the ruling and Sikorski published the apology himself, Kaczyński was ordered to pay the costs. In 2024, an investigation by Tusk’s government found that the PiS administration had wasted tens of millions of zloty on a commission, headed by Macierewicz, that was tasked with re-investigating the Smolensk disaster. It notified prosecutors of dozens of suspected crimes relating to the functioning of the commission. Macierewicz, however, accused the government of spreading “lies and disinformation” designed to “protect Putin”. Poland has urged the European Union to adopt tougher measures in response to the recent migration crisis in Spain’s African exclave of Ceuta, including making migrants who enter the bloc illegally ineligible for obtaining residence rights. During a special meeting of EU interior ministers on Tuesday, Poland shared its own experience of dealing with “weaponised” migration from Belarus, which prompted the Polish government last year to restrict the right to asylum for people who cross irregularly. 🔵 KOMUNIKAT | Polska przedstawiła swoje stanowisko ws. migracji na nadzwyczajnym posiedzeniu Rady JHA w sprawie ostatnich wydarzeń w Ceucie 🇵🇱🇪🇺 Wiceminister spraw wewnętrznych i administracji @MaciekDuszczyk wziął udział w odbywającym się we wtorek (4 sierpnia br.)… pic.twitter.com/glfyiu5ZW3 — MSWiA 🇵🇱 (@MSWiA_GOV_PL) August 4, 2026 Last week, tens of thousands of migrants entered Ceuta, most of them by swimming there from neighbouring Morocco. Dozens died while trying to cross. Among those who managed to enter Ceuta, Spain says that the vast majority have been returned to Morocco. The incident prompted expressions of concern from many European leaders, including calls to restrict Spain’s participation in the Schengen free movement zone (despite the fact that anyone leaving Ceuta for the European mainland is subject to identity checks). Among those to speak out was Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, who on Friday called on Spain to “follow our example if Schengen is to survive”. Poland has tightened asylum laws, border procedures, and has built effective barriers on its border with Belarus, which is the eastern border of the EU. We have invested billions of euros and engaged thousands of soldiers, police officers and border guards. Spain must follow our… — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) July 31, 2026 That was a reference to Poland’s response to a crisis on its eastern border, where since 2021 Belarus has encouraged and assisted tens of thousands of migrants – mainly from Asia and Africa – to try to cross irregularly into the EU. Both Poland and the EU have accused Belarus and its ally Russia of deliberately “weaponising” migration in an attempt to destabilise European societies as part of Moscow and Minsk’s broader “hybrid threats” against the EU. Tusk noted that, in response, Poland has restricted the right to asylum, invested billions in strengthening physical and electronic barriers along the border, and has deployed thousands of soldiers, police officers and border guards there (who have also been given expanded rights to use firearms). A court has ruled that Poland's recently introduced partial suspension of the right to asylum is justified and lawful. It rejected a complaint by a Sudanese man who had been denied the right to claim asylum after crossing irregularly from Belarus https://t.co/jx3s1AxRgG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 10, 2025 On Saturday, Tusk and 21 other EU leaders jointly signed a letter expressing “serious concern” at the situation in Ceuta and warning that the EU “cannot allow uncontrolled mass border crossings, the instrumentalisation of migration, or other hybrid threats to create the impression that illegal entry…is possible”. While they welcomed Spain’s cooperation with Morocco to send most of the migrants back, they also called for an extraordinary meeting of EU interior ministers to “agree on a coordinated European response, including the rapid mobilisation of available EU instruments and the necessary support to Spain”. At that meeting, which took place on Tuesday, Poland’s interior ministry said that it had expressed the view that “illegal entry into the European Union should automatically exclude the possibility of obtaining residence permits, and therefore the possibility of permanent stay in the future”. While Poland’s statement did not mention it directly, earlier this year Spain’s government launched an amnesty that allowed undocumented migrants to apply to legalise their stay in the country. Over one million people had signed up for the scheme by the time it closed at the end of June. In its statement, Poland’s interior ministry warned that “migration must be fully controlled”, as otherwise it can “be used against the values that guide the EU”. It also called for the “official recognition of migration as a challenge directly linked to security”. It added that during Tuesday’s meeting it had “presented its own experiences with border protection in the context of the instrumentalisation and weaponisation of migration and adapting law to migration challenges”, including restrictions on asylum claims. “The example of Ceuta clearly demonstrates that absolute access to asylum is impossible to maintain in the face of such real threats,” wrote the interior ministry, which said that it “welcomed the shared perspective on migration among a growing number of member states”. In a statement of its own, the European Council noted that there had been a “common understanding of the need to continue relentlessly fighting migrant smuggling networks, to reinforce returns, to strengthen EU borders, to build deep partnerships with third countries, and to improve foresight.” It added that member states “were united in expressing strong solidarity with Spain”, appreciated its “swift and effective efforts” to deal with the crisis, and had also expressed their condolences for the people who died while attempting to cross from Morocco to Ceuta. ESPAÑA: CEUTA PIDE CERRAR LA FRONTERA POR LA LLEGADA MASIVA DE MIGRANTES DE MARRUECOS Más de mil jóvenes marroquíes se congregaron en la frontera con Ceuta para intentar ingresar al enclave español, y cientos lograron superar las barreras de protección, que en ese momento no… pic.twitter.com/Mx0LuQwMW2 — Clarín (@clarincom) July 30, 2026 When the migration crisis on its border with Belarus broke out in 2021, Poland recorded almost 40,000 attempted illegal crossings that year. Despite efforts to discourage and prevent crossings, the figures remained high, with just under 30,000 attempted crossings recorded in each of 2024 and 2025. However, those figures have fallen dramatically this year, with only 235 attempted crossings recorded in the first half of 2026. Meanwhile, the estimated number of successful crossings has been falling, from 12,000 in 2023, to 5,000 in 2024, 1,700 in 2025, and zero in the first half of this year, according to the Polish interior ministry. Last August, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen visited Poland’s border with Belarus, where she thanked the Polish authorities for defending Europe from “cynical hybrid attacks” orchestrated by Belarus and Russia. World.title: Unexploded WWII ordnance discovered under busy Warsaw street
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Part of central Warsaw was shut down today after unexploded ordnance from World War Two was found buried under a major road during construction work. The discovery, which came just days after the city commemorated the anniversary of its wartime uprising against Nazi-German occupation, led to traffic being diverted and residents being warned to stay away from their windows and avoid going outside while bomb disposal experts worked to safely remove the item. W Al. Solidarności znaleziono niewybuch, najprawdopodobniej z czasów II wojny światowej. ℹ️ Czytaj więcej: https://t.co/Fv6oe84XiM pic.twitter.com/BfjQPZveYZ — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 4, 2026 The object, reportedly around 70 centimetres long, was found early on Tuesday morning on Solidarity Avenue, a major thoroughfare, during modernisation work on tram lines. “We were digging a trench and I literally just touched it with the tip [of my digger],” the operator of the excavator who found it told broadcaster TVN. Staff working at the site were immediately evacuated to a safe distance. Police later confirmed that the item is unexploded ordnance, and that initial findings indicate it dates from World War Two. Bomb disposal experts arrived at the scene in the afternoon. However, they have not confirmed precisely what type of ordnance was discovered or its origin, reports Polsat News. Warsaw was the site of major fighting during World War Two, beginning in 1939, when Nazi Germany invaded and occupied Poland. In 1943, the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising, the largest single act of Jewish resistance during the war, took place. On 1 August 1944, the Polish underground Home Army launched the Warsaw Uprising, which was the largest single act of armed resistance anywhere in German-occupied Europe during the war. In response, the Germans destroyed much of the city, around 85% of which lay in ruins by 1945. Warsaw’s historic Old Town was meticulously rebuilt after the war. But many other parts of the city were redeveloped by the newly installed communist authorities, including Solidarity Avenue (which during the communist era was named after Polish-Soviet Red Army General Karol Świerczewski). Thousands of vehicles drove over the unexploded ordnance every day for decades. “Warsaw is marked by history, and there are many such surprises,” Witold Urbanowicz, spokesman for the city’s tram operator, told news website Interia. After the fall of the Warsaw Uprising – which began 80 years ago today – the German occupiers expelled the city's entire population. However, some survivors decided to remain among the ruins. They became known as "Robinson Crusoes" and this is their story https://t.co/UuVbfbcpQ4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 1, 2024 Unexploded ordnance is regularly found in Poland. In May this year, around 200 anti-personnel mines dating from World War Two were discovered at the construction site of a student dormitory at Kraków’s Jagiellonian University. In October last year, two men were hospitalised after an artillery shell that one of them had brought home from a forest exploded in his apartment while the pair were under the influence of alcohol. Earlier that year, wild boars unearthed 21 mortar shells buried in a forest since the war. In 2023, 72 unexploded artillery shells were discovered during renovation work at a primary school and four pieces of World War Two ordnance were found in the walls of a church undergoing renovation. Wild boars dug up 21 mortar shells from World War Two that had been buried in a Polish forest. The unexploded ordnance has now been safely removed without harm to either the animals or humans https://t.co/W9kaPr1BNw — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Russia condemns Poland’s “sacrilegious” demolition of Soviet monument
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Russia has criticised the demolition of a Soviet-era monument in Poland, calling the decision “sacrilegious” and a “flagrant violation” of an agreement between the two countries on respecting places of remembrance. However, Poland’s state Institute of National Remembrance (IPN), which financed the demolition, says that the monument was a “Soviet propaganda object” that was removed under a law requiring the “decommunisation” of public spaces. On Friday, around 150 residents in Pyrzyce, a town of 12,000 in northwestern Poland, gathered to watch the demolition of a monument to the Red Army that had stood there for decades. Initially, a memorial had been established in the town alongside a cemetery for Red Army soldiers in the immediate aftermath of World War Two, when the Soviets had driven the Nazi German occupiers out of Poland but then introduced a new communist government of their own. However, the soldiers’ remains were later moved to a military cemetery elsewhere in the region and the monument itself was redesigned and moved to another location within Pyrzyce. Its final form, created in 1984, was a huge rectangular concrete structure weighing several hundred tons and featuring a relief depicting the head of a Soviet soldier. A plaque said “Eternal glory to the fallen heroes 1941-1945” (a timeline that ignores the Soviet invasion and occupation of parts of Poland in 1939). Such Soviet monuments remained in many Polish towns and cities long after the fall of communism in 1989. In 2016, the then-ruling national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government introduced a law requiring local authorities to “decommunise” public spaces by removing objects and names that “propagate communism”. However, only in 2022, after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, did the removal of Soviet-era monuments gather pace, with dozens demolished since then. Those efforts were led by the IPN, in particular during the time that the institute was headed by Karol Nawrocki between 2021 and last year, when he was elected president of Poland. Another Soviet memorial has been demolished in Poland – the 43rd since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. "We say ‘no’ to Russians who believe these lands somehow belong to their sphere of influence,” declared the Institute of National Remembrance https://t.co/aG9VQVlUQI — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 12, 2025 At the start of this year, the local authorities in Pyrzyce began public consultations on removing their Soviet memorial, finding that a majority were in favour of the move, according to the IPN. In February, the town council voted to remove the monument. It will now be replaced with a new one commemorating Polish independence. “We are aware that this change evokes various, often very strong, emotions among residents,” wrote the local authorities on social media. “We respect both the voices of those supporting the actions taken and those who differ in their assessment of the current monument and its place in the history of Pyrzyce.” “We hope that independence – as a paramount value for all Poles – will unite residents beyond differences of opinion and assessment of the past. We want the emerging space to be a space of shared remembrance, reflection, and a dignified celebration of the most important national ceremonies.” The removal of the monument drew condemnation from the Russian embassy in Warsaw, which announced on Monday that it had lodged a formal protest. It called the decision the “latest sacrilegious step by the Polish authorities” and said that it “constitutes a direct and flagrant violation” of a 1994 agreement between Poland and Russia on respect for graves and other places of memory. “The illegal dismantling of monuments is an overt attempt to falsify history, to erase from the consciousness of the Polish nation the memory of the heroism of Soviet soldiers,” added the embassy. ⚡️Komentarz Ambasady Rosji w Polsce 31 lipca 2026 r. w Pyrzycach (województwo zachodniopomorskie) na podstawie decyzji władz polskich został przeprowadzony demontaż pomnika ku czci poległych w latach 1941–1945 bohaterów – żołnierzy radzieckich. ❗️Ten kolejny świętokradczy krok… pic.twitter.com/cKhfFxIL9s — Russian Embassy, PL (@rusemb_pl) August 3, 2026 In response to such complaints from Russia, Poland has regularly pointed out that the 1994 agreement relates to graves and war cemeteries, not separate monuments and symbols, which can be legally removed. The IPN notes that such monuments were “Soviet propaganda objects”, designed to support the Moscow-backed communist regime, rather than genuine places of commemoration. Attending the demolition ceremony in Pyrzyce on Friday, IPN deputy president Karol Polejowski pointed out that the final version of the monument had been established in 1984 shortly after the period of martial law in Poland, when the authorities brutally clamped down on the democratic opposition. “Local communist activists, eager to curry favour with their Soviet masters, erected a monument honouring the Soviet army. This is not a symbol of liberation – it is a symbol of enslavement!” he declared, as the monument was torn down. 💪 Sowiecki obiekt propagandowy zostanie zastąpiony przez Pomnik Niepodległości, a przestrzeń wokół nowego monumentu stanie się godną sceną dla uroczystości patriotycznych. pic.twitter.com/5x4KEzG3Vb — Instytut Pamięci Narodowej (@ipngovpl) July 31, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland’s WIG20 stock market index hits record high
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s blue-chip WIG20 stock market index hit its highest ever level on Monday, surpassing a record that had stood for almost 19 years. The WIG20 has been Europe’s best-performing major blue-chip index so far this year. According to market monitoring website MarketScreener, the index has gained just under 25% since the start of 2026, ahead of the Dutch AEX (16.9%) and Sweden’s OMX Stockholm (14.9%). The WIG20, which tracks the 20 largest and most liquid companies on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (GPW), climbed to 3,963.21 points on Monday, breaking its previous record of 3,940.53 points set in October 2007. It continues a rally that began in October 2022, since when the index has almost tripled in value. “The market continues to be supported by solid economic growth, rising consumer spending, and the prospect of further EU investment,” commented analysts from BNP Paribas, a bank, quoted by business daily Parkiet. “However, after such strong gains, we do not expect the pace of appreciation to remain as high as in recent years,” they added. On Monday, the biggest boosts to the WIG20 index were provided by PGE, Poland’s biggest power producer, and KGHM, a Polish multinational mining company, with their shares rising 3.3% and 1.6%, respectively. The surge was also supported by improving risk appetite across global markets following signs of a de-escalation in tensions in the Middle East. This has pushed WIG20 above the levels last seen 19 years ago, just before the index plunged almost 70% during the 2008 global financial crisis, and then suffered another sell-off during the euro zone debt crisis in 2011. Reform of one of the pillars of Poland’s pension system in 2014, which reduced the role of open pension funds, ushered in years of market stagnation and left the index struggling to meaningfully rebound in the following years. Another decline came during the COVID-19 pandemic and then in the aftermath of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. In October 2022, however, the WIG20 started its rebound, rising by 195% since then. More than 30 Polish-listed companies have doubled in value over the past three years, including large-cap stocks such as Orlen, PKO BP, Bank Pekao, KGHM and Tauron, according to an analysis by economic journalist Rafał Hirsch published by news service WNP. Polish state energy firm Orlen has seen its market valuation rise to its highest ever level, and surpass Russia’s Gazprom for the first time https://t.co/w3po4izshJ — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 12, 2026 BNP Paribas’s analysts, however, note that, “despite a long-term upward trend and reaching record highs”, the Polish stock market “is still valued below many other European markets”. “Our stock market…remains significantly cheaper than the US market and most European markets, but at the same time, when viewed against its own historical performance, it is now relatively highly valued,” they said. Poland’s main stock index, the broader WIG, also closed on Monday at a record high of 148,428 points, having hit several records in recent months. Poland’s benchmark WIG stock index has passed the 100,000-point mark for the first time. Meanwhile, the Warsaw Stock Exchange has been the world’s best performing so far this year "It is a clear signal of the strength of our economy," says the PM's office https://t.co/fIgGWOLLn8 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 25, 2025 Analysts warn, however, that unlike in the case of WIG, the WIG20’s record may prove short-lived because the benchmark is a price index, which excludes dividends. When companies in the index pay dividends, their share prices usually fall by about the same amount, which automatically pulls the index down even if nothing has changed in the companies themselves. Monday was the last day investors could buy shares in PKO BP and qualify for this year’s dividend. From Tuesday, the bank’s shares will trade ex-dividend, a move expected to reduce the WIG20 by about 0.8% because of PKO BP’s large weighting in the index. World.title: Morawiecki confirms breakaway Polish opposition group will form new party

Mateusz Morawiecki has confirmed that the group he leads, Development Plus (Rozwój Plus), which is in the process of splitting from the national-conservative opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party, will soon form a party of its own. He laid out a vision of a more moderate, centre-right party that would focus on economic development rather than “ideological disputes” over abortion or same-sex marriage. However, Morawiecki made clear he retains a hardline position on migration, saying he wants “zero Muslim migrants”, even legal ones, in Europe. He also categorically ruled out ever working with current Prime Minister Donald Tusk, but left the door open to potentially cooperating with the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL), which is part of Tusk’s current ruling coalition, and with the far-right Confederation (Konfederacja), an opposition group. Morawiecki u Rymanowskiego: „Do 15 października założymy partię” No coraz ciekawiej 👀 pic.twitter.com/0FrMafvTEl — chrzanik (@chrzanikx) August 3, 2026 Development Plus was founded as an association by Morawiecki, a former PiS prime minister and current deputy leader of the party, in April this year. That immediately prompted criticism from some other members of the party, who saw it as a step towards creating a breakaway group. Matters came to a head last month, when PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński demanded that all the party’s lawmakers sign a pledge of loyalty and commit to leave any political associations they are part of. Morawiecki and his allies refused to do so, prompting Kaczyński to declare that meant they had effectively resigned from the party. Last week, Development Plus announced it had formed its own separate parliamentary caucus with 40 MPs in the Sejm, the most powerful lower house of parliament. The move immediately made it the third-largest group in the parliament, while also meaning PiS was no longer the biggest. Former Polish PM @MorawieckiM says 41 lawmakers aligned with him will form their own parliamentary caucus, deepening a split in conservative opposition party @pisorgpl. World.title: Pole becomes first person to swim 160km Baltic Sea route between Sweden and Poland
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Polish swimmer Bartłomiej Kubkowski has become the first person in history to swim across the Baltic Sea between Sweden and Poland, covering a distance of just over 160 kilometres (99 miles). On Sunday evening, an exhausted Kubkowski clambered onto the beach in the town of Dziwnów on Poland’s northern Baltic coast, around 56 hours after he had set off from Kaseberga in Sweden on Friday. The achievement marks a personal triumph for Kubkowski, for whom this was the fifth attempt to complete the route. His effort this year has raised over 715,000 zloty (€166,000) for children’s cancer treatment so far, with donations to his fundraiser still coming in. View this post on Instagram A post shared by PURELY ATHLETICS (@purelyathletics) During the crossing, Kubkowski was unable to sleep and, although a support boat accompanied him and provided food and drink, he was not allowed to touch the vessel itself. His journey of around 160km was not far off the longest-ever continuous, unassisted open-water swim ratified by the Marathon Swimmers Federation, which was the 168.3 km swum by American Sarah Thomas in 2017 in Lake Champlain, between the US states of New York and Vermont. Kubkowski has been attempting to swim the route between Sweden and Poland since 2022, getting progressively closer to achieving the goal. Last year, he came within 11km of the Polish coast before extreme exhaustion and deteriorating weather forced him to give up, reported Eurosport. However, Kubkowski, a former competitive swimmer who now devotes himself to ultraswimming, did last year manage to break the world record for the longest distance swum in a swimming pool over 24 hours, after he managed to cover 103.6 km (64.5 miles). Another Polish swimmer, Karolina Szczepaniak, is also currently attempting to swim from Sweden to Poland along a slightly different route to Kubkowski’s. At the time of writing, she is around 110km into the 172km journey, and has raised almost 400,000 zloty for charity. Szczepaniak, a former Olympic swimmer, also attempted the feat last year, but was forced to give up after 57 hours amid worsening weather. However, the 146.7km she swam set a new record for the longest distance covered by a female swimmer in the Baltic Sea and a Polish record for open-water swimming by a woman. A Canadian multinational operator of convenience stores, Alimentation Couche-Tard, has announced plans to acquire Poland’s Żabka Group, which runs Europe’s largest chain of convenience stores. The company has offered 32 zloty per share, valuing Żabka at 32.6 billion zloty (€7.56 billion). Żabka’s main shareholders have agreed to sell their stakes, with final approval still required from stock market investors. If the transaction is completed, Żabka is likely to be delisted from the Warsaw Stock Exchange just two years after its market debut. Właściciel Circle K chce przejąć 100% Żabki. Alimentation Couche-Tard has already secured commitments to acquire at least 57.2% of the company. Heket, an entity linked to CVC Capital Partners owning 37.6% of Żabka’s shares, and PG Investment Company, holding 10%, have agreed to sell their entire stakes. A group of major individual shareholders, together controlling 9.6% of Żabka’s shares, has also agreed to sell its holdings to the Canadian buyer. The investors include members of the company’s management and former executives. They have also agreed to reinvest part of the proceeds from the sale into Alimentation Couche-Tard shares. The tender offer for the remaining shares was announced on Friday by Ipopema Securities, which is acting as the intermediary in the transaction. Alimentation Couche-Tard and Żabka expect subscriptions for the offer to open around 26 August, following a review of the tender document by the Polish Financial Supervision Authority (KNF). The companies foresee the transaction closing by the end of the year. The Canadian company expects Żabka to continue operating independently, under the leadership of its current management team, and to retain its brand. Żabka shares jumped after the announcement, rising from 29.26 zloty to around 31.60 zloty on Friday afternoon, an increase of about 8%. World.title: “Ivan, Go Home!” Rally to Take Place Outside Russian Embassy in Prague
World.content:
A Czech-Ukrainian rally will take place outside the Russian Embassy in Prague on August 20 to mark the 58th anniversary of the Soviet-led invasion of Czechoslovakia.

The event, titled “Ivan, Go Home!”, is scheduled to begin at 6 p.m. on Thursday, August 20, at Boris Němcova Square in Prague 6.

The rally comes one day before the anniversary of the night of August 20-21, 1968, when troops from five Warsaw Pact countries entered Czechoslovakia to crush the Prague Spring reform movement.



The invasion brought an end to the country’s attempt to pursue a more liberal form of socialism and was followed by two decades of political repression and Soviet military presence.

The event is being organized jointly by People in Need (Člověk v tísni), Memory of the People (Paměť národa), Million Moments for Democracy (Milion chvilek pro demokracii), and the European Congress of Ukrainians.

Organizers say the rally will connect the historical experience of the Soviet occupation with Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine.

Participants will gather to remember those killed or persecuted following the 1968 invasion and the people who lived under the communist regime that followed. The organizers also plan to express support for Ukraine and draw attention to what they describe as the continuing use of imperial violence by Russia.

The choice of the rally’s name refers to one of the best-known slogans associated with the 1968 invasion. “Ivan, go home!” appeared on posters, walls, buildings and military vehicles as Czechoslovaks protested against the foreign troops occupying the country.

The invasion halted those reforms. Soviet troops remained in Czechoslovakia until the end of the communist era, while the subsequent period of “normalization” brought censorship, political purges and restrictions on civil liberties.

World.title: World of Warcraft Film Ibelin to Shoot in Prague
World.content:
Production of Ibelin, a new film based on the life of Norwegian World of Warcraft player Mats Steen, is moving to Prague this summer.

Filming is expected to take place at Barrandov Studios from early August through early October, following the production’s spring shoot in Norway.

The film is not connected to the 2016 Hollywood movie Warcraft. Instead, it tells the real-life story of Steen, who lived with Duchenne muscular dystrophy and built friendships, relationships and a social life inside the online world of World of Warcraft.



The Prague production is reportedly seeking extras for roles including blacksmiths, guards and innkeepers. The casting suggests that parts of the film set in the game’s fictional world could be filmed in the Czech Republic. The producers have not yet officially confirmed which scenes will be shot in Prague.

Charlie Plummer leads the cast

American actor Charlie Plummer will portray Mats Steen. Toni Collette and Stephen Graham will play his parents, while the supporting cast includes Bill Nighy, Isabela Merced, Maisy Stella, John Bradley and Ivanna Sakhno.

The film will be directed by Norwegian filmmaker Morten Tyldum, whose credits include The Imitation Game and the science-fiction film Passengers.

At the center of the story is the difference between Steen’s increasingly restricted physical existence and the freedom he experienced online. His character, known in World of Warcraft as Ibelin, became an important figure to people he met through the game.

One of Norway’s largest film projects

The Prague shoot is part of an international production with a reported budget of CZK 1 billion.

According to the Norwegian Film Institute, the project received 20 million Norwegian kroner in production support.

Ibelin is being produced by Vendôme Pictures, Pathé and Neby-Tyldum as an international co-production. The Norwegian Film Institute describes it as an English-language drama with a planned running time of around two hours.

The film is being developed for theatrical release, with its premiere currently expected in the third quarter of 2027.

World.title: GALLERY: Time Capsule Buried Beneath Prague’s Wenceslas Square Tramline
World.content:
A time capsule containing different items, newspapers and messages documenting life in 2026 has been buried beneath Prague’s reconstructed Wenceslas Square.

The capsule was placed on Wednesday, August 5, near the statue of St. Wenceslas as work continues on the upper section of the square.

The Prague New Town Association, which is involved in activities around the statue and the surrounding area, organised the ceremony.

The date was not originally chosen for its historical significance. Construction work ultimately determined both the day and the location of the burial. But the association later discovered that August 5 also marks the 60th anniversary of the release of the Beatles’ Revolver album.

“We were wondering what made August 5 go down in history. Then we found out that it was 60 years ago that the Beatles released their famous album Revolver. So now we are leaving a message here for future generations,” said Monika Vlková, the association’s executive director.



The box, measuring 60 by 40 by 23.5 centimetres and weighing about eight kilograms, was then taken to a prepared pit beside the statue. Workers had excavated the hole to a depth of around 1.7 metres, where the capsule was placed before the site was covered.

The container had been wrapped in transparent protective film, as had its contents.

The collection includes coins, newspapers published during the first week of August 2026, T-shirts, badges and written messages. It also contains proposals submitted by architects during the competition for the redesign of Wenceslas Square.

The box reportedly also holds a hammer and a beer glass.

The objects are accompanied by a 20-page report describing everyday life in the Czech capital in 2026. The capsule also contains USB drives with digital material documenting the period of the Covid-19 pandemic and its effects on life in central Prague.

The capsule is intended to remain underground for decades. The association estimates that Wenceslas Square could undergo another major reconstruction in roughly 50 years, although nobody can predict when the next intervention will actually take place.

World.title: Czechia Tightens Temporary Protection Rules for Ukrainian Men Aged 23 to 60
World.content:
New rules affecting Ukrainian men seeking temporary protection in the Czech Republic will take effect on August 5, 2026.

Under the changes, men aged 23 to 60 applying for temporary protection will have to demonstrate that they are exempt from military service in Ukraine.

The requirement will apply to new applications and certain other applications for protection, but not to people who already hold valid temporary protection.



The Czech Interior Ministry says the new rules follow an EU Council decision published in the Official Journal of the European Union on August 4. The decision also extends temporary protection for people fleeing Russia’s war in Ukraine until March 31, 2028.

For applicants aged 23 to 60, military registration documents will be checked as part of the application process. Applicants will use Ukraine’s Reserv+ system to demonstrate their military status, with the electronic military registration document showing whether they are exempt from military service.

The rules are different for younger applicants. People aged 18 to 22 will only need to demonstrate that they are registered in the Reserv+ system.

The new requirement concerns people applying for temporary protection for the first time, as well as repeat applications and applications connected with family reunification. It does not apply to people who already have valid temporary protection.

The military-service requirement will also not be introduced as part of the regular extension process. Ukrainians whose temporary protection is already valid will therefore not have to provide this additional documentation when extending their status through March 2028.

Interior Minister Lubomír Metnar said the Czech government had pushed for stricter conditions for new applicants. According to the ministry, the change is expected to reduce the number of new arrivals and ease pressure on public services, including health care and social security.

World.title: Filming of American Spy Series to Bring Restrictions to Prague 7
World.content:
Filming for the American series Birdwatcher will take place at the Prague 7 tax office on Kapitána Jaroše Embankment from August 8 to 24, bringing temporary restrictions to the area.

The production will use the tax office building at Kapitána Jaroše Embankment 1000/7, while part of the sidewalk outside the building will be closed to accommodate filming equipment.

The restrictions will not affect the normal operation of the tax office.



Drivers should also expect temporary parking restrictions on nearby Na Ovčinách Street. Vehicles will still be allowed to pass through the street, but parking will be prohibited during the designated filming periods.

The restrictions will not be in force continuously throughout the filming period. They will apply only on specific dates, with Prague 7 publishing a map showing the affected areas and individual dates on its website.

Prague has become a major filming location

Birdwatcher is an American spy fantasy series set during the Cold War. The production is being led by Legendary and Apple TV, with Andy Goddard directing. Wyatt Russell plays the lead role.

The story follows Colonel Lee Shaw as he embarks on a covert mission behind enemy lines to prevent the Soviet Union from unleashing a new Titan capable of devastating the United States and altering the balance of the Cold War.

The series is set in the 20th century against the backdrop of the Cold War, and parts of the production are being filmed in Prague.

Czech production company Stillking Films is handling the local production. The company has previously worked on major international productions filmed in the Czech capital, including The Gray Man.

World.title: Seven Prague Rooftops to Visit Before Summer Ends
World.content:
Summer is already moving on, and Prague’s rooftop season won’t last much longer.

August is the time to make the most of the city’s terraces, sunset views and outdoor events before they disappear for another year.

Here are seven rooftops and terraces worth visiting before autumn arrives.



1. REASON at Masaryčka

Eleven floors above Masaryk Station, REASON offers one of Prague’s newest rooftop dining spots, with views over the city and the Zaha Hadid-designed Masaryčka development.

This summer, its terrace is also home to the seasonal Frerejean Frères Champagne Bar, serving champagne by the glass, cocktails, oysters and light bites. The menu includes THE REASON KIR, made with herbs grown on the rooftop.

This summer: Champagne, oysters and cocktails above Masaryčka.

2. W Prague – ABOVE Rooftop

ABOVE Rooftop at W Prague brings a Mediterranean feel to the top of Wenceslas Square.

The daily Mediterranean Hour runs from 5 to 6 PM, with two spritzes and a Taste of the Mediterranean platter for CZK 990. Oysters are also served from Thursday to Saturday, alongside a programme of summer events and pop-ups.

This summer: Mediterranean Hour, sunset drinks and oysters in the centre.

3. MINUTY Rooftop Terrace

The rooftop at Fairmont Golden Prague offers views across Pařížská, Letná and the city centre from nine floors up.

MINUTY Rooftop Terrace by Golden Eye focuses on champagne, oysters, caviar and cocktails. The terrace is seasonal and is expected to remain open until September, weather permitting.

This summer: Champagne, oysters and caviar with a view.

4. Sky Lounge 360°

For the view alone, Sky Lounge 360° is hard to beat. The rooftop looks across Prague’s historic centre and becomes livelier during the summer months, with DJs, sunset events and Prague Rooftop Festival activities.

It is more about drinks and atmosphere than a long dinner — a good option for an evening that starts at sunset and continues after dark.

This summer: Sunset events, DJs and panoramic views.

5. The Cloud One Rooftop

The Cloud One Prague on Hybernská has its own rooftop cocktail bar overlooking the Masaryčka area.

The relaxed terrace works well for an after-work drink, while summer events bring DJs and a livelier atmosphere at sunset. It has also joined the Prague Rooftop Festival programme.

And if you want to make a night of it, REASON is just a short walk away.

This summer: Cocktails, sunset events and views of Masaryčka.

6. Casablanca Sky Bar

On the sixth floor of The President Hotel, Casablanca Sky Bar looks out over the Vltava and Prague skyline.

With DJs, cocktails and regular sunset events, it has more of a party atmosphere than a traditional hotel rooftop. It is also one of the venues taking part in the Prague Rooftop Festival.

This summer: DJs, cocktails and sunset parties above the Vltava.

7. Monkey Bar

Monkey Bar at Falkensteiner Hotel Prague is a quieter alternative, with a green, jungle-style terrace close to the main railway station.

Every Thursday until the end of August, the terrace hosts BBQ & Beats, combining barbecue, live music and summer drinks. Frozen margaritas are also on the menu.

For daytime plans, there is Jungle Brunch, including a bottomless mimosa option.

This summer: BBQ & Beats every Thursday through August.

World.title: Prague Kettlebell Brand Železná Koule Opens 600-Square-Metre Gym in Karlín
World.content:
Czech kettlebell training brand Železná koule has opened its largest location yet at Danube House in Prague’s Karlín district.

The new 600-square-metre gym expands the brand’s presence in Prague and comes ahead of the next edition of its flagship Amazing 12 fitness programme.

Železná koule has built a community around kettlebell training and coached workouts rather than the traditional self-service gym model. The company says more than 20,000 people have trained through its programmes since its launch.

At its Karlín location, members train under the guidance of coaches in small groups. The approach is designed to provide more personal instruction and a structured training environment, rather than simply giving members access to gym equipment.



The new location is also the latest venue for the company’s Amazing 12 programme, a 12-week fitness and body transformation course that combines regular training with nutrition guidance and ongoing support.

What is the Amazing 12 programme?

The programme is aimed at both people who are new to structured strength training and more experienced gym-goers looking for a more organised approach to their workouts.

Although the programme itself lasts 12 weeks, participants first complete a preparation week, making 13 weeks in total. During the programme, they take part in 64 training sessions, with one-hour workouts held every weekday under the supervision of a coach.

Groups are limited to a maximum of five participants, allowing coaches to work closely with each person throughout the programme.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Železná koule (@zelezna_koule)

The programme is designed to provide a structured routine covering exercise, nutrition and recovery, with progress tracked throughout the 12 weeks.

The next Amazing 12 programme starts on August 31, 2026, with places available at the new Karlín location as well as Železná koule gyms in Smíchov and Strašnice.

The Karlín opening is part of the continued expansion of a Czech fitness brand that has developed a following around kettlebell-based training and small-group coaching. For people unfamiliar with the name, Železná kloule roughly translates from Czech as “iron ball,” referring to the kettlebell at the centre of its training approach.

More information about the Amazing 12 programme, including registration, is available at amazing12.cz.

World.title: A New Bus Line to Prague Airport Could Launch This Autumn
World.content:
A new private bus service could soon connect Prague’s main railway station directly with Václav Havel Airport, offering passengers another option for getting between the city center and the airport.

Transport company Dinarica is planning to launch the service at the end of October. The route would run between the main railway station and the airport, providing a direct alternative to the Airport Express operated by České dráhy.

The company says it wants to address one of the main practical problems passengers face when travelling by bus to the airport — luggage storage.

Dinarica plans to use Setra and MAN buses equipped with air conditioning, seat belts and more spacious seating. Each vehicle will accommodate between 70 and 90 passengers.



The planned service would operate from morning until evening, with buses running approximately every two hours.

A one-way ticket is expected to cost around CZK 125, making the service considerably cheaper than the Airport Express. Its fare is set to rise to CZK 200 following the latest price increase.

Prague’s public transport system already offers cheaper ways to reach the airport. Trolleybus 59 and bus 100 connect Václav Havel Airport with the Prague public transport network, but neither provides a direct connection to the main railway station.

Both services are primarily designed as part of the regular city transport system.

If approved and launched as planned, the Dinarica service would give passengers another direct option between Prague’s main railway station and the airport, with a lower fare than the Airport Express.

World.title: Water levels start to rise: Paks NPP may escape complete shutdown – latest water and energy crisis updates
World.content:
Water levels on the Danube are up 9cm from lows on Sunday, and rain is expected in areas of Austria that feed into the river, Prime Minister Péter Magyar said in a post on Facebook early Thursday.

Magyar said the last one of eight turbines at the Paks nuclear power plant continued to operate. He urged industrial and household consumers to continue to scale back their electricity consumption. Output of the Paks NPP, which accounts for about half of domestic electricity generation, has gradually been ramped down as water levels on the Danube, used to cool the plant, reached record lows.

Good new concerning the Paks NPP: water level rises by 4cm at Paks in 24 hours

The Danube at Paks rose by four centimetres over the past 24 hours, with the upward trend continuing, according to a report on the heat alert published by the Hungarian government on Thursday morning on kormany.hu.

The Danube at Paks a couple of days ago. Photo: MTI

The report said hydrological data showed that the river stood at -134cm at 7am on Wednesday. The water temperature at the Paks monitoring station was 27.9C.

To ensure the safe operation of the Paks nuclear power plant, 16 pumps are stationed at the pumping facilities, with a further four in the harbour and 11 held in reserve on the riverbank, officials said.

Domestic power plants generating electricity, imports ensured – minister

Domestic power plants are generating electricity, and electricity imports are ensured, Economy and Energy Minister István Kapitány said in a post on Facebook early Thursday. Kapitany also urged industrial and household consumers to continue to scale back their electricity consumption.

World.title: Schumacher family set to grow as Vivien Keszthelyi shares sweet baby news
World.content:
Vivien Keszthelyi, the 25-year-old wife of David Schumacher, is expecting a baby. The Hungarian racing driver married the son of Ralf Schumacher — and nephew of Michael Schumacher — in February this year.

A new milestone in the youngest Schumacher family: Vivien Keszthelyi to become a mother

The image, posted on social media, shows the couple embracing and kissing in a mirror against a picturesque mountain backdrop. Pink lettering spelling “Baby” has been placed on the mirror, alongside a teddy bear and a tiny pair of children’s shoes.

While the post is romantic, it also appears to hint at the baby’s sex: the shoes are pink, suggesting the couple may be expecting a girl.

The pair also shared a touching message alongside the announcement, saying that their love had made them a couple and that a new life will soon emerge from the life they have built together. The post suggests the baby’s arrival is the next major step in their relationship after their February wedding, Blikk wrote.

Racing dynasties

David Schumacher is well known in motorsport circles. The young driver is the son of former Formula 1 racer Ralf Schumacher and the nephew of seven-time world champion Michael Schumacher. Keszthelyi is also a racing driver, and their shared passion brought them together early in the relationship.

The couple reportedly met around eight years ago, when Vivien was 18 and David 17. They kept their relationship largely out of the spotlight, becoming engaged last November before marrying in Salzburg in February, in the company of close family and friends.

Vivien Keszthelyi, David, and Ralf Schumacher at a birthday party. Photo: Instagram/vivienschumacher_official

Family tensions

The wedding was not entirely free of family drama. David’s mother, Cora Schumacher, was not invited to the ceremony and learned of the marriage through press reports. Despite that, she wished her son and his Hungarian bride well, though she told German newspapers she was stunned not to have been invited.

If you missed: Budapest film shoot rules could be tightened over Schwarzenegger and Sharon Stone disruption

The relationship between Ralf and Cora has long been stormy, marked by bitter rows and a messy divorce. David has said his mother even threatened him during that period. Cora later formally gave up custody of David, allowing him to remain with his father in Salzburg. For that reason, and for others, he has said he does not want any contact with his mother and would prefer to keep her away from his new family.

Ralf Schumacher came out in 2024 and later married his partner in Saint-Tropez, France, after what he said had already been a stable relationship for some time. Michael Schumacher’s exact state of health remains a closely guarded family secret, with no official medical update available, though reports suggest he is no longer completely bedridden.

World.title: Hungary’s largest, more than 100-year-old paddle steamer, Szőke Tisza, catches fire – photos
World.content:
Firefighters have brought under control a blaze at the wreck of the Szőke Tisza, the largest paddle steamer ever built in Hungary, in Szeged on Wednesday afternoon, the Csongrád-Csanád County Disaster Management Directorate said.

Szőke Tisza in fire

Krisztina Molnár said undergrowth caught fire near Kőrös sor, in the Tápéi Bay area of Szeged. The flames then spread to the remains of the Szőke Tisza steamship, which had been placed there.

Facebook/BM OKF

Sixteen firefighters from Szeged and Hódmezővásárhely were sent to the scene, where they used several jets of water and hand tools to tackle the vegetation and the lower deck of the vessel. The blaze affected around 500 square metres and part of the ship, she said. Firefighters are continuing to cool the hull and monitor the wreck.

At the scene, firefighters from four units were still spraying the wreck with a jet of water from an aerial ladder appliance on Wednesday afternoon, while vegetation over a wider area around the wreck had been completely burnt off, MTI’s reporter observed.

Facebook/BM OKF

The boat served almost a century

The Szőke Tisza was built in 1917 at the Ganz shipyard in Újpest. The more than 77-metre-long, twin-funnel paddle steamer was originally named IV. Károly. Following the collapse of the Habsburg Monarchy, it was renamed Sas, and in 1930 became Szent Imre. During the Second World War it was taken to Austria and only returned to Hungary in 1947.

If you missed: Budapest Danube boat carrying 85 passengers nearly sinks in city centre — video

It was renamed Felszabadulás in 1950, then refurbished and converted into a pleasure cruiser in 1957-58. It was withdrawn from service in 1976 and subsequently used as a floating vessel in Budapest. Two years later it was moved to Szeged, where it operated as a restaurant and later as a disco boat in the 1980s. The badly deteriorated vessel was towed to Tápéi Bay in 2000, where it sank in 2012.

The remains of the country’s largest river paddle steamer came into the ownership of the Hajózásért Foundation in December 2017. The foundation was set up specifically to save the Szőke Tisza by Mihály Varga, founder of the KÉSZ Group, and Csaba Portás, a shipping specialist who had been committed to the cause for years. The wreck was raised in 2020.

World.title: Hungary among the top 5 countries for expat career opportunities!
World.content:
Hungary was named the 5th best country for expat career opportunities in 2026, based on a new survey by insurance specialists William Russell.

The research comes from the international health insurance specialists William Russell, who analysed factors such as foreign-born employment rates, to reveal the countries with the most migrant employees.

The countries with the highest migrant employment rates:

Rank Countries Foreign-Born Employment Rate 1 Iceland 84.2% 2 New Zealand 82.3% 3 Czech Republic 79.5% 4 Slovakia 78.5% 5 Hungary 77.9% 6 Australia 77.5% 7 Switzerland 77.1% 8 Ireland 77.0% 9 Chile 76.5% 9 Portugal 76.5%

Iceland has the highest employment rate for expat workers, with 84.2% of foreign-born residents in work. The country’s strong labour market and high levels of workforce integration mean expats are more likely to secure employment quickly and settle into stable careers.

New Zealand ranks second, with 82.3% of expat workers in employment. Strong demand for skilled workers, combined with a resilient jobs market, continues to make it one of the most attractive destinations for people relocating overseas.

The Czech Republic takes third place, where 79.5% of expats are employed. A growing economy and expanding employment opportunities have helped the country become an increasingly attractive destination for international professionals looking to build their careers abroad.

Hungary is one of the best choices for expats. Source: canva.com

Further Study Insights:

Iceland ranks as the most welcoming country, offering one of the strongest environments globally for expat integration.

Japan ranks as the least welcoming country overall, offering one of the most challenging environments for expat integration.

Zurich was named as the friendliest city, with a score of 9.06/10, combining high safety (76.7) with low social friction (24.9).

William Cooper, Director at William Russell, adds:

“One of the biggest mistakes expats make is assuming that popular countries guarantee an easy transition. In reality, the first few months are when most challenges arise, such as navigating healthcare systems and securing a stable income. Preparing for those early stages is often more important than the choice of destination.”

World.title: Several heat records broken in Hungary again, good news about drinking water supply
World.content:
Several heat records were broken on Wednesday, the weather service HugaroMet said on its website.

The record for the highest minimum temperature ever recorded was broken on Janos Hill in Budapest, where the air cooled to just 28 degrees Celsius by morning. This figure also marks a new record for the highest daily minimum temperature in the capital and across the country. The new national record for the highest daily maximum temperature was recorded in Budakalász, near Budapest, where it reached 41.4 C, whilst the capital’s highest daily maximum, 41.1 C, was recorded in Újpest, MTI wrote.

Lake Tisza also struggling. Photo: Facebook/Közép Tisza vidéki Vízügyi Igazgatóság – Kötivizig

Hungary’s drinking water supply is secure

Hungary’s drinking water supply is completely secure, and there is no strategic water shortage in the country, government spokesperson Anita Köböl said in a video posted on the government’s Facebook page on Wednesday. She noted that misunderstandings about drinking water supplies have emerged in recent days. The spokesperson said she understood the concerns, as many people have seen reports of temporary drops in water pressure or the appearance of water tankers.

Extreme drought in Budapest. Photo: Anadolu/Németi Róbert

Supplies are adequate and water has not run out, she said, adding that temporary disruptions are due to increased consumption during the heatwave, which empties reservoirs faster, while water treatment facilities have limited capacity. Water tankers are a safety guarantee and part of protocol: if a settlement experiences a pipe burst or a temporary drop in pressure, the provider immediately arranges a replacement supply, she said.

If you missed – A parched Danube: should Budapest worry about its water supply? Expert highlights a surprising fact

Restrictions serve to protect drinking water, Köböl said, emphasising that this is best supported by everyone paying attention to their own consumption. She advised people not to use drinking water for gardening, car washing, or filling swimming pools, and to avoid unnecessary water use, preferring showers over baths. Tap water in Hungary is of good quality, safe, and available, she said. The government asked everyone not to believe unfounded rumours, and said there is no need to rush to shops, as “the purest source is still in all our homes, in our own taps.“

World.title: Majka, a rapper critical of Orbán, received murder threats from Transylvanian Hungarian: historic decision made

Addressing people in Sepsiszentgyörgy, Majka said that at 11 PM on Tuesday evening he received a death threat on his private phone number.

Majka pulls out: ‘They apparently know everything about us’

They also say they know where we are staying, which security company is working at the event, and what route we will take with the band. Lawyer says threat must be taken seriously

He added that although he was used to abuse and to people occasionally being irritated by what he says, being harassed in the middle of the night on his private number was another matter entirely.

His lawyer advised him to take the threat seriously, he said, adding that they will file a police report and try to discover who was behind the apparent attempt to cause trouble.

He said they could not go ahead with the concert, the trip, or the two days they had planned to spend there until the matter was clarified. If the situation is resolved, they will make it up to the audience.

According to the SIC Feszt schedule, Majka had been due to appear on the main stage at 10 PM on Wednesday.

First such cancellation ever

World.title: Hungary AI readiness ranks among global leaders, tops public adoption
World.content:
Hungary has emerged as one of the world’s most AI-ready outsourcing destinations, placing fourth in a new international ranking and achieving the highest population-level artificial intelligence adoption score among all 25 countries examined.

The 2026 Global Outsourcing AI Readiness Index gave Hungary an overall score of 69.1 out of 100. This placed the country behind only India, Brazil and Malaysia, while narrowly ahead of the Philippines, Chile and Czechia.

The result makes Hungary the highest-ranked country in Central and Eastern Europe, underlining its growing potential as a destination for technology-supported business services and outsourced work.

Hungary AI readiness stands out in everyday adoption

Hungary’s strongest result came in the population AI adoption category, where it received 86 points – the highest score among the 25 outsourcing destinations included in the study.

The country finished ahead of Bulgaria, which scored 82 points, as well as Brazil with 79 and India with 78.

According to the 2026 Global Outsourcing AI Readiness Index, the population adoption category assesses how widely AI tools have entered the daily lives of working-age residents. It considers current use, the pace of adoption and whether infrastructure such as internet access, electricity and smartphones can support further growth.

The result does not mean that 86 per cent of Hungary’s population necessarily uses AI. The figure is a comparative index score showing that Hungary performs close to the top of the selected group across the indicators examined.

Nevertheless, the ranking suggests that Hungarians are highly open to using generative AI and other artificial intelligence tools in everyday life.

Hungary leads Central and Eastern Europe

Hungary also outperformed every other Central and Eastern European country included in the ranking.

Czechia placed seventh globally with 66.9 points, followed by Bulgaria in ninth place with 62.8. Poland finished 11th with 61.2 points, while Romania ranked 13th with 59.4.

For international readers, Hungary already plays an important role in the regional business services sector. Budapest and several major university cities host shared service centres, software development teams and multilingual corporate operations serving customers across Europe and beyond.

A high level of public familiarity with AI could make it easier for Hungarian employees and companies to introduce AI-supported workflows, particularly in administration, customer service, finance, information technology and digital marketing.

If you missed it: Giant AI data centre platform planned near Paks, GLOBWISE wins mandate, targeting 2028 – visuals

Businesses are also embracing artificial intelligence

Hungary received 67 points for enterprise AI adoption, placing seventh among the 25 destinations. The category measures whether companies have moved beyond testing AI and begun integrating the technology into their regular operations.

Hungary ranked behind India, Brazil, Malaysia, Czechia, Chile and the Philippines in this area, but remained well above most countries examined.

The figures indicate that Hungarian businesses are adopting AI at a relatively rapid pace, although corporate implementation has not yet reached the same level as public enthusiasm.

Hungary’s workforce AI literacy score was lower, at 54 points, resulting in 15th place in that category. Workforce literacy covers factors such as the concentration of AI specialists, the strength of the developer community and the availability of professional AI skills.

The 32-point difference between population adoption and workforce literacy was the largest among the six highest-ranked countries. Rather than diminishing Hungary’s achievement, the gap highlights an opportunity: public interest in AI could provide a strong foundation for professional training, workplace development and education programmes.

A promising position in the AI-driven economy

The index combines four areas: population AI adoption, workforce AI literacy, enterprise adoption and the AI education pipeline. These categories account for 30, 30, 25 and 15 per cent of the final score respectively.

The authors stress that the ranking is a snapshot rather than a prediction, and that it focuses specifically on countries competing for outsourced work. Scores are relative to the group examined and should not be interpreted as absolute measures of national technological development.

Even with those limitations, Hungary’s fourth-place finish represents an encouraging result. Its strong public adoption score indicates that AI is already becoming familiar to many people, while its regional leadership could strengthen the country’s appeal to international companies.

World.title: Hungary’s MÁV is slowing trains and protecting tracks from the heat with paint
World.content:
MÁV is slowing trains and protecting tracks from the heat with paint, Transport and Investment Minister Dávid Vitézy said in a Facebook post on Wednesday.

He said that extreme heat also places a severe strain on the railway network and, in extreme cases, can even cause rail breaks, the Hungarian news agency wrote.

According to experts, the temperature of a rail exposed to blazing sun can be as much as 20 degrees higher than the air temperature, he wrote, adding that MÁV orders enhanced track inspections when rail temperatures exceed 45C, while also paying close attention to the technical condition of rolling stock.

He said that from Saturday the railway company introduced speed restrictions across 282 track-kilometres, on 73 kilometres continuously and on a further 209 kilometres during the hottest hours only.

Extreme heat may damage not only the rail tracks but also railway infrastructure. Photo: Facebook/MÁV-csoport

He added that work is under way on lasting solutions. The use of heat-reflective white paint on the Pécs railway line has produced encouraging results, with measurements showing that it reduced rail temperatures by 3C to 7C. In addition, cabinets housing level-crossing equipment are being fitted with a special coating to reduce warming caused by sunlight.
