World.title: Hundreds of passenger and luxury cars registered as vans in Estonia
World.content:
As of July 1 this year, 19 Porsche Cayennes, BMW X5s and X6s, and various Land Rover models were registered in Estonia as vans to save on taxes, Eesti Ekspress reported.

The weekly writes that one common tactic is temporarily converting passenger cars into vans by removing the rear seats and installing a partition for inspection, then restoring the original interior after registration.

Transport Administration data shows hundreds of ordinary passenger models, including Škoda Octavias, Toyota Land Cruisers, Audi Q7s and Porsche Cayennes, are registered as vans.

Another scheme exploits tax breaks for eight- and nine-seat minibuses by registering vehicles with extra seats that may later be removed, significantly lowering the registration fee.

Some buyers also avoid paying the registration tax by leaving the previous owner listed in the vehicle register while becoming only the primary user, although the annual vehicle tax still remains the owner's responsibility.

Authorities have also observed owners reweighing vans and pickups to adjust their power-to-weight ratio and qualify for lower tax rates. In some cases, heavier versions of the same vehicle, equipped with more options, can incur substantially lower registration taxes because of the way the tax thresholds are structured.

Used car seller Mobile Autokeskus manager Silver Havamaa argues these examples show the tax system contains rigid thresholds and loopholes that encourage optimization rather than reflecting real vehicle use. He also contends that powerful plug-in hybrids receive disproportionately low registration taxes because the tax formula heavily favors their official CO₂ emissions.

The Ministry of Finance maintains that emphasizing CO₂ emissions in the tax calculation is intended to encourage the purchase of more environmentally friendly vehicles.

World.title: Estonia and Sweden set rules for holding Swedish prisoners in Tartu
World.content:
A newly signed memorandum lays out everything from clothing and access to television to electricity use and nicotine products, defining how Swedish inmates will live inside Tartu Prison.

The first couple of dozen Swedish prisoners will arrive in Tartu in mid‑August. The exact day will not be disclosed for security reasons, and the public will learn about it only once the prisoners are in their cells. Tartu Prison, which has undergone a refresh renovation, will offer access to Swedish TV channels, but the prisoners will be subject to the Estonian legal system. The rules were clarified in the cooperation memorandum signed on Wednesday.

"We are solving the issue of the Tartu prison standing empty — while being very modern at the same time. Secondly, it is very important for Estonia that we have trained personnel working in the field of internal security. We will train them further at the expense of Swedish taxpayers," said Minister of Justice Liisa Pakosta.

A Swedish prisoner cannot choose whether they serve their sentence in Estonia. But many have shown interest in the possibility.

Niklas Bellström. Source: Iris Tähema/ERR

"My impression is that it is adventurous. It is a historic thing, even for the prisoners," said Niklas Bellström, head of a unit at the Swedish Prison and Probation Service.

In Tartu, prisoners will have access to a gym and can play basketball and football. Swedish prisons generally do not offer such opportunities, but they will have to give up smoking and the popular Swedish snus. As a compromise, the prison's e‑shop will allow weaker nicotine pouches and patches.

"After long and very intense discussions, we finally agreed that nicotine pouches containing synthetic nicotine may be used in the prison. Prisoners will buy them themselves," Pakosta said.

The concession made for Swedes will be extended to Estonian prisoners by end of November at the latest. Cigarettes will remain banned. The biggest concern among Tartu residents is who will come to visit the Swedish prisoners. Each prisoner is guaranteed at least one one‑ to two‑hour visit per month and, once every six months, a longer visit lasting from 24 hours up to three days.

All visits take place on prison grounds, but friends cannot simply show up at the door. Every visitor must apply for permission, and the prison service will check their background. If a visitor may pose a security risk, permission will not be granted.

Liisa Pakosta. Source: Iris Tähema/ERR

"In reality, visitors come to about every fifth prisoner, and usually it is a crying mother. We have a very modern prison where inmates have tablets and can hold video meetings," Pakosta said.

Estonia may choose which prisoners it accepts. Terrorists, leaders of organized crime, women and minors will not be taken. No Swedish prisoner will receive city leave, and before release they will be transferred back to Sweden. The average stay in Estonia will be nine months. By the end of the year, there may be 200 Swedish prisoners in Tartu, and next year up to 600.

"Tartu Prison has not caused any concerns for Tartu residents that would undermine their sense of security, and we intend to keep it that way," said Rait Kuuse, head of the prison service.

Isamaa leader Urmas Reinsalu has promised to terminate the prison‑rental agreement if he comes to power. It cannot be done overnight. Sweden must be notified a year in advance.

"In the event of terminating the agreement, we have 12 months to plan the implementation of that decision," Bellström said.

World.title: Eesti 200 head: 67 MPs back Ülle Madise for president
World.content:
Potential presidential candidate Ülle Madise currently has the backing of 67 members of the Riigikogu, Eesti 200 chair Kristina Kallas said Thursday.

"Our three parties together account for 63 votes, because Zuzu Izmailova has said she will not support her, and as far as I know there are three independent MPs. That makes 67 votes," Kallas said when asked how much support Madise currently has.

A presidential candidate needs at least 68 votes to be elected in the Riigikogu.

Madise has been endorsed by the governing Reform Party, which has 37 MPs, along with two independent lawmakers. Eesti 200 has 13 MPs, while the opposition Social Democratic Party (SDE) has nine MPs, with five additional lawmakers voting alongside the party. One of those five, Izmailova, has said she will not support Madise. Based on those figures, the three parties together would have 65 votes, meaning they would still need at least three votes from independent MPs to elect the president.

Asked about the remaining shortfall, Kallas replied: "What's missing is support from Isamaa or the Center Party."

"Ülle Madise has the broadest support in the Riigikogu today, but the final outcome — whether Ülle Madise becomes the next president — now depends on the decisions of the Center Party and Isamaa," she added.

"Why they are not telling the people of Estonia what that decision is, I don't understand. I believe the statesmanlike thing to do would be to say clearly that if Ülle Madise is nominated — and there is no problem in submitting the required 21 signatures as early as tomorrow, even though the deadline is still some time away — then would Isamaa and would the Center Party support Ülle Madise? That answer is the missing piece in knowing whether Ülle Madise will become the next president," said Education and Research Minister Kallas.

Kristina Kallas. Source: Siim Lõvi / ERR

She added that she sees no reason why any party should refuse to support Madise.

"I don't see any reason, except for partisan interests ahead of the parliamentary elections — wishing to paint the government as incapable and to derail the presidential election for that purpose. Not because Ülle Madise would be unsuitable as president. Ülle Madise enjoys very strong public support in Estonia, but unfortunately, in some cases partisan interests outweigh the interests of society," she said.

According to Kallas, Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise is a highly capable, competent and widely respected public figure who is well suited to serve as president.

The Riigikogu will convene to elect the president on September 2, 2026. A presidential candidate must be nominated by at least one-fifth of the Riigikogu's members (21 MPs). Candidates must be Estonian citizens by birth who are at least 40 years old. Active-duty members of the armed forces and anyone who has already served two consecutive terms as president are ineligible. If no candidate is elected in the Riigikogu, the election will be decided by the Electoral College where MPs are joined by local government electors.

Key dates:

August 21–24: Nomination period for candidates.

September 2: First round of voting in the Riigikogu.

September 3: Second and third rounds of voting in the Riigikogu, if necessary.

World.title: Tallinn will not rebuild drainage system for cleaner Inglirand water
World.content:
Tallinn does not plan to rebuild the stormwater drainage system to clean the water at Inglirand beach. Instead, it is trying to identify illegal wastewater connections, Deputy Mayor Kristjan Järvan said.

For years, one of Tallinn's most prominent waterfront areas has been known for its unpleasant odor and polluted water.

"Naturally, we want our beaches and coastal waters to be in good condition and pleasant and safe for both residents and the ecosystem," Järvan told ERR.

"The main cause of the unpleasant smell along the shores of Tallinn Bay is algae, whose growth is fueled by the water's high nutrient content," the deputy mayor said.

"Looking at the broader picture, the vast majority of the nutrient load in Tallinn Bay comes from the Pirita River, with the sources located mainly within the river's watershed. Agriculture is responsible for the largest share of that pollution and there are no quick or easy solutions to reduce its impact," Järvan said.

In 2021, the then-head of Tallinn's Kesklinn district said he hoped Inglirand would become an official public swimming beach. The beach was revitalized following the completion of Reidi tee, when the shoreline was also renovated. However, the Health Board has repeatedly warned that swimming in the waters at Inglirand may be unsafe.

Last summer, then-Kesklinn district head Sander Andla (Reform) said the root of the problem was that several stormwater outfalls, as well as a port, are located near Inglirand.

At the time, Andla said the only solution would be to relocate the stormwater outfalls farther away. "As for the timeline, it's important to understand that this isn't the kind of job that can be completed in a week by three people. It would cost the city several million euros," Andla said.

According to Järvan, redirecting the stormwater flowing into the Inglirand area is not a realistic solution because it would require extensive reconstruction of the stormwater drainage systems in Kesklinn and Lasnamäe. "That is why the city is focusing on improving stormwater quality, including identifying illegal wastewater connections to the stormwater drainage system," Järvan said.

"To that end, the city has commissioned a study to identify possible sources of pollution. Because the watershed being examined is large, the first study was unable to identify them. The search for pollution sources will continue and additional studies will be commissioned if necessary," Järvan added.

World.title: Opera singer says the art form thrives as a social gathering place, not an elite tradition
World.content:
Estonian opera singer Mart Mikk says opera is far from fading and remains in excellent health, adding that the art form was never meant to be elitist but has always served as a place for social leisure.

Mikk spent his first summer in Savonlinna in 1988 at master classes. "There I understood very clearly that opera is in no way a fading art, but in very good health, and its address is Savonlinna," Mikk said.

The yearly Savonlinna Opera Festival is Finland's premiere cultural event. The month-long festival is held in Olavinlinna, a towering medieval castle by Finland's largest lake. First Savonlinna Opera Festival took place in 1912.

Mikk recalled that in 1992 the Savonlinna Opera Festival choir was disbanded. "The work is quite tough; rehearsal periods last seven weeks in a row. I have counted that with master classes and opera visits combined, I have spent more than a year's worth of days in Savonlinna. I have learned to know that town inside and out," Mikk said.

Former choir director Kyösti Haatanen formed a new choir, and since singing students did not have many opportunities to earn money alongside their studies, it was a good chance. "I went to the choir auditions, got in, and when it turned out there was a dire shortage of tenors, I invited three wonderful tenors from Estonia," Mikk recalled. "The workdays were very long, but people also knew how to relax."

Autor/allikas: Siim Lõvi /ERR

"Opera was never meant to be elitist; it was a place for social leisure. Italians met their guests at the opera," Mikk added.

"I must honestly admit that thanks to the roads of Eastern Finland, I rediscovered my passion for riding a motorcycle. After a long break I bought a motorcycle again, and since then it has become a major hobby alongside opera. By now I have traveled to 40 European countries on a motorcycle," Mikk noted.

According to him, there is indeed a certain charm in visiting music events by motorcycle. "Not only operas; in Estonia the entire theater landscape is very rich. I actually visit more spoken‑theater performances than musical‑theater ones," Mikk noted. "This summer I saw 'Das Rheingold,' and also 'Baskin' in Kiidjärve."

In the summer of 2027, the Estonian National Opera will travel to the Savonlinna Opera Festival as a guest performer. "Estonia was actually the first guest theater from outside Finland to appear at the Savonlinna Opera Festival," Mikk said.

World.title: Experts: Coming winter to bring sharp electricity price hikes
World.content:
Electricity prices are expected to see spikes due to natural gas prices, uncertainty over LNG supplies and the heat wave that has hit Europe, energy experts told ERR.

"I switched my country home's electricity contract to a fixed-price plan starting in October. There seem to be too many unpredictable variables in this winter's pricing mix," Timo Tatar, the former deputy secretary general for energy at the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications and now head of the Estonian operations of Lithuanian energy group Ignitis, wrote on social media recently.

Explaining his reasoning to ERR, Tatar said the region and Europe as a whole are heading into winter with several factors that have more room to push electricity prices higher than lower.

"Especially if we end up with a colder-than-average winter that is also short on wind and precipitation," he said.

One unpredictable factor is the volatility of natural gas prices following the conflict involving Iran. Compared with last year, natural gas prices in Europe are around €20 per megawatt-hour higher. Since many traders expected — and some still expect — the conflict to be resolved and prices to fall, gas storage facilities are less full than usual ahead of the autumn and winter season, Tatar said.

Gas stockpiling has also been hampered by the heat in Western and Central Europe. Low water levels have reduced the output of nuclear power plants, forcing greater reliance on gas-fired power generation.

Alexela sees the same risks, Kalvi Nõu, the company's head of energy trading, told ERR. Europe's gas storage facilities are currently below typical levels and there are also concerns about the reliability of liquefied natural gas (LNG) supplies. All of this affects natural gas prices, and when gas prices are high, part of that increase is passed on to electricity prices.

Another concern is the low water level in the Nordic hydropower reservoirs, which also kept electricity prices higher in July than a year earlier.

"If hydropower generation remains more limited, there will be less low-cost electricity available on the market," Nõu said.

Tiit Hõbejõgi, a member of Enefit's management board, also agreed with Tatar that current conditions point to greater-than-usual uncertainty this winter, citing natural gas prices, Europe's gas reserves and the low hydropower reservoir levels caused by the hot weather.

If there is one positive development compared with previous years, Nõu said, it is the growing role of energy storage. Batteries are increasingly participating in the day-ahead electricity market — the market that matters most for ordinary consumers.

Uncertainty not a guarantee of higher prices

The unpredictability of electricity and natural gas prices is built into the system, however, since prices are influenced by many factors, including the weather, which is notoriously difficult to forecast.

"Exchange prices are inherently unpredictable. That's nothing new," Tatar said. "It's just that this year, we can expect periods of particularly high price peaks because of the warning signs in global markets. That's also reflected in futures prices, which are at roughly the same level as last winter or even slightly higher."

"Electricity prices are affected by a large number of factors simultaneously, many of which cannot be forecast far in advance," Hõbejõgi said.

At the same time, it would also be premature to assume that unpredictability necessarily means higher prices.

"It's important to point out that last winter we also saw very high exchange prices for electricity and natural gas, mainly because of exceptionally cold weather. Compared with last winter, it's difficult to expect even higher heating bills," Nõu said.

Tatar said consumers have become accustomed to price volatility in recent years, so he does not expect a repeat of the public shock seen during the 2022 energy crisis.

"That said, prices could still reach uncomfortably high levels during individual hours," he added.

As an example, Tatar pointed to winter hours when electricity demand is high and there is not enough renewable generation available. If natural gas remains €20 to €30 per megawatt-hour more expensive on the European market than it was a year ago, the production cost of electricity at gas-fired power plants would rise by €40 to €60 per megawatt-hour compared with last year.

Kiisa synchronous condenser. Source: AK

Nordic electricity futures currently put Finland's electricity price for the fourth quarter of this year at about €90 per megawatt-hour, or 9 cents per kilowatt-hour.

"If Finland's average electricity price this winter does end up close to the €90 per megawatt-hour indicated by the futures market, Estonia's average winter price could be around €110 to €120 per megawatt-hour," Nõu estimated.

Tatar noted that a Finnish price of €90 per megawatt-hour would translate into fixed-price electricity offers in Estonia of roughly €140 per megawatt-hour.

"That's because the financial transmission rights (FTR) fee has to be added and there is still considerable uncertainty around that in the market. On top of that, the baseload electricity price has to be adjusted to match the customer's actual consumption profile, which also affects price expectations," he said.

While Tatar believes Finnish futures are not particularly important for forecasting prices in Estonia, Hõbejõgi said they are certainly a key indicator.

"They provide a basis for estimating prices in Estonia as well. At the same time, the margin of error is significant because Estonia's price area could ultimately end up either more expensive or cheaper depending on the availability of cross-border interconnections, regional generation and demand, local weather conditions and other factors," Hõbejõgi said.

Given the shortage of competitively priced electricity generation in the Baltic region, Estonia's electricity prices are still likely to remain higher than Finland's, he added.

Last winter, the average exchange electricity price in Estonia over the three winter months — December, January and February — was about €130 per megawatt-hour.

Gas stocks low but supply crisis not on the horizon

As noted, electricity and natural gas prices are closely linked, especially in winter, when gas-fired power plants have to operate more and their generation costs depend directly on the price of natural gas.

"The extent of that impact depends primarily on weather conditions. The colder the winter and the higher the electricity demand, the more important natural gas becomes in electricity generation," Nõu said.

Hõbejõgi said that although relatively little electricity is generated from natural gas in Estonia, gas plays such an important role in other countries that it still affects electricity prices in Estonia.

"If renewable energy generation is strong, demand remains around average and cross-border interconnections function well, electricity prices can remain moderate even when natural gas prices are high," he said.

Although Europe's gas storage facilities have not yet reached their usual levels ahead of winter, Nõu said he does not expect this winter to differ from previous ones in terms of security of supply.

Tatar also said he does not see a direct risk to natural gas supply security.

"However, if this winter turns out to be colder than average, we could certainly see sharp price spikes driven by gas-fired electricity generation," he said.

Hõbejõgi likewise said there is currently no reason to be concerned about supply security, though prices could still fluctuate significantly this winter.

"We certainly cannot rule out individual days or periods when prices change very rapidly. That's why the main thing to prepare for is price volatility, not supply security problems. There is also the possibility of isolated days with exceptionally high prices," he said.

Because of the conflict involving the U.S., Israel and Iran, Europe has been replenishing its gas storage more slowly than usual ahead of winter and estimates indicate that gas inventories in July were at their lowest level in 15 years. As of mid-July, European Union gas storage facilities were, on average, just over half full.

Natural gas. Source: Siim Lõvi /ERR

By the middle of this week, EU gas storage was 57 percent full. Levels vary by country: Germany's storage facilities were less than 50 percent full, while Italy's were more than 75 percent full.

Natural gas prices at the Dutch TTF gas exchange have fluctuated since the conflict involving Iran began. Just two weeks ago, prices surged, with natural gas climbing well above €60 per megawatt-hour. By Wednesday, the price had fallen back to €54 per megawatt-hour.

World.title: US lifts sanctions on Iraq’s Fly Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The United States has lifted Iraqi carrier Fly Baghdad from its sanctions list after deciding that the airline has made substantial operational adjustments, overturning limitations originally imposed due to suspected connections to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

Following an administrative review, the US Treasury withdrew two of the airline’s planes off the sanctions list but maintained sanctions on Basheer Abdulkadhim Alwan al-Shabbani, the company’s previously acknowledged owner.

Fly Baghdad was sanctioned in January 2024 after US officials accused it of aiding the IRGC’s Quds Force by transferring men and supplies to Iran-backed militias in Iraq, Syria, and Lebanon.

A US Treasury official told AFP that the airline had made significant changes to its business; thus, its categorization was no longer justifiable. The person emphasized that the move does not represent a shift in US policy toward Iran, the IRGC, or Tehran-backed extremist organizations.

The ruling benefits Iraq’s aviation industry, since sanctions have hampered Fly Baghdad’s access to international banking, insurance, and aircraft leasing while restricting its potential to grow abroad operations.

It also comes as Baghdad strives to enhance economic connections with Washington after a slew of large investment deals announced with US corporations in recent weeks in energy, banking, technology, and infrastructure.

While the airline has been removed off the sanctions list, the US has said that it would continue to target firms that assist Iran’s regional network of armed organizations, emphasizing that Fly Baghdad’s delisting was the consequence of operational adjustments rather than a reduction in pressure on Tehran.

For Iraq, the move is expected to boost confidence in the country’s aviation industry and potentially expand international air connectivity as the government works to boost tourism, business travel, and foreign investment.

World.title: Iraqi security delegation to visit Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein and his Saudi counterpart, Faisal bin Farhan, discussed on Wednesday arrangements for the upcoming visit of an Iraqi security delegation to Saudi Arabia.

The Iraqi Foreign Ministry mentioned that the two ministers convened in Amman, the capital of Jordan, during the Arab ministerial meeting focused on Jerusalem.

The meeting addressed the importance of enhancing ties between the two countries, issues of common interest, preparations for the upcoming Arab summit, and the security developments in the region.

The two sides also reviewed plans for the Iraqi security delegation’s future trip to Saudi Arabia, as well as mutual visits between the two countries to strengthen cooperation.

As Hussein discussed the Iraqi government’s initiatives to bring weapons under state control, Farhan conveyed Saudi Arabia’s backing for the new Iraqi government and its efforts to enhance security within the country and uphold regional stability.

The two sides reviewed security development in the region and their impact on oil export routes and energy security. They also discussed regional initiatives and potential agreements focused on the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to facilitate maritime traffic.

Both parties stressed the significance of ongoing collaboration within the Arab League framework to promote common interests and improve regional stability.

World.title: US dollar slightly rises against Iraqi dinar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Wednesday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,521.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,519.5 Iraqi dinars on Wednesday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,525 Iraqi dinars and 1,515 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,524 and 1,523.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq, Jordan, Egypt discuss cooperation mechanism, energy partnerships
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq, Jordan, and Egypt highlighted on Wednesday the importance of activating the trilateral cooperation mechanism via specialized committees and enhancing coordination in the economic, investment, industrial, and energy sectors.

Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein, Jordanian Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi, and Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty met in Amman, the capital of Jordan, to discuss the trilateral cooperation mechanism.

The meeting was held on the sidelines of the foreign ministers’ participation in the Arab ministerial meeting on Jerusalem, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Foreign Ministry.

The three parties agreed to activate the tripartite system through specialized technical committees and organize periodic discussions at various levels to monitor the progress of joint projects.

The three ministers reviewed cooperation in the energy sector, including oil and electricity interconnection projects, as well as measures to broaden partnerships in these areas to enhance economic integration and improve energy security.

The meeting addressed the latest developments in the region, particularly efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to strengthen regional stability.

The foreign ministers highlighted the need to halt military operations, reduce tensions, and adopt diplomatic means to resolve crises in the region.

World.title: Graham Arnold extends Iraq contract ahead of Gulf Cup and AFC Asian Cup 2027
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq national team head coach Graham Arnold has officially signed a contract extension with the Iraq Football Association (IFA), ensuring he will remain in charge of the Lions of Mesopotamia for the country’s upcoming major international tournaments.

The renewal secures Arnold’s position on the sidelines as Iraq prepares for the Gulf Cup and the 2027 AFC Asian Cup, providing continuity as the national team continues its long-term development.

According to a source within the Iraq Football Association, Arnold finalized the agreement on Wednesday, extending his tenure as head coach of the Iraqi national football team.

The new deal confirms that the Australian manager will oversee Iraq’s preparations and participation in the upcoming Gulf Cup before leading the team into the AFC Asian Cup 2027.

The contract extension reflects the federation’s confidence in Arnold’s leadership and its desire to maintain stability ahead of two of the region’s most important football competitions.

Keeping the same coaching staff allows Iraq to continue building tactical consistency, squad cohesion, and long-term planning without interruption.

The upcoming Gulf Cup will provide valuable competitive experience before the national team shifts its focus to the AFC Asian Cup, where Iraq will aim to compete for continental honors.

Coaching continuity is considered an important factor in international football, particularly as teams prepare for major tournaments.

By extending Arnold’s contract, the Iraq Football Association signals its commitment to maintaining the current technical project while continuing preparations for future regional and Asian competitions.

Further details regarding the duration and financial terms of the renewed agreement have not yet been officially disclosed.

World.title: Iraq, Jordan, and Egypt agree to boost trilateral cooperation
World.content:
Amman (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq, Jordan, and Egypt have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening trilateral cooperation by activating specialized technical committees and expanding coordination across key economic sectors, including investment, industry, and energy.

The agreement was reached during a trilateral ministerial meeting held in Amman, where the three countries also discussed regional developments, the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, and the importance of diplomatic efforts to reduce tensions across the Middle East.

According to a statement from Iraq’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein participated in the meeting alongside Jordanian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi and Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty.

The meeting took place ahead of the Arab ministerial meeting on Jerusalem and focused on accelerating implementation of the Iraq-Jordan-Egypt cooperation mechanism.

The ministers agreed to activate the partnership through specialized technical committees and hold regular meetings at various levels to monitor the progress of joint initiatives.

The three countries emphasized expanding cooperation in strategic sectors that support long-term economic growth.

Discussions focused on increasing collaboration in:

Economic development

Investment projects

Industrial cooperation

Trade facilitation

Infrastructure development

Officials said stronger coordination would help deepen regional economic integration while creating new opportunities for sustainable growth.

Energy cooperation was a central topic during the talks, with ministers reviewing ongoing and future projects involving:

Oil cooperation

Electricity interconnection

Regional energy security

Cross-border energy infrastructure

The three governments stressed that expanding joint energy initiatives would contribute to improving energy security and strengthening economic ties between Iraq, Jordan, and Egypt.

The ministers also exchanged views on regional developments, particularly the situation surrounding the Strait of Hormuz.

They welcomed ongoing efforts aimed at reopening the strategic waterway as quickly as possible, highlighting its importance for regional stability, international trade, and global energy markets.

The meeting concluded with a joint call for an end to military escalation across the region, emphasizing that dialogue and diplomatic engagement remain the most effective means of resolving regional crises.

The ministers reiterated their shared commitment to peaceful solutions and closer regional cooperation in addressing common political and economic challenges.

World.title: Al Qaim Cement Plant expands exports to Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Al-Qaim Cement Plant has reached its full designed production capacity of 840,000 tonnes annually, strengthening domestic cement supplies while increasing exports to neighboring Syria, the Ministry of Industry and Minerals announced on Wednesday.

The achievement marks a significant milestone in Iraq’s efforts to boost local industrial production, reduce reliance on imports, and expand the country’s non-oil exports.

According to the ministry, the Al-Qaim Cement Plant is now operating at its full design capacity, producing approximately 70,000 tonnes of sulfate-resistant cement each month.

The output is sufficient to meet demand across Anbar Province and other Iraqi governorates while supporting the government’s strategy to enhance domestic industrial self-sufficiency.

In addition to serving the local market, the plant currently exports around 7,500 tonnes of cement per month to Syria, reflecting growing cross-border trade and regional demand for Iraqi construction materials.

General Company for Iraqi Cement Director General Zuhair Dawood Ahmed said the facility is operated through a partnership with Al-Maysarah Cement Industry Company.

He explained that the plant features a fully modernized production line equipped with advanced machinery and internationally sourced equipment, alongside a modern centralized control system that manages production processes efficiently.

The factory also includes advanced laboratories for testing both raw materials and finished products, ensuring quality standards are maintained throughout the manufacturing process.

To ensure uninterrupted production, the Al-Qaim Cement Plant operates its own 30-megawatt power station, providing stable electricity independent of the national grid.

This dedicated energy supply enables the plant to maintain around-the-clock production, minimizing operational disruptions and supporting consistent output.

Officials said continuous operations are essential to meeting domestic demand while expanding Iraq’s presence in regional cement markets.

The Ministry of Industry said increasing production at state-owned industrial facilities remains a key objective in supporting economic diversification beyond the oil sector.

By achieving full operational capacity and maintaining exports, the Al-Qaim Cement Plant contributes to strengthening Iraq’s manufacturing base, creating greater industrial resilience, and expanding opportunities for Iraqi products in foreign markets.

The ministry added that efforts will continue to increase cement exports while supporting the country’s infrastructure and construction sectors through reliable local production.

World.title: Iraq lawmakers scrutinize Karbala Refinery contracts amid government anti-corruption drive
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi lawmakers have begun reviewing government contracts suspected of containing inflated costs, as Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi intensifies efforts to tighten oversight of public spending and prevent corruption before contracts are approved.

The renewed scrutiny comes a day after Al-Zaidi ordered the Federal Board of Supreme Audit to establish a specialized team responsible for conducting pre-contract financial audits within 10 working days. The initiative aims to identify high costs before agreements are finalized, marking a shift from investigating corruption after it occurs to preventing it at the contracting stage.

MP Haider Mohammed Al-Mutairi, a member of the Ishraqat Kanoun bloc, called on the prime minister to review several contracts related to the Karbala Refinery, arguing that some agreements warrant immediate investigation due to their financial burden on the state.

Al-Mutairi urged the formation of a high-level investigative committee to examine a consultancy contract involving 49 advisers, claiming it costs the Iraqi government approximately $52 million annually.

He also highlighted an operational contract for the refinery valued at $180 million per year, which he said amounts to nearly 750 million Iraqi dinars in daily expenditures.

The MP called for greater transparency in reviewing major state contracts, particularly those involving strategic infrastructure projects.

The parliamentary review follows a broader government campaign to strengthen financial oversight across ministries and state institutions.

Prime Minister Al-Zaidi directed the Federal Board of Supreme Audit to implement mandatory pre-audit procedures for government contracts, including setting financial thresholds that determine which agreements require advance scrutiny.

According to the prime minister, inflated contract values and weak oversight have long been among the primary channels through which public funds were lost.

He stressed that Iraq’s next phase of anti-corruption efforts should focus on preventing irregularities before contracts are signed rather than relying solely on post-contract investigations.

The government says the new oversight framework is intended to improve transparency, accelerate contract reviews, and safeguard public finances without delaying legitimate development projects.

The initiative forms part of a wider reform agenda aimed at enhancing accountability, improving governance, and restoring confidence in public procurement procedures.

No official findings regarding the Karbala Refinery contracts have been announced, and any investigation would be subject to the legal and auditing procedures established by Iraqi authorities.

World.title: ‘Will be a pressure group’: CJP announces nationwide 'Kya Bolti Public' campaign from September
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) said on Thursday that they will continue to function as a public pressure group instead of entering electoral politics for now, after a two-day meeting of the organisation's core team in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.

Addressing a press conference after the meeting, its founder Abijeet Dipke said CJP would focus on building a nationwide citizens' movement around issues including unemployment, education, transparency, accountability and institutional reforms. In this context, they announced a "Kya Bolti Public" campaign.

The campaign will involve CJP representatives across the country to seek people's views on the issues they face and understand what they think about the present political and social situation.

âDuring the âKya Bolti Publicâ campaign, we will get to know what people think of the present situation in the country and what the issues they face are,â he said.

"For now, CJP will be a pressure group because what India needs right now is a pressure group," he clarified.

He said the organisation's work would extend beyond education-related issues and focus on wider concerns around governance and democratic institutions.





"Whether it is the political system, the judiciary, the media, or the Election Commission, the reality is that people have lost faith in all these institutions," Dipke said.

He added that CJP wanted to build public pressure to restore accountability and neutrality in these institutions, adding that "the political system today, in my opinion, is in a very bad state".

Unemployment is another issue the organisation plans to take up nationally.

"Unemployment is a major problem, we will make it a nationwide issue," Dipke said.

He also said CJP would work on education reforms and criticised the rising cost of education. "Education has remained unaffordable since schooling. Education is used for making profits. But we want to change it," he said.

Dipke further stated that young people would be a key focus of the nationwide campaign, noting that 60 per cent of India's population is below the age of 35.

He said unemployed youngsters had also participated in CJP's protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi last month.

The organisation had led protests over the NEET paper leak and other alleged examination irregularities. Dipke described the resignation of former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan as a major outcome of the agitation. "Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation is the biggest achievement of the students' agitation," he said.

The two-day core committee meeting also focused on expanding CJP's grassroots presence across states, strengthening its organisational network and preparing for the nationwide youth outreach campaign.

Dipke rejected speculation that CJP was preparing to enter electoral politics, saying the organisation had no immediate plans to become a political party. Instead, it would seek to build a nationwide citizens' movement around transparency, accountability and institutional reforms.

World.title: 'Hemant Soren unfit to hold office': Jharkhand students on hunger strike demand CM's resignation
World.content:
We remain steadfast until the government accepts our demands, a student protestor said.

NEW DELHI: Students protesting in Jharkhand over the irregularities in the government-job recruitment process have grown livid over the state dispensation's inability to address the issue swiftly and efficiently.One of the several students on hunger strike lashed out at chief minister Hemant Soren for not visiting the protest site and called the JMM supremo "unfit to hold" the hightest office in the state, demanding his resignation.Gearing up for assembly "gherao" on August 10 in the backdrop of the ineffective redressal, a protester said: "We remain steadfast until the government accepts our demands. We now demand the chief minister's resignation, as he is unfit for the office he holds. It has been so long since he returned from Bengaluru, yet he has taken no cognisance of the situation.""My health is deteriorating. I feel dizzy if I try to stand up. I try to speak as little as possible... Various false rumours are being spread claiming that Devendra Nath Mahato called off his hunger strike... Sonam Wangchuk urged him to at least drink some water. He only drank water because his lips were parched... I want to tell everyone that Devendra Nath has not called off the strike," the same protester told news agency ANI.The competitive exam aspirants on Thursday intensified their agitation by continuing a hunger strike over alleged irregularities in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC),and JSSC CGL recruitment tests.Protesting aspirant Rahul Kranti, told ANI that despite the students' readiness for talks, the state government appears unresponsive to their demands.Kranti highlighted that the fast has entered its third day, noting that chief minister Hemant Soren has not visited the spot to inquire about the protesting students' well-being, even as a gesture of moral support."We are ready for talks. However, judging by the government's actions and what we are hearing through the media, it still does not appear to be taking a positive approach toward our demands. The government continues to say that it is investigating the matter through its own agencies. If that is the case, what is the objection to ordering a CBI inquiry?" Kranti asked.Kranti said the students on strike have grown weaker and the health has been steadily deteriorating."Initially, we wanted the government's delegation to come to the protest site. However, since there has been no positive response from the government on that front, we have decided to send our own delegation for the discussions...We have been on a hunger strike for the past three days. Our health is steadily deteriorating, and we are growing weaker with each passing day. The gherao of the Legislative Assembly is scheduled for the 10th. So far, the Honorable chief minister has not even come to inquire about our well-being, not even as a gesture of moral support," Rahul Kranti told ANI.Amid intensifying protests over alleged irregularities in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC), JSSC CGL and other recruitment examinations, agitating students today announced a "Vidhan Sabha Gherao" on August 10 if their demands are not met.Protester Radhe Kumar said the decision to gherao the assembly was taken after the government initiated contact with the agitating students.Earlier on Wednesday, CM Hemant Soren said the state government was treating allegations of irregularities in recruitment examinations with "utmost seriousness and sensitivity," assuring students that justice would be delivered within the constitutional and legal framework.Soren's remarks marked his first public response since students launched protests over alleged paper leaks and irregularities in recruitment examinations."I cannot tear open my chest to show how serious we are, but the government is taking this matter very seriously. This government has eyes, ears and sensitivity. Whatever is appropriate and in the interest of students, the state government will decide accordingly," he added.The chief minister said investigations into the allegations were under way and that the government would take a decision after receiving reports from the agencies probing the matter.

World.title: 'Convey sentiments': Rajya Sabha Chairman tells Kiren Rijiju after opposition demands Amit Shah's presence
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Parliament proceedings remained disrupted on Thursday as opposition parties continued to demand the presence of Union home minister

over the police action against student protesters at Jantar Mantar.

The Lok Sabha was also repeatedly adjourned amid the continued uproar.

Amid the repeated disruptions, Rajya Sabha Chairman C P Radhakrishnan asked Parliamentary affairs minister

to "echo the sentiments" and demand to the home minister.

As the Rajya Sabha reassembled, the Chairman attempted to take up the Question Hour, but opposition members continued sloganeering. He repeatedly urged protesting MPs to maintain order and assured them they would get an opportunity to raise their concerns.

The Chair then allowed leader of opposition

to speak. However, members of the Treasury benches objected, triggering a heated exchange between the ruling and opposition members.

Kharge reiterated the opposition's demand that Amit Shah address the House on the police action against protesters and said the opposition was ready for a discussion.

"We only raise genuine questions concerning the country and its 140 crore people.





We are asking the Home Minister and the Prime Minister to come to the House. We request the Chair to direct the Home Minister to come and give a statement. We are ready to discuss it," Kharge later posted on X.

"In this very House, Arun Jaitley ji himself said that disruption is a part of Parliamentary Democracy. You can raise any questions that is relevant to the proceedings. But here, when we are asking genuine questions, they are escaping," he added.

Responding to the demand, Rijiju said Kharge had not cited any rule while making the request and could not decide which minister should reply on behalf of the government.

"The leader of the opposition did not quote any rule, cannot give direction to the Chair, only make requests, cannot dictate. New Congress members not learning anything because their leadership not giving them a chance", Rijiju told Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge in Rajya Sabha.

Following the exchange, the Rajya Sabha Chairman directed Rijiju to convey the sentiments of the opposition to the home minister.

"Now i request you to consider his request. Kharge requested the presence of home minister in the house. You represent him. As a parliamentary affairs minister you can echo the sentiments to the home minister," the RS Chairman said.

Outside Parliament, Kharge said the Chairman had asked the Parliamentary affairs minister to ensure Amit Shah came to the House and made a statement.

"This is a simple request, and it is well within the government's control. Why they are not present is still unknown. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha told the Parliamentary affairs minister that the home minister should come to the House and speak on this incident. Rijiju alone does not have the authority to resolve the issue. He only conveys the matter, and then the issue fizzles out," Kharge said.

"When I raise a point of order, I am not allowed to speak. We want the House to run peacefully, and for that, the Home Minister should make a statement in the House.

Instead of asking students to seek forgiveness, the government should apologise to the students and their families," he added.

Asked whether the opposition would continue its protest, Kharge said the next course of action would depend on the government's response.

World.title: 'What if patients die? Can you bring them back to life?': Bombay HC orders resident doctors to call off strike
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Bombay high court on Thursday expressed concern over the impact of the Maharashtra resident doctors' strike on patients and warned the protesting doctors that it would order their salaries to be stopped if they failed to return to work immediately.

"We are concerned about the health of thousands of patients as well as the people of Maharashtra," a bench of Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad said.

Questioning the doctors' decision to strike, the bench asked, "Why are you resorting to a strike at the cost of patients? Even if your agitation succeeds tomorrow, will you be able to bring back the lives of patients who may have died during the strike? Can the protesting doctors bring the dead back to life?"

The bench, which took suo motu cognisance of the matter, also noted that the doctors had warned of suspending services in intensive care units if the deadlock with the Maharashtra government continued.

Following the high court's observations, the Maharashtra Association of Resident Doctors (MARD) and the Indian Medical Association announced that the strike would be called off.

The bench appointed senior counsel Vineet Naik and advocate Amogh Singh as amici curiae to assist the court and directed them to prepare a petition so that appropriate directions could be issued to prevent doctors from resorting to such strikes in the future.





The matter has been posted for further hearing on September 8.

MARD launched an indefinite strike on Wednesday to protest the Maharashtra government's decision to allow homoeopaths to register with the Maharashtra Medical Council (MMC) and prescribe allopathic medicines.

World.title: 'We are with students': Kharge's 1st reaction on Jharkhand student protests
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress president

on Thursday backed students protesting over alleged irregularities in Jharkhand's recruitment examinations, saying his party stands with students and youth "whether it is Jharkhand, Punjab, Delhi or anywhere else".

Additionally, he also demanded that the Union home minister come to Parliament and explain the alleged lathi-charge and use of pellet guns against protesting students in Delhi's Jantar Mantar.

"We want the Union Home Minister to come to the House and tell us who ordered the lathi-charge and the use of pellet guns on students," Kharge said while addressing a press conference in Delhi.

Speaking on the protests in Jharkhand, which have entered their 13th day, Kharge said the Congress stands with students and youth across the country.

"We stand with the students, whether it is Jharkhand, Punjab, Delhi or anywhere else. Rahul Gandhi ji and I stand with the students," he said.

Kharge said the party would seek answers on what happened during the protests and was also reaching out to those involved. He added that the Congress would continue to raise students' concerns, irrespective of whether they were protesting against an alliance partner or the Opposition.





"We will ask why this happened and whether any mistake was made on our part. We are also writing to each of them (allaince partners) to understand what happened. Whether it is our alliance partner or the Opposition, we stand with students and youth and will continue to fight to resolve their problems," Kharge said.

The statements came as the LoP accused the Centre of refusing to respond to repeated demands for a statement in Parliament on the issue.

"We have been asking for a statement from him on this. What is preventing him from making a statement? It could only be his arrogance. Either they are scared or don't regard the existence of Parliament. I want to tell them- they should come to the House and make a statement," Kharge said.

The remarks came as protests over alleged irregularities in Jharkhand's recruitment examinations reached the state Assembly on Thursday, the first day of the Monsoon Session.

Opposition MLAs raised slogans on the Assembly premises as the student agitation entered its 13th day, with six demonstrators continuing their hunger strike.

The protest began on July 25 under the banner of the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in Ranchi. The students are demanding the cancellation of the 14th Jharkhand PSC Civil Services Examination and an independent probe into alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations.

Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren on Wednesday said his government would "soon take action" over protests alleging recruitment exam irregularities after meeting governor Santosh Kumar Gangwar and discussing the situation. The protesters have demanded a CBI investigation or an inquiry by a panel of retired High Court judges from outside Jharkhand.

World.title: Soaked in rain, fired by anger: JPSC-JSSC aspirants & students' Tiranga march rocks Ranchi
World.content:
Holding the Tricolour aloft and carrying what organisers described as an approximately 600-metre-long national flag, the students marched through Ranchi.

As the march drew to a close, the rain intensified, but so did chants of "Jai Jharkhand".

RANCHI: Undeterred by relentless rain, hundreds of students gathered at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in Ranchi on Wednesday before setting out on a Tiranga March to Albert Ekka Chowk, intensifying an agitation that has entered its second week over alleged irregularities in Jharkhand's recruitment examinations.The march came amid an indefinite protest by students demanding a CBI investigation into the alleged paper leaks and recruitment irregularities in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) examinations.The movement has also escalated on the hunger strike front. Alongside Devendra Nath Mahto, dubbed by protesters as "Sonam Wangchuk 2.0", four more students have joined an indefinite fast, pressing three principal demands: cancellation of all JPSC and JSSC examinations conducted during the Hemant Soren-led JMM government's tenure; a CBI probe into the alleged irregularities, paper leaks and delays in recruitment results instead of an investigation by the state's Criminal Investigation Department (CID), which the students say they no longer trust; and comprehensive reforms to Jharkhand's recruitment and competitive examination system.The Tiranga March began with chants of "Jai Jharkhand" and slogans celebrating student unity. Organisers repeatedly instructed participants to refrain from using abusive language in slogans or on placards, stressing that the protest would remain peaceful and disciplined.The emphasis on restraint reflected the students' attempt to draw a clear distinction between their movement and political organisations.Protesters pointed out that two separate demonstrations have been taking place in Ranchi: one led by students and another believed to be backed by local MLA Jairam Singh Mahato's party. Organisers also appeared mindful of the aftermath of the recent Jantar Mantar protest in New Delhi, where FIRs and complaints were lodged against some protesters over the use of profanities. Students said they were determined to ensure that no such controversy overshadowed their movement.Holding the Tricolour aloft and carrying what organisers described as an approximately 600-metre-long national flag, the students marched through Ranchi despite the downpour."Our flag march represents the moral spirit of India. It highlights our constitutional rights. Look at all these students getting drenched in the rain while waving the Tricolour. This is a symbol of our unity and a symbol of our constitutional rights," one protester said.As the march reached Albert Ekka Chowk, groups of students gathered at the intersection and continued raising slogans. Traffic disruption remained limited, largely because authorities had already closed one of the approach roads. Protesters also allowed vehicles to pass intermittently, saying they did not want to cause unnecessary inconvenience to commuters.Appealing directly to the Hemant Soren government, another protester said, "We are the children of Jharkhand. You speak about working for the indigenous and tribal communities. Please work in our interest too. Thousands of students are studying with the hope of securing jobs in their own state. We request the government to reform the JPSC and JSSC."Several protesters contrasted the Ranchi agitation with the earlier demonstrations at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, insisting that their movement had remained peaceful throughout. They also warned that any police action, including a possible lathicharge, would only intensify the agitation."We are protesting peacefully. If the police take action against us, it will only raise questions about the government's role because we have not indulged in any violence. Every evening we gather at our protest site and peacefully put forward our demands," one participant said.As the march drew to a close, the rain intensified, but so did chants of "Jai Jharkhand". Some protesters invoked the state's historical icons while asserting that Jharkhand's identity extended beyond sporting achievements."Our identity is not defined by MS Dhoni. Our identity is defined by Birsa Munda, Tilka Manjhi, Shibu Soren, Binod Bihari Mahto, Bisheshwar Prasad Keshari, Sidhu and Kanhu," a protester said.Meanwhile, the Hemant Soren government has constituted a committee of ministers and senior officials to initiate talks with the agitating students. State minister Rajat said complaints regarding recruitment examination irregularities were already under investigation and that the agencies concerned were working on them with urgency.The students, however, rejected the proposal for closed-door discussions. They insisted that any dialogue with the government must be conducted transparently, in the presence of the media and television cameras, arguing that only an open process would inspire confidence among the protesters.

World.title: Assam floods crisis deepens: 1.6 lakh people affected across 14 districts, death toll rises to 95
World.content:
Six deaths reported: Two each in Sivasagar and Biswanath districts, and one each in Golaghat and Morigaon. (Photo: PTI)

NEW DELHI: The death toll from the devastating floods in Assam rose to 95 after six more people died, while more than 1.6 lakh people remained affected across 14 districts, officials said on Thursday.According to the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA), six deaths were reported on Wednesday, two each in Sivasagar and Biswanath districts, and one each in Golaghat and Morigaon.Sivasagar continues to be the worst-affected district, accounting for 50 of the 95 deaths reported so far.Neighbouring Charaideo has recorded 21 fatalities, followed by Jorhat (9), Golaghat (5), Dhemaji (3), Karbi Anglong (2) and Biswanath (2). One death each has also been reported from Sonitpur, Kamrup Metropolitan and Morigaon.The floods have affected over 1,60,600 people in Biswanath, Charaideo, Darrang, Dhemaji, Golaghat, Jorhat, Kamrup Metropolitan, Karbi Anglong, Lakhimpur, Nagaon, Sivasagar, Sonitpur, Tinsukia and Udalguri districts.Sivasagar alone has around 57,000 affected residents, followed by Golaghat (34,000) and Jorhat (25,000).The number of affected people has risen sharply from 1.22 lakh in five districts reported on Tuesday.Authorities have set up more than 100 relief camps and relief distribution centres across six districts, where 44,523 people are currently taking shelter.Floodwaters have submerged 16,951.76 hectares of cropland, while embankments, roads, bridges and other public infrastructure have suffered extensive damage in several parts of the state.Union health and family welfare minister J P Nadda, who was deputed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, visited the flood-hit Nepalikhuti area along the Assam-Nagaland border in Sivasagar district on Wednesday, one of the regions worst affected by the latest wave of floods that began on July 19.Later in the day, Nadda chaired a high-level review meeting with Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma and senior state officials to assess the flood situation and review ongoing relief, rehabilitation and healthcare measures."I have visited the flood-hit Nepalikhuti area. Along with CM Sarma, I have witnessed the scale of devastation. The damage is so huge that it will take time (for normalcy to return)," Nadda told reporters after interacting with flood-affected families."The Central Government and the State Government have stood with complete sensitivity and utmost promptness beside every flood-affected family. We are continuing the relief and rehabilitation efforts with full commitment. I assure everyone that there will be no lapses of any kind in the relief and rescue operations. Teams of Central Government representatives are conducting extensive assessments of the flood damages, and all kinds of financial assistance are being extended," he added.Nadda is scheduled to visit Yazali in Arunachal Pradesh on Thursday to inspect areas affected by flash floods and interact with affected residents. During the visit, Nadda will chair a review meeting with state government officials to assess the health situation and review ongoing relief and rehabilitation efforts in the region.The visit is part of his three-day tour of the Northeast from August 4 to 6.

World.title: 'Not fluent in Tamil is an insult': Actor Dhanush pushes for mother tongue first
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Actor Dhanush has renewed the focus on the language debate with his remarks stressing the importance of learning Tamil and being "fluent in one's mother tongue."

Speaking at an event, the actor strongly backed the Tamil language and urged people to prioritise fluency in their mother tongue.

Recalling his school days, Dhanush said, "When I was in school, we were fluent in Tamil and we struggled with English. Now the situation is opposite."

He added, "Now, out of the 10 people I meet, eight don't know Tamil. One should be fluent in their mother tongue before everything else. To say I'm not fluent in Tamil is not a matter of pride. It's an insult. Focus on learning Tamil language."

His remarks come amid the long-running language debate in Tamil Nadu, where the issue has frequently put the state government at odds with the Centre. Leaders across the state's political spectrum, from DMK chief and former CM MK Stalin to TVK founder and CM Vijay, have repeatedly accused the Centre of attempting to impose Hindi on southern states.

World.title: This new restaurant in Bengaluru is playing with neo vegetarian cuisine
World.content:
Modern Indian cuisine is a concept that is usually met with apprehension. We are fiercely protective about our food. The Silky Elephant in Bengaluru is challenging this. The restaurant in JP Nagar has a modern vegetarian menu. Here papdi chaat meets bruchetta, tempura meets thecha and the tomato shorba has kaffir lime. But do they work? We find out over lunch.

Styled with a modern look, the restaurant is brimming with guests even on a Monday afternoon. We take a seat by the window overlooking the street. The service is warm and helpful. We peruse the menu (QR code only unfortunately), and it is expansive, with Asian, Indian and global cuisines.

The hibiscus pani puri is colourful and eye-catching. The crispy puris are served with potato and a red hibiscus pani, which is floral and subtle. A fun spin on a crowd favourite. The charcoal dahi kebabs are a visual delight. Coated on the outside with activated charcoal, the kebabs are striking and taste balanced with tang and spice. From the Asian section, we enjoy the wild mushroom dim sum. The thin casing of these is tinged purple, and the mushroom stuffing is earthy and delicious. We pair these with a refreshing cranberry mocktail.

For the main course, we stick to Indian, but the restaurant offers pasta, pizza and Chinese as well. From the ‘progressive’ section, we order dum aloo panch phoran with mascarpone, nadru rezala and bhatt ki dal.

The dum aloo is stuffed with mascarpone cheese, and served with a Bengali panch phoran-spiced gravy. A good mix of spicy and creamy. The nadru is the winning dish on the table. The Kashmiri-style dish is made with large pieces of steamed lotus stem in a white, yoghurt-based gravy. The gravy had a delicate flavour with green cardamom, mace, and kewra water. The Himachali dal is spicier than we imagine, with red chillies and wild herbs. We pair these with a delicious leavened Khamiri Naan, where the fermented flavour of the dough shines. The cheese chilly naan is spilling with gooey melted cheese, and almost feels like a pizza.

It’s A Date!! is one of our desserts. Described as British sticky toffee pudding meets Medjool dates, this has a cake topped with butterscotch toffee sauce and fresh cream. However, the sponge cake is a little dry in this one. The signature pistachio forest dessert comes highly recommended. Pistachio cream is filled in a chocolate log, atop chocolate soil. The presentation is gourmet, and the flavours on this are light.

The Silky Elephant is a solid choice for family dining in the JP Nagar area. The shareable innovative starters impress us and there is something for everyone.

₹1,800 for two. At JP Nagar, 8th phase, Bengaluru. For reservations, call 91872 06152

World.title: U.S. requests Filipino pastor’s extradition on sex-trafficking charges: Philippine Ambassador
World.content:
The United States has formally requested the extradition of a Filipino pastor wanted on sex-trafficking charges, the Philippines’ ambassador to Washington said on Thursday (August 6, 2026).

Apollo Quiboloy, a self-proclaimed “Appointed Son of God” and ally of former president Rodrigo Duterte, was arrested in the Philippines in 2024 on human-trafficking charges.

He faces life in prison if found guilty in the case, which accuses him of using women and child sect members to sell goods and raise funds for his church.

Quiboloy, who pleaded not guilty shortly after his August 2024 arrest, has been held in a Manila jail ever since.

A U.S. grand jury had indicted Quiboloy three years earlier for conspiracy to engage in sex trafficking by force, fraud and coercion, sex trafficking of children, and bulk cash smuggling.

The 2021 U.S. indictment alleges girls and women between the ages of 12 and 25 were recruited as personal assistants for Quiboloy to prepare his meals, clean his residence, give him massages, and have sex with him.

On Thursday (August 6, 2026), Ambassador Jose Manuel Romualdez told AFP the United States had formally asked for the pastor to be handed over.

“The formal request has been transmitted to the Dept of Justice,” he said via text message, without providing further detail.

The U.S. Embassy and the Philippine Department of Justice did not reply immediately to requests for comment.

Quiboloy was allowed to run for Senate in the country’s 2025 midterm elections despite his incarceration and garnered 5,667,438 votes.

Police said following his arrest that Quiboloy’s alleged victims were told they were having sex with the “Spirit of God” and were threatened not to tell anyone on pain of being hunted down by “angels of death”.

Quiboloy’s Kingdom of Jesus Christ church said at the time that members had “freedom of choice” and thus “anything that happens to you... is your own voluntary will or choice”.

The powerful sect claims millions of followers in the mainly Catholic Asian nation and owns a television network.

Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos said in 2024 that the government was not yet looking to extradite Quiboloy because it was “focusing on the cases filed in the Philippines”.

World.title: Why Mechuka Trout Quest is drawing anglers to Arunachal Pradesh
World.content:
Neega Ngurang began fishing as a child, “local style” with a “bamboo pole rod, using a single monoline and one hook,” recalls the sports angler, river guide, and content creator from Sagalee, near Itanagar in Arunachal Pradesh.

In 2013, he discovered angling and was hooked — pun intended. “I did not know what sport fishing is, but when I saw a spinning rod on television, I realised that I also wanted to buy it and learn how to use it,” says Neega, who spent the next two years practising angling in the rivers in and around where he lived. “As I gained experience, I also picked up the catch-and-release technique used in sport fishing, and began attending competitions, starting from 2016 or 17,” he says.

Today, he runs training programmes on angling and also a popular fishing YouTube channel, Neega Fishing Adventures, through which he educates people about the sport, which he insists is addictive. “You have to experience it to understand. It is really fun.”

Angling in the hills

Neega was recently in Mechuka to attend the second edition of the Mechuka Trout Quest, the annual angling championship, held between July 25 and 26, which saw 56 elite competitors from within and outside the country, including Bobby Satpal, widely recognised as one of India’s top fly anglers, and Tup Meesupwatana, a popular professional angler and YouTuber from Thailand.

Organised by the State’s Department of Tourism, the Mechuka Trout Quest is envisioned as a flagship international angling event “designed to position Arunachal Pradesh as a leader in high-value, low-impact eco-tourism”, according to the pre-event press release. “The landscape is already endowed with Nature, and we have many places to visit,” says Pasang Dorjee Sona, the local MLA and the State’s Tourism Minister who also serves as the Minister of Education, Rural Works, Parliamentary Affairs and Libraries. “That is why this idea came up,” he says.

Fishing as a sport

Fishing is deeply tied to human history, going back at least a couple of million years: early humans likely caught animals with bare hands and later, crude spears. Evidence of line fishing for food emerged atleast around 23,000 years ago, as shown by mollusc hooks recovered from the Jerimalai Cave in East Timor, though the first mention of sport fishing would come much later, in the 15th-century book A Treatyse of Fysshynge wyth an Angle, written by Juliana Berners.

“I think it is human nature, which is why so many people take up the sport,” says tournament director Derek Dsouza, the India representative of the International Game Fishing Association (IGFA), who became involved in the initiative a couple of years ago, when Dr Gebu Sona, a doctor from Tato and an avid angler himself, got in touch with him.

Though traditional line and net sustenance fishing is and has been prevalent in India for millennia, angling as a recreational sport is a relatively modern phenomenon here. First practised by homesick British officials, it is now an emerging sport in the country, with interest in it growing, says Derek, who believes that “we have a huge potential in India because we have a large coastline and a lot of big rivers”.

In recent years, Arunachal Pradesh, particularly Mechuka, has been on the map of the angling community, with anglers being especially drawn to the trout found here. Among the popular game trout are the brown and rainbow trout, both of which were introduced by the British to India in the 19th and 20th Centuries. “Mechuka is one of the few places in Arunachal Pradesh where we have trout. The climatic conditions are conducive because it is a cold-water fish,” explains Fisheries Minister Gabriel Denwang, adding that the State plans to invest heavily in trout farming. “It would help us boost tourism in this area. That is what we are targeting for.”

Trout tourism

The pine-studded, emerald slopes of the Eastern Himalayas loom as Sonam Tshering reels in a brown trout, the early morning sun gleaming off its tawny, speckled body. He then scoops the fish into a soft net and gently unhooks it before crouching in the pellucid waters of the Yargyap Chu River, live fish in damp hands, to pose for a photograph taken by a waiting marshal. A sudden splash as the fish is released and quickly skitters away, while Sonam straps the net to his back and wades back deeper with his rod, all ready for his next catch.

But it is not the actual catch that draws Sonam to the sport. “I just like the experience,” says the Bhutanese angler, who participated in and won the fly fishing category at the Mechuka Trout Quest this year. “I enjoy being in Nature, wading through the water, learning about the river structures and trout behaviour.”

Nasreen Sultana Naaz, the sole female angler among the participants, echoes Sonam’s view. “The best part about angling is that I get to travel and see all these beautiful destinations. We all live chaotic, urban lives, but once you come to an angling spot, it is completely different,” says the Gauhati-based indie rock musician, who was drawn to angling when she began accompanying her husband, also an angler, on various fishing trips. “I am now hooked on the game,” says Nasreen.

Mechuka calling How to get there: The nearest airport is Dibrugarh, and from there it is a 370 km journey by road. There is also a chopper service twice a week, on Monday and Friday, from Itanagar. What to visit: Yargyap Chu river banks, Dorjeeling Village, Buddha Park, Samten Choeling Monastery, Gonpa Samten Yangchag Heritage Museum, Guru Nanak Taposthan, Lamang Border Where to stay: There are a number of good, affordable homestays in Mechuka, such as the Hornbill, Owa, Mae and Yargyap-Chu Cottage Homestay, among others.

Like Sonam and Nasreen, most anglers love coming to off-beat places like Mechuka to fish, says Derek, who believes that angling can indeed play a significant role in boosting sustainable ecotourism. “Anglers don’t need to have expensive accommodation, just a pristine river. And if they have that, it could lead to a significant economic boom in a place,” he says, pointing out that anglers are largely fairly responsible tourists, who ensure that they keep their surroundings clean, respect Nature and are willing to pay well for an angling experience. “That is the tourism required here,” he says.

Minister Dorjee Sona, too, is aware that tourism models need to be developed very carefully in a State like Arunachal Pradesh, which, like most of its northeastern counterparts, is ecologically fragile and vulnerable to large-scale development. “We want to have niche tourism only. I’ve been very vocal about saying that, and the best part is our people are also aware of this,” he says. Instead, they are targeting a very specific sort of tourist: “the adventure seekers,” he says. According to him, the Government is also now focused on creating better infrastructure for adventure sports like kayaking, mountain biking, mountaineering and, of course, angling. “We got a lot of attention for angling, so we are taking it forward,” he says.

Based on the success of the first two editions of the trout quest, it now looks likely to be a permanent fixture on the angling map. “Everyone absolutely loved it, including people from other parts of Arunachal who had never come to this part of the state,” says Derek, who noticed that many of the participants had also attended the first edition. “Everyone wants to come back, including the people from Bhutan and Jammu and Kashmir for whom getting here is a challenge,” he says. ‘I think if we continue the same path we are going and get more people’s support, this could be one of the best trout destinations in the world. “

The writer was at Mechuka on the invitation of the Arunachal Pradesh’s department of tourism

World.title: West Asia LIVE: Pakistan hopes Hormuz agreement will lead to resumption of Iran-U.S. talks
World.content:
Pakistan hopes an agreement over the Strait of Hormuz will lead to the United States and Iran resuming talks under a memorandum of understanding Islamabad helped mediate, Foreign Ministry spokesman Tahir Andrabi said on Thursday (August 6, 2026).

Also read | What’s at stake in the latest U.S.-Iran talks?

Israel reported on Thursday (August 6, 2026) its first military fatalities in southern Lebanon in more than a month, after carrying out fresh strikes despite ongoing U.S.-backed talks in Rome aimed at ending hostilities.
